dossier.title: Taught, Not Selected: Reflective Harness Evolution Absorbs a Simulator's Errors Through Its Traces, Not Its Scores (formerly "Evolving in a Dream")
dossier.claim: When reflective harness evolution (GEPA-style) is scored inside a simulator with steerable, decision-relevant errors, most of the real-environment loss is *taught* (it enters through the traces the reflector reads) rather than *selected* (through the simulated score). At matched base outcome-error δ₀, giving the reflector real traces while keeping simulated fitness recovers most of the loss; giving it real fitness while it keeps reading simulated traces does not. So the pre-registered contrast G_SR − G_RS > 0. An identical error that leaves a textual marker is exploited faster than the same error made silent. The opposite sign is a pre-registered, first-class alternative ("selected, not taught"): G_RS ≥ G_SR and legibility does not matter.
dossier.design:
Domain: a procedural, deterministic τ²-retail-style Python DB environment in single-instruction mode, so the real environment has no LLM user. It uses 150 evolution tasks, 50 validation tasks and 300 held-out tasks. The task agent is Qwen3.5-9B, the evolver is GEPA with a Haiku-class reflector, and evolution runs to depth 40. The "simulator" is a labelled quirk layer over the real environment, with Q1 lenient validation and Q2 missing error state, each in a legible variant and a silent variant. All quirks are matched on δ₀ ≈ 0.15. The core instrument is a 2×2 of fitness source × reflector-trace source (SS/SR/RS/RR) with 8 seeds per cell. The legibility contrast is SS-silent vs SS-legible. Controls at matched δ₀:
- NOISE (symmetric label flips) and UNSTEER (random one-sided false passes), for the optimizer's curse;
- a Q5 lenient-judge positive control;
- a δ₀≈0.30 dose arm.

Mitigations:
- REDACT: the reflector sees actions plus binary outcomes only.
- ANCHOR10: a cost-matched selector that scores 10% of candidates in the real environment.

Exploratory checks: one natural prompted Qwen3.5-27B simulator ("self-dreaming") and an E2 code-level evolver replication. That is 88 runs in total, about $300 API plus ~250 GPU-h, OSF pre-registration by Dec 20 2026, and a mixed model on task-level paired outcomes at pooled d ∈ {20,30,40}. A ≤$60 one-week pilot gates the study on G_RR(20) ≥ 8 pp with seed SD ≤ 4 pp, L(20) ≥ 8 pp, and Q5 showing exploitation.
dossier.priorScores: R1 critique 71.3 → R1 proposal self-score 74.6 → R2 novelty-killer 63.8 / R2 sharpness-reviewer 67.9 (projected ~78–80 if steerability pivot taken) → v2 self-rescore 76.3 (rank #3 in round-2 REPORT, Go-with-changes; downside fallback ≈62–65)

closestPapers.title: Does Failure Feedback Direct Agent Self-Modification?
closestPapers.summary: Measures 'directedness': whether a self-modification repairs the randomly chosen target failure better than the parent's other failures. Across 145 Darwin Gödel Machine edits, it finds no target-specific advantage. In controlled instruction-revision experiments with a pre-specified analysis plan, target feedback raised repair by 20 pp for Qwen3-4B, while the +7 for Phi-4-mini was not significant. Target repair did not reliably imply held-out improvement, and GEPA and 8-step revision loops ended at similar held-out accuracy.
closestPapers.relation: The closest conceptual neighbour, and the source of v2's split prior. It asks whether *correct* feedback steers edits. v2 asks whether *erroneous* simulator feedback steers edits toward exploitation, across depth and against real ground truth. Its null on DGM supports 'selected', and its +20 pp controlled result supports 'taught'. It leaves the erroneous-evaluator, multi-iteration, trace-vs-score case open. A follow-up by this author is a plausible fast-follower.

closestPapers.title: What Should the Reflector See? An Empirical Study of Evidence in Reflective Prompt Optimization
closestPapers.summary: Uses Qwen3.5-9B as both task model and reflector in a single-parent Pareto-guided search. It compares nine reflection-evidence strategies on five datasets. Failures-only gives the largest mean test gain (+8.0 pp). No-examples improves sampled parents most locally but gives only +1.4 pp at test. Calibration gains can overstate held-out improvement.
closestPapers.relation: The same model scale and the same evidence knob that v2 manipulates; v2's REDACT arm borrows its no-examples and outcome-only controls. But it uses only correct evaluators on single-turn QA, with no simulator and no exploitation. v2 crosses the reflector's evidence source with an erroneous fitness source. The round-2 proposal names this 'reflector evidence' line as the likeliest fast-follower (~20–25% before May).

closestPapers.title: Lineage Is Memory: Parent Inheritance and Feedback Disclosure in Short-Budget LLM-Guided Optimization
closestPapers.summary: Across 1,750 pre-registered runs on nine prompt- and program-synthesis benchmarks, it separates parent inheritance from feedback disclosure under matched evaluation budgets. Greedy parent inheritance drives most optimization progress and beats seed-reset resampling, even when the seed-reset proposer is given clustered summaries of all failures or is a larger model. Proposer reflection is a small fraction of GEPA's token cost.
closestPapers.relation: It shows that feedback disclosure matters less than lineage *for gains* under correct evaluators. v2 asks whether disclosure matters *for exploitation* under an erroneous simulator. Its result is a prior for the 'selected' branch, since the inheritance/selection pathway dominates. v2 uses its pre-registration style as a template.

closestPapers.title: Optimizing the Score, Losing Sight of the Task: Reward Hacking Across Weights, Selection, and Prompts
closestPapers.summary: A comparative theoretical framework for reward hacking across three optimization substrates: weights, selection among outputs, and persistent prompt revision. It formalizes a distance-dependent bound on evaluator disagreement and a capacity ordering of nested policy classes. It shows that distance alone cannot rank vulnerability, and gives an exact finite-output illustration. It also maps which defenses transfer across substrates.
closestPapers.relation: Theory only, with no LLM experiments. According to the v2 proposal's read, it argues that prompt optimizers need not 'understand' a defect because selection suffices, which is the 'selected' hypothesis. v2 would be the first experiment that separates trace-driven 'understanding' from selection for prompt/harness substrates.

closestPapers.title: Not All Errors Matter: Decision-Relevant Prediction Error Predicts Planning Quality (DRPE)
closestPapers.summary: Introduces Decision-Relevant Prediction Error and an iso-error protocol that holds total error fixed while moving error between decision-relevant and irrelevant state dimensions. Across 55 models in a factored gridworld with a fixed planner, total error barely predicts success (ρ=−0.25) while DRPE does (ρ=−0.84). Models within 1% total error can differ by 60 pp in success. Deeper imagination amplifies relevant error.
closestPapers.relation: It killed v1's 'error type, not rate' / iso-accuracy headline. That is why v2 pivoted, and v2 makes all quirks decision-relevant and δ₀-matched rather than claiming type effects. It has no iterative optimizer and no LLM reader, so it is no threat to v2's trace-vs-selection channel question.

closestPapers.title: Learning in Dreams, Winning in Reality: A Continuous Dyna Loop for a Ten-Hero MOBA
closestPapers.summary: Trains a PPO policy only inside a learned multi-agent MOBA world model, with real games used only for world-model data and anchoring. It reaches 70.2% real wins as radiant. Model exploitation is invisible from inside the dream: unanchored runs collapse with no in-dream metric tracking it. Dyna repair on the policy's own games is worth +9.2 pp. The policy 'inherits its world model's fidelity profile mechanic by mechanic'.
closestPapers.relation: Weight RL, correlational evidence, with the causal per-mechanic intervention left as future work. It motivates causal quirk injection, and it is a naming threat ('dreams') that forced the rename. Fresh-scoop flags its author running the intervention as a residual risk. That would be RL, though, and could not produce a trace-vs-score split.

closestPapers.title: One Frozen Simulator Is Not Enough: Simulator Collapse in Multi-Agent RL
closestPapers.summary: Shows that RL of an LLM policy against a single mode-collapsed LLM user simulator overfits to strategies that exploit the simulator's dominant mode and transfers poorly to unseen simulators and real users. It proposes Verbalized Sampling at inference and population Co-Training at training time, with up to +9% and +14% held-out success on Persuasion for Good, τ²-bench and CooperBench, plus a human study.
closestPapers.relation: The canonical weight-level 'Goodhart-in-simulator' curve. v2's null branch ('harness search exploits lies about success, not about consequences') is framed as the contrast to it. Weights, user simulator, no channel decomposition. The fact-check caveats that the fall below base holds only for the most modal simulator (Gemini-3-Flash) and the human study.

closestPapers.title: World Models Need Not Be Right to Rank Policies Right: Relative Bounds and Audit Limits
closestPapers.summary: Derives a pairwise simulation identity separating common-mode from policy-specific world-model error, and proposes RAVEL, a policy tournament audited on real outcomes. On 45 SAC/TD3/PPO policies in DMC cheetah-run and walker-walk, model rankings stay strong (τ=0.962/0.800). But audit-error correlations are near zero, and frozen-model optimization lowers real return. Ranking fidelity, audit covariance and exploitation are distinct properties.
closestPapers.relation: It pre-empted v1's ranking-fidelity metric (τ_path), which v2 dropped. Its optimizer's-curse remark motivates v2's NOISE/UNSTEER controls. Continuous control with fixed policy pools and no LLM reader, so it is not a threat to v2's channel question.

closestPapers.title: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning
closestPapers.summary: Introduces GEPA (Genetic-Pareto), a prompt optimizer that samples system trajectories (reasoning, tool calls, tool outputs), reflects on them in natural language to propose prompt updates, and keeps a Pareto frontier of candidates. It argues that language reflection is a richer learning signal than sparse scalar rewards, and reports gains over GRPO with far fewer rollouts.
closestPapers.relation: Foundation. It is the primary evolver E1, and its two separable pipes (traces into the reflector, scores into Pareto/gate selection) are exactly what v2's 2×2 routes independently. v2 tests whether GEPA's rationale ('reading traces is richer than scalar reward') becomes an attack surface when the traces come from a simulator.

feedback.point: The metric claim ('prediction accuracy is the wrong fidelity metric') is known from Lambert 2020 objective mismatch, 2610.19375 and 2609.33335; it applies to prompts only.
feedback.addressed: Yes. v2 explicitly drops it and makes no fidelity-metric claim.

feedback.point: Fidelity is not manipulated causally, and comparing 2–3 natural simulators confounds fidelity with style and determinism. Use BreakingWeb-style labelled quirk injection with dose–response.
feedback.addressed: Yes. The quirk layer over the real environment, with logged firings and a δ₀≈0.30 dose arm, is the core instrument.

feedback.point: Live 'real sites' are a reproducibility hazard, and the transfer-fraction ratio is noisy; use self-hosted environments with ≥150 tasks per site and deterministic verifiers, and report gaps with CIs.
feedback.addressed: Yes. Procedural deterministic τ-retail with 300 held-out tasks, and gains reported as paired differences in a mixed model rather than as ratios.

feedback.point: The confound battery is missing: add real-env evolution at matched evaluation count and at matched dollar cost, plus held-out-task evaluation, to separate simulator Goodhart from task-set Goodhart.
feedback.addressed: Mostly. RR (=REAL-count) arm and a 300-task held-out set; ANCHOR10 is cost-matched to SR. There is no explicit matched-dollar-cost real-evolution arm.

feedback.point: Too few sites and too little evolver diversity; add a non-web domain and a second (code-level) evolver.
feedback.addressed: Partially. Uses a non-web domain (τ-retail) plus the E2 code-level evolver (6 runs), but web was dropped, so it is one domain and one agent model, accepted as a scope limit.

feedback.point: No constructive output. Propose harness-ranking fidelity (Kendall τ) as the predictive metric, and test mitigations (ensembles, disagreement early stopping, sparse real anchors).
feedback.addressed: Reframed. τ_path was dropped in v2 as circular. The constructive outputs are now REDACT (zero-cost trace hygiene) and ANCHOR10. Ensembles and disagreement early stopping were cut.

feedback.point: Frame directly against 2608.12253 (weights + user simulator) and AdvSim2Real/DarwinX (positive transfer) as foils.
feedback.addressed: Partially. 2608.12253 is the explicit foil for the null branch. AdvSim2Real and DarwinX appeared in v1's table but are absent from v2's closest-papers table.

feedback.point: Feasibility: GPU serving of trained world models plus simulator engineering is heavy for a solo undergrad.
feedback.addressed: Partially. Trained world models were replaced by a quirk layer plus one prompted Qwen3.5-27B simulator (~40 H100-h). The total is still ~250 GPU-h and 88 runs.

feedback.point: DRPE 2609.32322 (iso-error protocol, 60 pp gap) pre-empts the 'type not rate' / iso-accuracy headline; cite it and demote the claim to a control.
feedback.addressed: Yes. The claim was dropped entirely. All conditions are decision-relevant and δ₀-matched, and DRPE is row #1 of the related-work table.

feedback.point: Add the √KL / edit-distance-from-seed baseline (2611.09670) and the selection-regret baseline (2611.01139); τ_path must beat them or RQ3 should be dropped.
feedback.addressed: Yes, by dropping τ_path. Edit distance from the seed is kept as a √KL-proxy covariate: does trace source predict loss beyond how far the harness moved?

feedback.point: Cite WRM 2610.38439 and SIRIS 2611.10329, and reframe RQ4 against WRM-style direct selectors rather than only WMRL anchors.
feedback.addressed: Yes. Both are cited, and ANCHOR10 is described as a WMRL/WRM-style selection-side comparator.

feedback.point: Rename the paper, since Dream-RSI 2609.14858 and 2610.08033 own 'dream'.
feedback.addressed: Yes. Renamed to 'Taught, Not Selected'.

feedback.point: Make the headline harness-specific: quirk legibility (legible vs silent traces) and reflector-vs-selector attribution via a 2×2 trace-source × fitness-source swap; trace redaction as a zero-cost defense.
feedback.addressed: Yes. This is exactly the v2 pivot: the 2×2 (H1), legible vs silent (H2), and REDACT (H4).

feedback.point: Make the 'harness search does not Goodhart' outcome a pre-registered first-class hypothesis.
feedback.addressed: Yes. 'Selected, not taught' is a first-class alternative, and the null branch is made interpretable by the Q5 positive control.

feedback.point: Post an early preprint of the core by Feb 2027, because a loose 'simulator-scored GEPA transfers' method paper is ~50–60% likely before May.
feedback.addressed: Partially. The preprint is planned for ~Mar 5 2027, slightly later than the recommended February.

feedback.point: Re-check OpenReview ICLR 2027 submissions once reachable; this is the biggest open risk.
feedback.addressed: No. Still unchecked (host blocked); listed as a re-check item for April.

feedback.point: Lower-scoop angles: harness vs RL/LoRA against the same simulator ('harnesses are safer to dream with'), and self-written simulators.
feedback.addressed: Not adopted.

feedback.point: The headline is a conjunction of 4 claims, and three pre-announced 'publishable' outcomes is hedging; commit to one directional claim.
feedback.addressed: Largely. One primary contrast (G_SR − G_RS > 0) is directional. v2 still lists three branches but argues each is a single sign test with a distinct recommendation.

feedback.point: 'Type, not rate' is near-tautological as operationalised, since cosmetic errors are decision-irrelevant by definition.
feedback.addressed: Yes. Cosmetic quirks were dropped.

feedback.point: Q5 lenient judge is reward hacking, not world-model error; keep it only as a labelled positive control.
feedback.addressed: Yes. Q5 is a positive control and a pilot gate.

feedback.point: Optimizer's curse: a noisy but unbiased simulator produces a 'peak' too, so add a NOISE condition at the matched outcome-error rate.
feedback.addressed: Yes. NOISE (symmetric flips) and UNSTEER (random one-sided false passes) are δ₀-matched controls (H3).

feedback.point: Wrong matching variable: match on base-policy outcome disagreement δ₀ = P(sim success ≠ real success | h₀), not on next-observation accuracy.
feedback.addressed: Yes. δ₀ ≈ 0.15 ± 0.02 for every condition, verified on 200 base rollouts and matched per legible/silent variant.

feedback.point: τ_path is circular (it needs real evaluations, which equals the anchor arm) and is confounded by the dose across conditions.
feedback.addressed: Yes. τ_path was dropped.

feedback.point: The oracle+quirk instrument does not model stochastic, belief-correlated LLM-simulator error, and a 3-point natural-simulator bridge validates nothing; cut it or make it one honest secondary analysis.
feedback.addressed: Yes. One natural Qwen3.5-27B simulator (9 runs), labelled exploratory.

feedback.point: Multiplicity: d_onset uses uncorrected tests and d_peak is a biased argmax; pre-register a single contrast or a parametric curve.
feedback.addressed: Yes. No argmax over d_peak, pooled d ∈ {20,30,40} in a mixed model, and Holm correction for H2.

feedback.point: Headroom risk (Rethinking Harness Eval / RRSI show ≈0 held-out gain). Gate the pilot on real gain under the oracle ≥ 8 pp with seed SD ≤ 4 pp, not on sim gain.
feedback.addressed: Yes. The pilot gate is G_RR(20) ≥ 8 pp with σ_seed ≤ 4 pp, plus a kill/pivot table and a corrupted-judge fallback.

feedback.point: Sprawl: ~140 runs, a web build, 4 mitigations and a 6-metric shoot-out is too much; make the D1-only fallback the plan (~60 runs).
feedback.addressed: Mostly. Cut to one domain, 88 runs and two mitigations; still larger than the reviewer's ~60-run design.

feedback.point: Rebuild the headline around error *steerability* (steerable vs unsteerable at iso-rate/type/δ₀, plus a noise control); add side claims of self-dreaming bias (same-family simulator) and steering budget (prompt vs code edits).
feedback.addressed: Partially. Steerability became a design constraint (all quirks steerable) and UNSTEER a control, not the headline. The natural simulator is same-family ('self-dreaming') but has no cross-family contrast. E2 covers steering budget only as an exploratory check.

feedback.point: 2610.08033 raises the bar: reviewers will expect a causal, per-quirk fidelity intervention, not a correlation. Residual risk is that its author or Meta's MIMESIS group runs it in a language setting.
feedback.addressed: Yes for the causal requirement (the quirk layer). The scoop risk remains but is mitigated by the channel framing.

feedback.point: Dream-RSI 2609.14858 owns 'dreaming over history for RSI'; cite it, and consider adding a nonparametric replay simulator class ('support-Goodhart' vs model-error).
feedback.addressed: Partially. Cited as a naming threat and the paper renamed; the replay simulator class was not added.

feedback.point: Add RHO 2606.05922 (self-judged on real re-rollouts) as a 'label-free' baseline arm vs simulator-scored evolution.
feedback.addressed: No. Not included in v2.

feedback.point: 2608.12253's held-out reward falls below base only for the most modal simulator (Gemini-3-Flash) and in the human study; the decline is gentler with GPT-5-mini.
feedback.addressed: No. The v2 table still states 'peaks, then falls below base' without the caveat.

feedback.point: There is a 55% chance that a causal simulator-fidelity study appears in weight RL, but only 30% for harness evolution, so the idea keeps a window if it stays harness-level and causal. It is ranked #3 (76.3, Go-with-changes) and is the fallback if the lead idea's pilot fails.
feedback.addressed: Yes. v2 is harness-specific and causal, and shares infrastructure (the procedural τ-world) with the lead idea.

openRisks: OpenReview-only ICLR 2027 submissions were never checked (the host was blocked in every pass); this is the biggest unknown scoop risk.

Fast followers. A 'reflector evidence' paper (2609.32452, 2610.14662 or 2610.41157 authors) crossing in erroneous evaluators is estimated at ~20–25% before May. A loose 'simulator-scored GEPA transfers' method paper is ~50–60% likely and would take the motivation, though not the channel decomposition.

Headroom. Real-environment harness evolution often shows ≈0 held-out gain (Rethinking Harness Eval 2607.12227, RRSI). If G_RR(20) < 8 pp or L < 8 pp, the paper falls back to a corrupted-judge pivot scoring ≈62–65.
The power analysis detects a teach/select split only at ≥70/30 when L ≥ 15 pp. Smaller splits may give an inconclusive TOST 'both channels' result.

Information confound in T=R cells: real traces also carry genuine error messages. Only the legible-vs-silent contrast isolates exploit revelation, so the 2×2 alone cannot separate 'concealment' from 'revelation'.
Legible markers may change base agent behaviour at d=0 (more than 0.1 triggers a redesign that moves legibility to the evaluator-feedback text only).

The priors are genuinely split. 2610.14662 (DGM edits not directed) and 2610.41157 (lineage dominates feedback) both favour 'selected'. This keeps the outcome surprising, but the headline 'taught' direction may well fail.

Scope: one domain, one agent model (Qwen3.5-9B) and a Haiku-class reflector, so reviewers may still call it a 'measurement paper'. Injected quirks may not reflect natural LLM-simulator errors; only 9 exploratory natural-simulator runs address that.
Feasibility: 88 runs, a procedural task generator, ~250 GPU-h and OSF pre-registration by Dec 20, all for one undergrad by mid-May 2027.
The v2 score (76.3) is a self-rescore that was not re-red-teamed. Some cited sources are unverified: Melcer et al. (possibly 2512.13598), 2606.15032 and 2604.13824.

judges.strongest: I found no ICLR 2027 OpenReview submission (Nov 12 sweep) and no 2026 arXiv paper that scores reflective harness evolution in a simulator and splits the transfer loss into a trace (reflector) channel and a fitness (selection) channel. The 2x2 route-swap is clean and specific to GEPA. The nearest work all tells selection-channel stories, which makes it ready-made foils: Improvement Fidelity Ah9eaA746Q, SEA 4HmKWgvoR5, Simulator Says Yes 0cb6zfwHm7, and 2609.25848 on the theory side. The priors are genuinely split (2610.14662 and 2610.41157 against PairEvolve FU8IgfEoHI), so a sign test is informative whichever way it comes out. The procedural deterministic environment with delta0-matched quirks, the NOISE/UNSTEER controls and the Q5 positive control is a strong design for its scale.
judges.weakest: The primary contrast G_SR - G_RS is confounded with GEPA's own premise. Real traces carry the genuine failure information that drives *improvement*, not only the absence of exploitation lessons, so G_SR > G_RS is close to expected whether or not simulated traces "teach" exploitation. The proposal admits this information confound, and only the legibility contrast addresses it, at one domain, one agent model and 8 seeds. Prior art also erodes the mitigation story. VHE in "The Harness Learns to Lie While Evolving" (ICLR27 5lWjRTK6Vk) already cuts what the reflector reads to stop false success during harness evolution, so REDACT is a causal test of an existing fix, not a new one. "Simulator Says Yes" (0cb6zfwHm7) and SEA already show natural silent-error exploitation and omission effects in weight RL. Power only resolves splits of 70/30 or more with L >= 15 pp, and real-environment harness evolution often shows almost no held-out headroom (Rethinking Harness Eval QDdWiaNkk2, RRSI).
judges.mustFix: 1. Replace or augment the gain-based contrast with a direct exploitation readout, so that "taught exploitation" is separated from "real traces teach real fixes". Candidates: the per-quirk exploit rate of the evolved harness (logged quirk firings and quirk-dependent actions on real held-out tasks), and loss measured relative to the RR arm at matched edit distance. Pre-register that a positive G_SR - G_RS without a raised exploit rate in the SS/RS cells does not count as "taught". 2. Cite and differentiate VHE (5lWjRTK6Vk) and position REDACT as a causal test of VHE-style trace hygiene, not as a new defense. Add VHE as a named mitigation arm. 3. Use the natural whitewashed-refusal error from Simulator Says Yes (0cb6zfwHm7), with its released refusal sets, as the silent arm. Cite Improvement Fidelity (Ah9eaA746Q), SEA (4HmKWgvoR5) and PairEvolve (FU8IgfEoHI) as selection-side and fitness-weak foils. 4. Control evaluator-state leakage between sim and real (GX4ucmiKZa). 5. Add a second agent model or reflector (for example a different-family reflector), even at 4 seeds, to blunt the "single-model measurement paper" objection. Fund it by cutting the E2 and self-dreaming exploratory runs if needed. 6. Hold the pilot headroom gate strictly, given that QDdWiaNkk2 reports near-zero real gains for harness evolution.
judges.reviewerQuote: The 2x2 is elegant, but real traces obviously carry more useful information than simulated ones; without a direct per-quirk exploitation measure, G_SR > G_RS restates GEPA's own premise rather than showing that simulator errors are 'taught', and REDACT is a re-test of VHE's trace hygiene on a single 9B agent in a single synthetic domain.

judges.strongest: The fitness-source × trace-source 2×2 is a clean, harness-specific causal decomposition that no 2026 arXiv paper or ICLR 2027 submission runs. The Nov 12 sweep confirms it is open: Improvement Fidelity (Ah9eaA746Q), SEA (4HmKWgvoR5) and Simulator Says Yes (0cb6zfwHm7) all give selection-channel accounts, so they serve as ready-made foils. The δ₀ matching, the NOISE/UNSTEER controls and the Q5 positive control make either sign of G_SR−G_RS interpretable.
judges.weakest:
1. Partial pre-emption. ICLR 2027 'The Harness Learns to Lie While Evolving' (5lWjRTK6Vk, VHE) already shows false success rising across harness-evolution rounds, and its fix cuts what the reflector reads. That takes REDACT/trace hygiene as a novel mitigation and half of the 'taught' intuition.
2. Confounds. The T=R cells carry genuine real-environment error information, not just the absence of simulator lies. 'Real traces recover the loss' is therefore partly 'real traces carry better information'. Only the legibility contrast isolates exploitation.
3. Thin scope. The 'simulator' is a hand-injected quirk layer rather than a learned simulator. There is one domain and one 9B agent model.
4. Feasibility. Headroom risk (G_RR ≈ 0 is common) plus 88 runs and ~250 GPU-h is heavy for a solo undergrad.
judges.mustFix:
1. Cite and differentiate against 5lWjRTK6Vk (VHE). Run VHE-style mechanical trace construction as a named baseline next to REDACT, and present trace hygiene as causally attributed, not new.
2. Use Simulator Says Yes (0cb6zfwHm7) whitewashed refusals as the natural silent-error arm, so injected quirks are anchored to a measured real simulator error.
3. Separate 'concealment' from 'revelation' in the T=R cells. Add an RS-variant where real traces are stripped of genuine error text, or a 'sim-trace + real-error-message-only' cell.
4. Add Improvement Fidelity (Ah9eaA746Q), PairEvolve (FU8IgfEoHI) and GX4ucmiKZa as foils and controls; refresh evaluator state between the simulator and the real environment.
5. Run the ≤$60 pilot now, gated on G_RR ≥ 8 pp. Post the preprint by Feb 2027, since 2609.32452 and 2610.14662 authors are natural fast-followers.
6. Add a second agent model (even a 4B) to blunt 'single-model measurement paper'.
judges.reviewerQuote: The 2×2 trace-versus-fitness decomposition is neat, but with one synthetic quirk layer, one domain and one 9B agent, and with real traces confounded by genuinely informative error messages, I am not convinced 'taught, not selected' is anything more than 'better feedback helps', which VHE already exploits.

judges.strongest: The ICLR 2027 sweep (Nov 12) confirms the core question is still open. No submission scores GEPA or harness evolution in a simulator and transfers it to a real environment, and none splits simulator error into a trace (reflector) channel and a fitness (selection) channel. The 2x2 routes GEPA's two separable pipes independently, so it is a clean causal design, and both signs are publishable. The foils have just appeared: Improvement Fidelity (Ah9eaA746Q), SEA (4HmKWgvoR5) and Simulator Says Yes (0cb6zfwHm7) all tell a selection story, against reflector-evidence work (2609.32452, 2610.14662) that is split. This sits squarely on the mentor's agenda (meta-agents, world models, self-improvement), and the shared tau-world infrastructure makes it cheap (~$300 API).
judges.weakest:
Novelty is boxed in on several sides, and the headline may simply fail.
- VHE in 'The Harness Learns to Lie While Evolving' (5lWjRTK6Vk, ICLR 2027) already cuts what the reflector reads to stop false success, so REDACT/trace hygiene is not new.
- 'Feedback Alignment in Self-Improving Agents' (C6EElQ2PRG) and GX4ucmiKZa already show that GEPA/scaffold evolution Goodharts evaluator-specific features, so the motivation is taken.
- The priors lean toward 'selected': 2610.14662, 2610.41157 and PairEvolve FU8IgfEoHI. The power analysis only resolves splits of 70/30 or more when L is at least 15 pp, so the likeliest outcome is a TOST 'both channels' muddle.
- The T=R cells mix exploit revelation with genuine error information.
- It is a single-domain, single-agent-model measurement paper at 88 runs plus ~250 GPU-h, which is tight for a solo undergrad, and the headroom gate (G_RR >= 8 pp) could fail outright given Rethinking Harness Eval QDdWiaNkk2.
judges.mustFix:
1. Cite 5lWjRTK6Vk (VHE) and frame REDACT as a causal test of trace hygiene, not a new defense. Add VHE-style mechanical experience construction as an arm or baseline.
2. Cite C6EElQ2PRG and GX4ucmiKZa, and refresh evaluator state between sim and real cells to remove the GX4ucmiKZa confound.
3. Set up Improvement Fidelity (Ah9eaA746Q), SEA (4HmKWgvoR5) and Simulator Says Yes (0cb6zfwHm7) as the explicit 'selected' foils. Replace or calibrate one silent quirk with 0cb6zfwHm7's whitewashed-refusal error so the silent arm is naturalistic.
4. Cite PairEvolve (FU8IgfEoHI) as the prior for the weak-fitness-signal branch.
5. Run the $60 pilot first and kill fast if G_RR(20) < 8 pp.
6. Cut the E2 code-evolver and the dose arm if the timeline slips. The core is the 2x2 plus legibility plus NOISE/Q5.
7. Post the preprint by February, not March, since reflector-evidence fast-followers are about 20-25% likely.
judges.reviewerQuote: The 2x2 decomposition of trace versus fitness channels is a clean idea, but with one synthetic quirk layer on one retail environment and one 9B agent, and VHE already showing that limiting what the reflector reads curbs false success, I am not convinced the 'taught' finding generalizes beyond the authors' own injected markers.

aka: Meta-Overfitting (round-2 recommended); merges round-1 procedure-vs-memory + meta-plasticity + swap-factorial

dossier.title: Meta-Overfitting: Self-Referential Improvers Get Better at Improving Only Where They Grew Up
dossier.claim: At a pre-registered checkpoint k* (12 accepted improver self-edits on home domain A), a Gödel-style improver's own procedure, with its memory wiped and domain facts scrubbed (Pk^s), helps a fresh executor improve on A by more than its gen-0 procedure (gate: H > 3 pp). On a far domain it helps by less (D_far = G_far(Pk^s,∅) − G_far(P0,∅) < 0, with a lineage-level 95% CI excluding 0 over n = 10 lineages). This deficit falls monotonically with pre-registered A→B distance and crosses zero between near and far domains. The paper is falsified if D_far ≥ 0 while the gate holds, which would be the first controlled evidence of domain-general procedural meta-learning.
dossier.design: One improver family, Gödel-lite, stripped down from Xunjian's Gödel Agent code. The improver is an open ~30B model (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B; DeepSeek V4 Flash as fallback) and the executor is an 8–9B open model. There are 10 independent lineages, each run on ALFWorld (A) to k* accepted improver edits. The incumbent improver is pre-registered, not the archive best. At k*, five arms (P0+∅, Pk^s+∅ primary, Pk+∅, P0+Mk, Pk+Mk) each run R = 5 rounds of improvement on a fresh seed executor, at a matched improver-call budget. The domains are A, ScienceWorld (near), SelfImprove-Bench games (mid) and Reasoning Gym (far). Distance is pre-registered as the zero-shot transfer gap of the evolved executor harness. The controls are a scrubber control (P0^s), a length-padded P0, a leak audit (regex count plus a blind 6-way domain judge), and a behavioural manipulation check (JS divergence of edit categories). Two contrasts make the result interpretable: the share of home gain removed by scrubbing (κ), and a design rule, "reset procedure, keep memory" (P0+Mk) vs forgetting (Pk+∅). Analysis is at the lineage level: a gate t-test, a paired t on D_far, a mixed-model dose slope and Holm correction, giving an MDE of about 4 pp. Everything is pre-registered on OSF by Dec 20. A 4-lineage replicate ports VERSE's optimizer with notes split from tools; if the port takes more than 7 days, it is replaced by a second-model Gödel-lite. The budget is about $1.4–1.7k, preceded by a ≤$50 pilot (Nov 16–23) with GO/PIVOT/KILL thresholds, and the preprint target is Feb 15, 2027.
dossier.history:
Round 1 had three separate T1/T2 candidates:
- procedure-vs-memory: a 2x2 transplant of improver procedure × memory. Critique score 72.5; standalone after proposal 71.3.
- meta-plasticity: a warm-start penalty on a new domain, plus reset arms. Critique about 68 (computed 67.9); standalone after proposal 72.9.
- swap-factorial: an improver × solver-state factorial. Critique 71.7.

The round-1 panel merged them into "Do Self-Referential Improvers Get Better at Improving? Effect, Cause, and Decay" (75.8, the lead paper). Swap-factorial became the slim Effect section, procedure-vs-memory became Cause, and meta-plasticity became Decay.

In round 2, both red teams cut the merged paper hard: novelty-killer 67.5, sharpness-reviewer 67.9. Each arm now had a one-cell 2026 precedent: MetaRSI §5.4 for Effect, SelfSearch Table 4 for Cause, VERSE App. G.2 for Decay. The paper also read as "three half-papers" with six hedged outcomes.

The v2 rewrite (effect-cause-decay.v2, "Meta-Overfitting", self-score 77.9) changes the paper as follows:
- **Decay** becomes the single directional, pre-registered claim.
- **Effect** is demoted to a home-gain gate.
- **Cause** shrinks to a fact-scrub (κ) and the "reset procedure, keep memory" design-rule contrast.
- **Scope** drops from 3 families and 40 generations to one family with 10 lineages and a single k*.
- **VERSE G.2** is recast as a motivating anomaly, reconciled by a distance dose that crosses zero.

The round-2 REPORT recommends it (77.9), with Blind-Spot Hiding (78.3) as backup.
dossier.priorScores: Round-1 critiques: procedure-vs-memory 72.5, meta-plasticity ~68 (67.9), swap-factorial 71.7. Round-1 standalone after proposal: meta-plasticity 72.9, procedure-vs-memory 71.3. Round-1 merged panel: 75.8. Round-2 red teams on the merged version: novelty-killer 67.5, sharpness-reviewer 67.9 (it projected ~76–80 if its fixes were made). v2 self-rescore: 77.9 (76.9 if the pilot needs a pivot; ~72.9 if a powered cross-domain improver probe appears before Feb 15). Path: R1 75.8 → R2 red team 67.5/67.9 → R2 v2 77.9 (Recommended).

closestPapers.title: VERSE: Verified Self-Evolving Optimizer for Agent Harnesses
closestPapers.summary: VERSE is a harness optimizer that evolves the executor's harness and also its own prompts, skills, tools, hooks and notes, with model weights fixed. A controlled study shows optimizer self-evolution fails without execution-based verification but gives the best result with it. VERSE improves four host optimizers on held-out SWE-rebench (42.3%) and OOD tasks (37.7%), and self-evolving optimizers build their own failure-analysis and verification tools. Per the round-2 red team, Appendix G.2 / Table 9 moves an evolved optimizer between SWE-rebench and Terminal-Bench, where the inherited optimizer helps (40.07 on SWE→TB round 1). The authors conclude the optimizer's 'methodology, its skills, notes, and tools' crosses domains.
closestPapers.relation: The most damaging Decay precedent. It is an existing cross-domain warm-vs-frozen optimizer comparison, and its result weakly contradicts the warm-start penalty. Its gaps: single runs, only 2 rounds on B, notes (memory) lumped with tools and prompts (procedure), no scrub, and one near-ish domain pair with no distance axis. v2 makes VERSE the motivating anomaly, predicts it sits on the positive (near) side of a zero-crossing dose, and adds a VERSE-port replicate with notes split from the scrubbed procedure.

closestPapers.title: SelfSearch: Reward-Free Search for Self-Improving Agents
closestPapers.summary: In SelfSearch, agents modify their own instructions, tools and procedures using records of previous self-improvement episodes, with no downstream reward during search. It improves population-mean success in all six model–benchmark settings (up to +11.2 pp on Terminal-Bench 2.1), and reaches 82.0% on TB2.1 with DeepSeek V4 Flash for $4.03 of search. Its Table 4 (per the red team) ablates 'w/o episode records' vs 'fixed improver' at generation 10 on SWE-bench Verified (GPT 76.2/74.2/74.6; DeepSeek 86.7/83.8/83.8).
closestPapers.relation: A crude, single-search, in-domain version of the Cause arm (procedure vs memory), framed in the idea's own words ('better at improving themselves'). It has no cross-domain test, no scrub, no distance axis, 2 lineages, and gaps of 1.7–2.9 pp that sit inside noise. Its generation 6–10 self-inspection tooling, never used downstream, is the source of v2's exploratory 'introspective drift' readout. The authors ask for replication across independent searches, so a v2 of SelfSearch is a plausible scoop vector for the in-domain split, though not for scrubbed far-domain decay.

closestPapers.title: RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training
closestPapers.summary: In RSI-Opt, a meta-agent evolves an optimizer-agent policy (prompt, playbook, code library, decision cadence) over 5 generations with an archive, on three training tasks. Summary z-scores rise from +10.48 to +14.33 on the evolution suite with Opus 5.5, and held-out results improve via cross-model transfer to GPT-5.5. Per the round-2 scoop check, held-out transfer peaks at generation 1 while the training-suite score keeps rising, which the authors call specialization. The evolved policy also slightly hurts its own generator model on held-out tasks.
closestPapers.relation: The closest precedent for the *shape* of the meta-overfitting claim (transfer peaks early, then specializes), but measured at the product/policy level. The meta-agent's own procedure is fixed. It has one evolution run with 3 final seeds, no matched gen-0 control, and no procedure × memory split. The 'home-model penalty' it hints at was considered as an add-on and deferred in v2.

closestPapers.title: FreeEvolve: Learning to Evolve Beyond Fixed Loops
closestPapers.summary: FreeEvolve lets an agent evolver control its own campaign: what to test, how much evidence to collect, which candidates to pursue and when to stop. The evolver follows an editable 'evolution skill' that is itself meta-evolved, scoring each candidate skill on the fresh target agent it produces. It improves held-out metrics by 13.6 points on average across τ³-bench, ARC-AGI-2, ARC-AGI-3 and TB2.1, and meta-evolved skills add 6.9 points over the seed skill on fresh target agents. In its evolver-capability ablation, a Haiku 4.5 evolver raises the evolution-set score (35.0→52.2) while the held-out score drops (33.3→32.2).
closestPapers.relation: It holds a fresh-worker Effect result (in-domain) and a single-point instance of meta-overfitting to the *task set* with a weak evolver, which the round-2 fact-check corrected from 'inert' to 'overfits'. v2 cites the Haiku result as motivation and gates it out (it requires a real home gain), then tests overfitting to the *domain* with a distance dose. FreeEvolve's claim that meta-evolved skills transfer across environments is exactly the 'improver edits are domain-general' assumption v2 tries to falsify.

closestPapers.title: MetaRSI / RSI2: A Meta-Recursive Self-Improving System for Recursive Self-Improving Systems Themselves
closestPapers.summary: MetaRSI is a meta-recursive self-improving system that improves the model-building machinery itself, extending RSI beyond coding and formal benchmarks. Per the fact-check and red team, §5.4 forks the same state S1 under the original vs the meta-updated improver at the same budget (+4.9 vs +7.2). A five-term curve over 5 outer seeds, on open Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, gives +26.2 vs +20.7 with a widening gap.
closestPapers.relation: It owns the in-domain Effect question ('does a later improver beat gen-0 from the same start?'), which is why v2 demotes Effect to a gate and cites MetaRSI as evidence the gate is attainable with an open model. It has no transfer, no state grid and no scrub.

closestPapers.title: Lineage Is Memory: Parent Inheritance and Feedback Disclosure in Short-Budget LLM-Guided Optimization
closestPapers.summary: Across 1,750 pre-registered runs on nine prompt- and program-synthesis benchmarks, the paper separates parent inheritance from feedback disclosure at matched evaluation budgets. Greedy parent inheritance drives most optimization progress, beating seed-reset resampling even when that gets clustered failure summaries or a larger proposer, because solved error modes are kept in the candidate. Per the red team, a one-sentence 'carry facts' instruction moves banking77 from 0.372 to 0.856.
closestPapers.relation: Object-level (the proposer is fixed), but it predicts that 'memory wins' and that domain facts migrate into artifacts. This is the basis for v2's κ estimand: scrubbing domain facts out of the evolved improver's code. It also set the rigor bar v2 adopts: pre-registration and n≈10 per cell. The κ ≥ 0.7 alternative ('procedures are memory in disguise') is its meta-level analogue.

closestPapers.title: Learning from Revision Consequences: Hindsight Meta-Experience Distillation for Self-Improving Agents (HMED)
closestPapers.summary: HMED re-executes the incumbent and revised Meta-Skills from the same restored discovery state, so that a revision's effect is observed under a shared condition. It distils each comparison into a reusable Meta-Experience record and improves Skill discovery over baselines on three interactive benchmarks (e.g., ALFWorld) with open and closed models. Per the fact-check, branch outcome and matched Δ disagree in sign for 45.5% (ALFWorld) and 75% (ScienceWorld) of revisions.
closestPapers.relation: Its frozen-meta-skill and reset-library reuse test equals v2's Pk+∅ cell, but in-domain, with no P0+Mk, no scrub and no distance. Its winner's-curse evidence is why v2 pre-registers the incumbent Pk. It also uses ALFWorld and ScienceWorld, v2's A and B_near, so numbers are comparable.

closestPapers.title: Agent Plasticity: Measuring Self-Improvement Through Experience
closestPapers.summary: Agents amortize experience into reusable artifacts inherited by future instances. Plasticity is defined as the efficiency of converting experience into held-out gains, measured at each checkpoint while accounting for learning cost. Frontier models show sharply different improvement trajectories despite comparable opportunities to learn.
closestPapers.relation: Object-level. It explicitly lists transfer of 'improvement strategies' across tasks, and actor–artifact swaps, as future work, so meta-level plasticity is unmeasured and Meta FAIR is a plausible scooper. Round-1 critique asked to adopt its plasticity metric; v2 uses its own gain G instead.

closestPapers.title: Auditing the Product, Not the Recursion: The Evaluation Evidence Behind Recursive Self-Improvement Claims
closestPapers.summary: A full-text coding of 114 RSI studies. Of the 26 claiming a better improvement procedure, only 4 compare earlier and later procedures from identical starting artifacts at matched budget, and only 22% audit two or more reruns. Three propositions show how selection effects, shared evaluator errors and state changes limit product evaluations, and the paper proposes a claim-indexed reporting standard, including a swap test.
closestPapers.relation: It publicly names the improver × state swap experiment (round-1 swap-factorial's framing) but runs none. It is both motivation and the source of the 75% forecast that a powered swap paper appears by May 2027. It is in-domain only; v2 adopts its reporting standard.

closestPapers.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
closestPapers.summary: Single agents, parallel agents and communicating teams in automated research all plateau as history accumulates, because agents anchor on their own past attempts and make fewer, smaller edits. Periodically discarding sessions and candidate history and restarting from the best candidate unblocks search at the same budget: up to 15% better than parallel agents and 39% better than a single agent.
closestPapers.relation: It owns the object-level claim that 'reset restores progress', and its forgetting reset (wipe context, keep the best artifact) is the analogue of v2's Pk+∅ arm. v2's design rule ('reset procedure, keep memory' beats forgetting on far domains) runs directly against Forgetting's practice. The REPORT flags defending that claim against these authors as an open question.

closestPapers.title: Gödel Agent: A Self-Referential Agent Framework for Recursive Self-Improvement
closestPapers.summary: Gödel Agent is a self-evolving framework, inspired by the Gödel machine, in which an LLM agent dynamically modifies its own logic and behaviour, guided only by high-level objectives and not by fixed meta-learning routines. On mathematical reasoning and agent tasks it shows continual self-improvement, surpassing hand-crafted agents.
closestPapers.relation: The mentor's (Xunjian Yin) own system, and the base of Gödel-lite, the primary improver family. The idea asks whether Gödel Agent's self-referential edits are meta-learning or meta-specialization. This is why relevance is scored 5/5 and engineering risk is lowest.

feedback.point: The procedure/memory partition is ill-defined: task knowledge leaks into the procedure's code and prompts, and the archive holds procedural information. Without a knowledge-scrubbed arm and a leak audit, the shares are not identifiable.
feedback.addressed: Yes. The scrubbed Pk^s is the primary arm, with an LLM scrubber, a regex count plus blind 6-way domain-judge leak audit, three scrub strengths (the κ curve) and a P0^s scrubber control.

feedback.point: Transplant compatibility: Ik memory may be formatted for Ik's retrieval code. Add a format-adapter arm.
feedback.addressed: Not addressed. v2 has no format-adapter arm, although P0+Mk (the design-rule arm) is exactly where an interface artifact would bias the result.

feedback.point: The base improver effect may not exist, so the decomposition is conditional on C1. Replace the arbitrary 70/30 thresholds with pre-registered estimands and CIs.
feedback.addressed: Yes. There is a home-gain gate (H > 3 pp SESOI) with a pilot kill rule, the 70/30 thresholds are gone, and κ is reported with a CI.

feedback.point: Use ≥3 improver families, and make cross-domain the arbiter, not an add-on.
feedback.addressed: Partly. Cross-domain is now the primary test. Families were deliberately cut to one (Gödel-lite) plus a small 4-lineage replicate (VERSE port or second-model Gödel-lite), on the opposite advice of the round-2 sharpness reviewer.

feedback.point: Add memory-dose curves and a procedure share over generations (k ∈ {0,5,10,20,40}). Frame the work as a reusable 'Transplant Test' protocol. Preprint by Feb 2027.
feedback.addressed: Mostly not. v2 uses a single k* (k*/2 only if budget allows) and has no memory-dose curve. The protocol and scrubber release is planned, and the preprint is targeted for Feb 15.

feedback.point: Novelty is thin: the headline is the forgetting result (2610.20563, Fork-and-Flush, Continual AutoResearch) moved one level up. The paper must isolate the meta level.
feedback.addressed: Largely. The primary arm is memory-free and scrubbed, so the decay must be carried by the procedure. A manipulation check (edit-category JS divergence) confirms the procedure behaves differently.

feedback.point: The meta level may not exist in practice: SelfImprove-Bench HyperAgents retained 0% improver edits. Report meta-edit share and use a fixed-improver control.
feedback.addressed: Partly. The generation clock counts accepted improver edits, and the pilot GO threshold requires ≥1 accepted improver edit per 4 iterations, with a pivot to forced improver edits. Open-model drivability is still a risk.

feedback.point: Power: the ratio PR(k) of two noisy gains with 3 seeds is unreadable. Use paired differences, a log-k dose and pre-registration.
feedback.addressed: Yes, with changes. v2 uses a paired difference D at the lineage level (n=10, MDE ≈4 pp). The k-dose was replaced by a domain-distance dose.

feedback.point: Confounds: context bloat under matched $, domain distance (a single A→B pair is uninterpretable), and the selection gate.
feedback.addressed: Yes for bloat (memory-free primary arms plus a padded-P0 control) and for distance (4 domains with a pre-registered distance).

feedback.point: Use published reset baselines (Forgetting, Fork-and-Flush) and adopt Agent Plasticity's P metric. Avoid the 'stability-plasticity' framing (owned by 2610.25858).
feedback.addressed: Partly. The Forgetting analogue is the Pk+∅ cell, but Fork-and-Flush is absent and the bespoke gain G is used instead of P. v2 still describes the claim as 'the meta-level version of the stability–plasticity dilemma', against the advice.

feedback.point: Novelty is a design, not an idea: 2610.27610 proposed the swap test, and MetaRSI, RSIFlow, FreeEvolve and Skill∞ ran same-start swaps.
feedback.addressed: Yes. The swap/Effect part was demoted to a gate, and the contribution is now the directional Decay law plus a design rule.

feedback.point: A capability floor makes a null uninterpretable. Include a capable improver and a capability axis.
feedback.addressed: Partly. A null is made readable by the gate, the manipulation check and the MDE, and DeepSeek V4 Flash is the fallback. There is no capability axis.

feedback.point: Headroom vs state confound; transplant-compatibility control; winner's curse in checkpoint choice; lineage is the real unit.
feedback.addressed: Yes for headroom (a fresh seed executor on each domain fixes it), winner's curse (incumbent Pk pre-registered) and lineage as the unit (n=10). Compatibility is only partly handled (scrub diff check; no adapter).

feedback.point: Kitchen sink: drop the directedness e-value (2610.14662's method), the SRN baseline and the standalone Hyperagents replication.
feedback.addressed: Yes, all dropped.

feedback.point: Each arm has a one-cell 2026 precedent: MetaRSI §5.4 (Effect), SelfSearch Table 4 (Cause), VERSE G.2 (Decay). Three groups plus 2610.27610 name the remaining experiment, so the paper reads as 'three existing ablations, powered' (K4-flavoured).
feedback.addressed: Yes. The paper is cut to the Decay claim; Effect is a gate, and Cause is reduced to κ plus the design rule. The proposal argues for K4 avoidance through the law plus design rule.

feedback.point: VERSE G.2 weakly contradicts the warm-start penalty (the inherited optimizer helps SWE→TB).
feedback.addressed: Yes, by reframing. VERSE is the motivating anomaly, a distance dose crossing zero is predicted, and a VERSE port with notes split from tools tests the explanation.

feedback.point: 'Memory wins' is expected given Lineage Is Memory, SelfSearch and MetaSkill σx. Procedure and memory are unidentified without a κ fact-scrub. Make κ ('procedures are memory in disguise') the headline.
feedback.addressed: Partly. κ is a reported estimand and a pre-registered alternative (κ ≥ 0.7), but the headline went with the sharpness reviewer's Decay claim instead.

feedback.point: Add a placebo/shuffled-memory 'vacuous-history' arm.
feedback.addressed: Only as an optional arm on A (Pk+shuffle(Mk)), if budget allows.

feedback.point: Scoop odds: a powered improver procedure × memory crossing has a 55–65% chance of appearing before 2027-05-15; cross-domain decay with a reset factorial ~30%. Preprint by early Feb, and check OpenReview ICLR 2027 by hand.
feedback.addressed: Partly. The preprint is targeted for Feb 15 with weekly citer checks. OpenReview ICLR 2027 is still UNCHECKED (proxy blocked).

feedback.point: Low-scoop angles: introspective drift, home-model penalty, accepted-edit clock.
feedback.addressed: Introspective drift is kept as exploratory RQ5, and the accepted-edit clock is adopted. The home-model penalty is deferred.

feedback.point: No crisp headline: six hedged 'all publishable' branches, and a penalty claim stacking four conjuncts. Commit to one directional prediction.
feedback.addressed: Yes. There is one directional claim (D_far < 0) with a stated falsifier and two single-interpretation alternatives.

feedback.point: Precondition: is there anything to decay? Make Effect a gate with a kill rule.
feedback.addressed: Yes: a 3 pp SESOI gate, a pilot GO/PIVOT/KILL table, and the kill fires if the unscrubbed Pk fails after one pivot.

feedback.point: Matched-$ penalizes long memory (token tax), and Pk may be longer. Use a memory-free primary arm and a length-padded P0.
feedback.addressed: Yes. There is a padded-P0 control, procedure length is a covariate, and the memory arms get a matched-token re-analysis.

feedback.point: Domain content leaking into the procedure makes a penalty trivial specialization. The penalty must survive scrubbing.
feedback.addressed: Yes. Pk^s is the primary arm, with a leak audit and a scrub-strength curve.

feedback.point: Power was overstated (probes counted instead of lineages). Use ≥10 lineages, a lineage-level test, and no ln k slope as primary.
feedback.addressed: Yes: n=10 lineages, MDE ≈4 pp, rising to 14 lineages if σ > 5 pp.

feedback.point: Near/far is uncalibrated. Use a dose over 3–4 B domains with pre-registered distance.
feedback.addressed: Yes. There are 3 B domains, ordered by the executor-harness zero-shot transfer gap and checked against an embedding distance.

feedback.point: Sprawl is a lab-year. Cut to 1 family, 4 arms, k ∈ {0,k*}, existing generators and 1 mechanism readout. Lift beyond 'just measurement' with a dose law and a tested design rule.
feedback.addressed: Mostly. v2 keeps 5 arms rather than 4 (adds Pk+∅ for κ) plus 2 controls, and keeps 2 readouts (manipulation check and introspective drift). It uses existing environments only, and the design rule P0+Mk vs Pk+∅ is the secondary test.

feedback.point: K3: confirm a Qwen3.5-27B Gödel-lite actually self-modifies, and keep a fallback.
feedback.addressed: Yes. The pilot measures the improver-edit rate. v2 names Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with a DeepSeek V4 Flash fallback (the reviewer's sketch said 27B).

feedback.point: FreeEvolve's Haiku evolver does not stall; it meta-overfits (evolution set 35.0→52.2, held-out 33.3→32.2). SelfImprove-Bench was misquoted: the like-for-like comparison is 1.326 vs 1.207, and 1.433 is an agent with zero improver edits. Open models can drive Gödel/DGM loops (VERSE, MetaRSI, HMED), but stock Hyperagents failed with open models in 2609.17817.
feedback.addressed: Yes. The Haiku result is cited as motivation, Gödel-lite is chosen over stock Hyperagents, and SelfImprove-Bench's forced-edit trick is the pivot.

feedback.point: RSI-Opt 2610.32026 already shows evolved-policy transfer peaking at gen 1 (product level). Decay must claim the improver's own improvement rate on B. It also hints at a 'home-model penalty'.
feedback.addressed: Yes for differentiation (the improver procedure on a fresh executor, scrubbed, with matched gen-0). The home-model penalty is deferred to follow-up.

feedback.point: SelfSearch 2609.37968 is the main must-cite for Cause ('suggestive but within noise; we power it'). Its generation 6–10 introspective drift is a new low-scoop idea. Add MetaExp 2610.21492 to Decay and Aspire's regression-recovery confound to the analysis.
feedback.addressed: SelfSearch, MetaExp and introspective drift are all incorporated. Aspire's confound is not explicitly mentioned in v2.

feedback.point: A powered improver × state swap paper is 75% likely by May 2027 (50% by Feb). Anchor on Decay plus one mechanism claim, which the wave will not reach.
feedback.addressed: Yes. That is the v2 strategy.

feedback.point: REPORT suggests folding it in as a memory-transplant arm of #1, since its expected result is null.
feedback.addressed: Not incorporated into v2.

openRisks: Scoop: the red team puts a powered improver procedure × memory crossing at 55–65% before May 2027, and the scrubbed cross-domain decay design at ~25–30%. Likely sources: SelfSearch v2, a VERSE follow-up that splits notes from tools, Organon/RSI-Opt v2, Agent Plasticity, and ICML-2027 submissions going public around late Jan–Feb.
OpenReview-only ICLR 2027 submissions and the NeurIPS 2026 workshop accepted lists are still UNCHECKED (the proxy blocked OpenReview).

Three abstract-only papers (2610.14662, 2610.31436, 2611.07624) must be read in full before the pre-registration freezes. 2611.07624 (Beneath the Surface) was deep-read in round 1 but is still listed as unread in v2.

Precondition and K2: open-model Gödel-lite may produce too few accepted improver edits, or a home gain below the 3 pp SESOI. SelfImprove-Bench HyperAgents kept 0% improver edits unless forced. If the gate fails after one pivot, the paper is killed.

The scrubber validity is load-bearing. Over-scrubbing handicaps Pk^s; under-scrubbing makes the decay mere specialization. The P0^s control, diff check and leak judge help, but the operational definition of 'procedure' remains contestable.
The P0+Mk design-rule arm has no format-adapter control: gen-k memory may be formatted for Pk's retrieval code, so the design-rule comparison may be biased against P0+Mk.

The distance metric (the executor-harness zero-shot transfer gap) may not order the domains as intended, and ALFWorld→Reasoning Gym is a big task-format jump. The dose slope needs simulation-based power from pilot variance.
One primary family. Generality rests on a 4-lineage replicate whose VERSE port may be dropped under the 7-day rule.

Internal inconsistencies to reconcile:
- v2 says 5 arms, a 35B-A3B improver, k*=12 and $1.4–1.7k.
- The red team's sketch said 4 arms, a 27B improver and ~$1.2k.
- v2 still uses the 'stability–plasticity' framing that the R1 critique said is owned by 2610.25858.
Resources: GPU serving for the executor and improver needs a 4–8×A100/H100-class node, which is not yet confirmed with Xunjian.
A defensibility question: the 'reset procedure, keep memory' design rule contradicts the Forgetting (2610.20563) practice.

judges.strongest: The paper makes one directional, pre-registered, falsifiable claim: the scrubbed, memory-free improver has D_far < 0, and the deficit varies with a dose of domain distance. Several ICLR 2027 papers now claim the opposite (RSI-Harness EOrtreQLbv, which reports improver transfer up to 4.5x; MetaEvoForge 0b4wysHrzh; FreeEvolve; Looped-RSI). None of them wipes memory, scrubs domain facts or grades distance. So a well-controlled sign flip on far domains would directly bound a live consensus. A replication of the positive transfer under these controls would still be a citable audit. Relevance to Gödel Agent is maximal, and the lineage-level stats (n=10, Holm, a gate, an MDE of about 4 pp) are well above the field's norm.
judges.weakest: The design space is now crowded, and generality is thin. The ICLR 2027 sweep shows RSI-Harness (EOrtreQLbv) asks the same question with the opposite answer. Learning to Repair the Learner (aEPJT4hW84) already does a code × history crossing (inherited procedure explains 45% of gain). Improvement by Inheritance (ZMmJDeDTXk) owns the nested-replay improver × state assay and confirms that improvers almost never edit themselves. The only novelty left is the distance axis plus the scrub. That rests on one improver family, one home domain (ALFWorld) and one k*. A contestable scrubber operationally defines what counts as procedure. ALFWorld to Reasoning Gym is a task-format jump that confounds distance with interface. Finally, open-model Gödel-lite may never reach 12 accepted improver edits, and ZMmJDeDTXk makes this K2 risk empirically real.
judges.mustFix:
1. Reframe the paper as a bounded rebuttal of the ICLR 2027 positive-transfer wave. Cite EOrtreQLbv (RSI-Harness), 0b4wysHrzh (MetaEvoForge), 8UyLPIcKqX, sBH9cdajAw, nw2tokNgb2 and rM2eQio3e3. Include a pre-registered cell that reproduces their positive near-domain transfer, so the zero-crossing is shown and not just asserted. Ideally run RSI-Harness's own setup or benchmark with and without the memory wipe and scrub.
2. Cite aEPJT4hW84 and ZMmJDeDTXk as the measurement lineage, and drop any claim that the crossing design is new.
3. Strengthen generality with a second home domain, or swap A and B for at least 4 lineages, so the result is not one ALFWorld artifact. Also give the second improver family a firm budget instead of the 7-day-drop VERSE port.
4. Separate distance from task-format change. Add an intermediate far domain with the same interface, or define distance in a way that does not mechanically correlate with format.
5. Add the format-adapter control for P0+Mk.
6. Use the pilot to verify the improver-edit rate directly against ZMmJDeDTXk's near-zero self-edit finding. Pre-specify what a forced-edit pivot means for the claim's validity.
7. Drop the stability–plasticity framing.
8. Confirm GPU access with the mentor before the OSF freeze.
judges.reviewerQuote: RSI-Harness and MetaEvoForge already report that evolved improvers transfer across domains, and code × history crossings exist. This paper's contribution therefore hinges on a single-family, single-home-domain distance dose whose 'far' end conflates domain distance with task-format change and whose 'procedure' is defined by the authors' own scrubber.

judges.strongest: It makes one signed, pre-registered prediction that runs against a field consensus that is now forming. RSI-Harness (EOrtreQLbv), MetaEvoForge (0b4wysHrzh), FreeEvolve and Looped-RSI (sBH9cdajAw) all claim that evolved improvers transfer across domains. None of them wipes memory, scrubs the procedure's code, or grades domain distance, and the scrubbed Pk^s arm plus the distance dose is exactly the control those papers lack. It also sits directly on the mentor's Gödel Agent codebase, so relevance is maximal and engineering risk is lowest.
judges.weakest:
The ICLR 2027 sweep moves the ground under the idea. RSI-Harness (EOrtreQLbv) asks the same question and reports the opposite sign: its improver transfers to unseen models, benchmarks and domains at up to 4.5x the gain, while its harness does not. Several other submissions also report positive improver transfer: MetaEvoForge (0b4wysHrzh), FreeEvolve (8UyLPIcKqX), Looped-RSI (sBH9cdajAw) and Meta-TTL (nw2tokNgb2). On top of that, Improvement by Inheritance (ZMmJDeDTXk) and Learning to Repair the Learner (aEPJT4hW84, a code x history crossing) already own the swap and crossing designs, and both confirm that improvers rarely edit themselves. That leaves three problems:
- The paper is now a bounded rebuttal resting on one improver family and one open ~30B improver.
- The gate is genuinely at risk: 12 accepted self-edits from an open model, which ZMmJDeDTXk suggests is hard to get.
- A null (D_far ≥ 0) is no longer "first evidence of domain-general meta-learning", because RSI-Harness and MetaEvoForge already claim that. The falsifying outcome therefore loses most of its publishability.
Reviewers will also ask whether the "far" domain (ALFWorld→Reasoning Gym) is simply a change in task format, not meta-overfitting.
judges.mustFix:
(1) Reframe the abstract and introduction explicitly as a rebuttal or boundary condition for EOrtreQLbv, 0b4wysHrzh, 8UyLPIcKqX and sBH9cdajAw. Include a reproduced positive near-domain cell in the RSI-Harness style, and add an arm where memory is not wiped, so the paper can show that their transfer is near-domain or carried by memory.
(2) Re-pre-register the null branch. With D_far ≥ 0 it becomes "first controlled, memory-scrubbed confirmation of RSI-Harness". Say what that adds, or accept that the paper is effectively one-sided.
(3) Present ZMmJDeDTXk and aEPJT4hW84 as the lineage of the design, not as contributions.
(4) Add a second improver model, not a 4-lineage replicate, so that the decay is not specific to one model. A capable, cheap closed or open improver such as DeepSeek V4 Flash should be a full arm.
(5) Add the format-adapter control for P0+Mk.
(6) Use a far domain that keeps the agentic interaction format (e.g. an RSIBench Q9AHmuAk4Y split), so distance is not confounded with task format.
(7) Confirm the GPU node and run the pilot that tests the edit rate before freezing the OSF pre-registration.
(8) Drop the "stability–plasticity" framing.
judges.reviewerQuote: Given that RSI-Harness and MetaEvoForge already report that evolved improvers transfer across domains, this paper's single-family, single-open-model evidence that they do not on one hand-picked far domain reads as a boundary condition on a format shift, not a law of meta-overfitting.

judges.strongest: The claim is a single falsifiable directional claim (D_far < 0, with a dose that crosses zero) that runs against the ICLR 2027 positive-transfer wave: RSI-Harness EOrtreQLbv, MetaEvoForge 0b4wysHrzh, FreeEvolve, Looped-RSI and Meta-TTL. None of these wipes memory, scrubs domain facts out of the procedure, or grades domain distance. A negative result would bound their claims, and a positive one would be the first controlled evidence of domain-general meta-learning, so either outcome can be published. It fits the mentor perfectly, since it is built on Gödel Agent. The pre-registration, n=10 lineages, the scrub, the leak audit and the gate are well above the bar this literature has set so far.
judges.weakest: On novelty, the ICLR 2027 sweep turns the "motivating anomaly" into a crowd. RSI-Harness (EOrtreQLbv) asks this exact question ("better improver or just better harness?") and reports the opposite sign: the improver transfers to unseen domains at up to 4.5x. MetaEvoForge and Looped-RSI add more positive results. The 5-arm Pk×Mk crossing has a design precedent in Learning to Repair the Learner (aEPJT4hW84, code×history crossing, 45% procedure share). The swap assay itself belongs to Improvement by Inheritance (ZMmJDeDTXk), which also finds that improvers almost never edit themselves. That finding makes feasibility the dominant risk. Ten open-model lineages that each reach 12 *accepted* improver edits, followed by 5 arms × 4 domains × 5 rounds, with a GPU node that is not confirmed, is a lot for a solo undergrad in 6 months. The scrubber's operational definition of "procedure" is still contestable, and the P0+Mk arm has no format adapter.
judges.mustFix: (1) Reframe the paper as a bounded rebuttal of the ICLR 2027 positive-transfer wave. Cite and engage RSI-Harness EOrtreQLbv, MetaEvoForge 0b4wysHrzh, FreeEvolve 8UyLPIcKqX, Looped-RSI sBH9cdajAw, Meta-TTL nw2tokNgb2 and RSIBench Q9AHmuAk4Y. Add a reproduction of their positive near-domain cell, with memory left in and no scrub, as the baseline that the controls then take apart. Consider adding RSIBench as a far domain. (2) Cite Improvement by Inheritance ZMmJDeDTXk and Learning to Repair the Learner aEPJT4hW84 as the source of the crossing/swap method, and claim novelty only for the distance axis and the scrub. (3) Make the pilot answer the improver-edit-rate question before anything else: a forced-edit pivot, and a fallback k* of about 6 if 12 accepted edits is unreachable. Confirm the GPU node with Xunjian before Nov 23. (4) Add a format-adapter control for P0+Mk. Drop the 'stability-plasticity' framing. (5) Cut scope if the pilot variance is high: for example, 3 domains, 3 arms (P0, Pk^s, Pk+∅), and the replicate only if time allows.
judges.reviewerQuote: Several concurrent works (RSI-Harness, MetaEvoForge) report that evolved improvers transfer across domains, and this paper's opposite conclusion rests on a single open-model Gödel-lite family, a hand-built scrubber whose notion of 'procedure' is contestable, and a domain-distance ordering of only four points, so I am not convinced the negative far-domain effect is not an artifact of weak improvers or over-scrubbing.

dossier.title: Self-Reference Buys No Self-Knowledge: Lineage-Level Privileged Access, Memory Transplant, and Self-Model Drift in Self-Modifying Agents
dossier.claim: This is the sharpened version from the bold-check. After self-modifying Gödel-lite lineages diverge, a foreign improver predicts the target agent's failures as well as the lineage's own improver, and selects repairs as well too. The foreign improver uses the same base model and is given the target lineage's code, traces and memory. Prediction is scored by within-task and disagreement-subset AUROC. The Social-Relations "self" effect is about zero once memory is transplanted: removing memory hurts, while changing the reader does not. The improver's stored self-description also goes stale faster than a stranger's fresh reading of the current code. The claim is falsified if the diagonal self effect is above 0.05 AUROC on the lineage-disagreement subset and survives a full memory transplant. That outcome would be the first evidence of procedure-level privileged self-access.
dossier.design:
1. Evolve 8 Gödel-lite lineages with open Qwen-class models (27B/9B) and checkpoint them at gens {5,10,20,40}. Checkpoints count only after a manipulation check shows divergence: agent code differs and behavior disagrees on at least 20% of tasks. Gen-0 is dropped.
2. At each checkpoint, run a full 8×8 improver×agent round-robin crossed with memory access {target lineage's memory/self-description, none}. This gives a reader-identity × memory 2×2 per pair. The decisive arm is a foreign reader given the target's memory.
3. Probes:
   - Predict pass/fail. Score with within-task AUROC on repeated runs and AUROC on the lineage-disagreement subset; report pooled AUROC only as a contrast, alongside a difficulty oracle.
   - Repair. Fix the candidate edits and score each with matched same-state rollouts of the target agent (as in 2610.38610). Separate selection regret (self-selected vs foreign-selected edits) from proposal quality (self-proposed vs foreign-proposed edits).
   - Describe. Score the description with a behavior-prediction probe.
4. Analyze with a Social Relations Model that splits accuracy into actor (improver skill), partner (agent legibility) and relationship/self (diagonal) effects. This controls the lineage-quality confound.
5. Drift probe: a self-description written at gen k is scored against gen k+j behavior, compared with a foreign reader's fresh description of the current code. The result is a staleness curve.
6. Pilot (under $50, 1 week): 4 lineages × 10 gens on one task family, to measure the inter-lineage disagreement rate (no power if it is under ~10%). Full budget is about $1–1.5k.
dossier.history:
The idea first appears in round 2 as bold idea SHARP-2 in bold_ideas.md. It has no round-1 candidate, critique or proposal. The bold idea is the only place it was pitched, and it went from there to the bold-check.

As pitched, the claim was that the own improver predicts failures no better than a foreign improver, with a repair advantage ≤0 that shrinks with generation. Gen-0 was included, the metric was pooled pass/fail AUROC on 200 tasks, and the budget was about $500.

The bold-check (73/100 as pitched, about 77 with fixes) reshaped it:
- "Self" was redefined as the lineage, not the weights.
- A memory-transplant 2×2 and Social Relations Model analysis were added.
- Gen-0 was dropped (logic bug) and replaced with post-divergence checkpoints.
- Scoring moved to within-task and disagreement-subset AUROC.
- Self-model staleness drift was promoted to the headline dynamic.

In the final round-2 REPORT it ranks #7 (73, "Promising / fold"). The verdict was that the expected result is null and the idea works better as a memory-transplant arm of the recommended paper #1 (Meta-Overfitting / Effect-Cause-Decay, with its procedure × memory transplant), not as a standalone paper.
dossier.priorScores: R1: none (new in R2) → R2 bold-check 73.3 as pitched (N3.5 S3.0 R5.0 C3.0 F4.0 T4.0), about 77 with fixes; REPORT rank #7, 73, "Promising / fold into #1"

closestPapers.title: Strangers to Themselves: What Language Models Say About Themselves Is Generic
closestPapers.summary: The paper turns self-knowledge into a prediction test across nine behavioral evaluations. Direct self-report barely predicts behavior (r=+0.04). An item-informed question about 'capable AI agents in general' predicts as well (+0.28), and other models' self-answers predict the target at least as well as its own. Frontier scale shows no self-specific gain, and first-person framing mainly shifts reports in a flattering direction.
closestPapers.relation: This is the closest conceptual scoop. It already establishes the model-level null that an outsider knows you as well as you do, including on τ² agentic evals (per the bold-check deep read), and it reports a fine-tuning-induced 'fixed-point' drift. It leaves open self-modifying lineages, code-level self-description, a repair outcome, and drift caused by self-modification. It also lowers this idea's Surprise score, because a null result is predicted.

closestPapers.title: Masked by Consensus: Disentangling Privileged Knowledge in LLM Correctness
closestPapers.summary: The paper compares self-probes and external probes (cross-model and embedding) on hidden states for predicting a target model's correctness, using Gemma-2-9B, Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen-2.5-7B. On full test sets there is no premium, because models agree on about 75–80% of items. On disagreement subsets, a significant self-premium (about 5% AUC) appears for factual QA but not for math.
closestPapers.relation: This is the methodological must-cite. It shows that pooled self-vs-other comparisons tie by construction under high agreement, which is why this idea moved to disagreement-subset AUROC. It is weight-level and single-model only, with no lineages, no code self-reference and no repair.

closestPapers.title: Evaluating and Improving LLM Self-Modeling
closestPapers.summary: The paper introduces a benchmark of verifiable self-modeling questions, for example whether a prompt edit would change the model's answer. Models show non-trivial but limited skill with systematic counterfactual errors. RL on synthetic data improves self-modeling, but the gains do not appear to come from privileged access to the model's internal decision process.
closestPapers.relation: This is another model-level null on privileged self-access; per the bold-check, cross-model explainers show no own-model advantage. It does not cover lineages, code-level self-modification or generational drift. Together with 2609.09899, it is why reviewers would say 'known null, transplanted to agents'.

closestPapers.title: Repairs for Whom? Evaluator-Executor Mismatch in Selecting Repairs for Failed LLM Agents
closestPapers.summary: The paper holds failed trajectories and candidate single-step repairs fixed, and labels each candidate with independent rollouts of the deployed policy (ALFWorld, WebShop). Greedy replay, stronger-model rollouts and log-reading judges all lose deployment value relative to the deployed agent's own rollouts. For example, 14B rollouts lose 0.25 in ALFWorld when choosing repairs for a 7B agent.
closestPapers.relation: Its lesson is that 'self' helps through execution (own rollouts), not through reading (the self-judge is among the worst evaluators). This dictates the repair-arm design: matched same-executor rollouts, and separating self-read from self-rollout and proposal from selection. It is not about improvers or lineages.

closestPapers.title: Disentangling Task Difficulty from Run-Level Failure in Agent Failure Prediction
closestPapers.summary: The paper argues that agent failure predictors reporting AUROC of 0.85–0.94 owe much of that to pooling runs across tasks, so they mostly recognize harder tasks rather than detect run-level failure. It separates task-level difficulty from run-level prediction.
closestPapers.relation: It kills the originally pitched metric, pooled pass/fail AUROC on 200 tasks, which both self and foreign readers would score well on via shared difficulty. The bold-check cites its finding that a difficulty oracle reaches 0.945 pooled but 0.5 within-task. The idea now uses within-task and disagreement AUROC with a difficulty-oracle control.

closestPapers.title: Does Failure Feedback Direct Agent Self-Modification?
closestPapers.summary: Across 145 modifications in public Darwin Gödel Machine logs, the paper finds no target-specific repair advantage from failure feedback. In controlled studies, relevant feedback can raise target repair (+20pp for Qwen3-4B), but target repair does not reliably transfer to held-out improvement.
closestPapers.relation: This is a companion result: self-modification edits are not target-directed. Together with a null self-advantage, it would support a 'selection, not self-knowledge' account of self-improving agents. It runs no self-vs-foreign comparison.

closestPapers.title: Identifying Introspection From the Inside
closestPapers.summary: The authors use LoRA fine-tuning to have models make decisions according to latent preference functions, and find that accurate self-reports of the learned preferences can emerge without self-report supervision. Weight ablations show preference representations shift to earlier layers, consistent with faithful self-report requiring access by verbalization mechanisms.
closestPapers.relation: This is weight-level introspection evidence that some genuine self-access can exist mechanistically. It motivates the question at the code/lineage level but does not test it there, and it has no foreign-reader comparison.

closestPapers.title: Gödel Agent: A Self-Referential Agent Framework for Recursive Self-Improvement
closestPapers.summary: Gödel Agent is a self-evolving framework inspired by the Gödel machine, in which an LLM agent dynamically inspects and modifies its own logic and code without predefined optimization routines.
