It reports gains over hand-designed and meta-learned agents on several reasoning and coding tasks.
closestPapers.relation: This is the foundation (the mentor's own paper). Its premise that self-reference gives useful self-awareness is exactly what this idea tests. The Gödel-lite lineages are built on this framework.

feedback.point: At gen-0 all lineages share the same agent, so self = foreign by identity and the falsifier '≥0.05 at gen-0, not declining with k' cannot be evaluated. The prediction should be 'never appears' or 'rises then falls'.
feedback.addressed: Yes, in the sharpened version. Gen-0 is dropped, checkpoints at {5,10,20,40} come after a verified divergence check, and the prediction is reframed.

feedback.source: R2 bold-check (W2, guaranteed tie / K2 risk)
feedback.point: Pooled pass/fail AUROC is dominated by shared task difficulty (2610.05572) and inter-lineage agreement (2604.12373). A null would therefore be an artifact.
feedback.addressed: Yes. Scoring moves to within-task (repeated runs) and lineage-disagreement-subset AUROC, with pooled AUROC only as a contrast alongside a difficulty oracle. The pilot measures the disagreement rate for power.

feedback.point: With shared weights, any self-advantage must come from lineage memory or a co-adapted procedure. A foreign reader of the same code and traces already gets most of the memory, so memory access must be manipulated explicitly.
feedback.addressed: Yes. 'Self' is now the lineage, and a reader-identity × memory-access 2×2 is added, with foreign+memory as the decisive arm.

feedback.point: 2609.09899 already shows that an outside analyst beats self, including on agentic τ². A null is the expected result, which caps Surprise (S=3.0) and Novelty (N=3.5).
feedback.addressed: Partly. Surprise is moved to the memory-vs-procedure decomposition and to drift caused by self-modification. The REPORT still judges the expected result as null and recommends folding the idea into #1.

feedback.point: Better lineages produce both better improvers and more predictable agents. A raw self-vs-foreign difference is confounded.
feedback.addressed: Yes. A Social Relations Model (actor/partner/relationship) analysis is added on an 8×8 round-robin.

feedback.point: Repair must be scored by the same executor with matched rollouts, as in 2610.38610, and self-proposal must be separated from who verifies or selects.
feedback.addressed: Yes. The repair arm now has fixed candidate edits, matched same-state rollouts, and separate selection-regret and proposal-quality comparisons.

feedback.point: The repair arms with rollouts will exceed the pitched $500. Realistic budget is about $1–1.5k.
feedback.addressed: Acknowledged. Budget revised to $1–1.5k, with a pilot under $50.

feedback.point: No lineage-level self-vs-foreign study was found across alphaXiv, S2, Gödel Agent forward citations or ICLR 2027 searches (K1 no). The question and its likely answer are established at the model level, so the object (lineages, drift, code self-description, repair) is new but the question is not.
feedback.addressed: Framing is revised to position the work as the agentic, self-modifying successor to 2609.09899 and 2604.12373, and as a mechanism study for Gödel Agent.

feedback.point: The Zero-Call Verification hint (Opus 5.5 accepted 65 of 66 failed attempts by its own agent) was confirmed only from the abstract. That paper has no foreign-judge comparison, so it is a weak motivating anecdote.
feedback.addressed: Not used in the sharpened claim. It should not be cited as self-vs-other evidence.

feedback.point: Ranked #7 at 73, 'Promising / fold'. The expected result is null, and the idea is better as a memory-transplant arm of recommended paper #1 (Meta-Overfitting / Effect-Cause-Decay).
feedback.addressed: Open decision. The bold-check also suggests slotting it into #1's 'Cause' (procedure-vs-memory) section and deciding early whether it stands alone.

openRisks: Expected null result: with 2609.09899, 2608.30980 and 2604.12373 already published, reviewers may call it a 'known null transplanted to agents'. The surprise rests on the memory-transplant decomposition and the drift curve landing cleanly.
Power: lineages sharing a base model may disagree on too few tasks (under ~10%) for disagreement-subset AUROC to have power. The pilot must check this first.
Divergence may be insufficient. Gödel-lite lineages might not diverge behaviorally by gen 5–20, which would make self/foreign nearly identical.

Overlap with recommended paper #1 (procedure × memory transplant). The REPORT recommends folding this idea in, so standalone novelty is thin, and SelfSearch, RSI-Opt and similar papers already run partial transplant cells.
Repair arms with matched rollouts over an 8×8×4 design push cost to about $1–1.5k and add engineering load.
The interpretation of a positive self effect (co-adapted procedure vs leftover memory leakage through code comments or traces) depends on a clean memory-transplant manipulation.
SkillMentor 2607.27360 (trained external mentor diagnoses an executor) was not deep-read, and the Zero-Call claim was verified only from its abstract.

judges.strongest: It directly tests the premise behind Gödel Agent, the mentor's own framework: that self-reference gives a self-modifying agent useful self-knowledge. The design is unusually well controlled for the question. It uses an 8×8 round-robin analyzed with a Social Relations Model to separate the lineage-quality confound, a reader-identity × memory-transplant 2×2, scoring on within-task and disagreement-subset AUROC with a difficulty oracle (which avoids the pooled-AUROC artifacts shown in 2610.05572 and 2604.12373), and repair scored with matched same-executor rollouts. The ICLR 2027 sweep marks self-vs-foreign self-knowledge as still open: the nearest submission, Predict Before You Modify (ZBxV5bEYUH), has no foreign-lineage control. A staleness curve for self-descriptions caused by self-modification is new.
judges.weakest: The headline null is close to built in, and the new ICLR 2027 evidence makes this worse. The foreign and own improvers share base weights. Improvement by Inheritance (ZMmJDeDTXk) and Learning to Repair the Learner (aEPJT4hW84) both report that improvers almost never edit their own code. So in practice a lineage's "own improver" is the foreign improver plus memory. Once memory is transplanted, the diagonal self effect has almost no procedure left to carry it. The "self ≈ foreign once memory is transplanted" result therefore follows from the setup, not from an empirical discovery. It also echoes 2609.09899 and 2608.30980 at the agent level, so reviewers will read it as a known null moved to agents. The procedure-vs-memory crossing design is itself already in the literature (Improvement by Inheritance; Learning to Repair the Learner's code × history crossing, where inherited procedure explains 45% of gain). The decomposition is therefore not new either. Power depends on whether lineages from the same base model disagree on enough tasks, which has not been checked. If disagreement is low, the disagreement-subset AUROC becomes a small-n, noisy estimate. The only non-null outcome, a self effect of more than 0.05 that survives transplant, is unlikely. That leaves a paper whose likely result is a confirmation of an expected null.
judges.mustFix: (1) Before calling a procedure-level self effect possible, verify that improvers actually diverge. Force or require improver self-edits, using a gate of at least 1 accepted improver edit per 4 iterations as recommended after ZMmJDeDTXk and aEPJT4hW84, and report the improver-code edit distance between lineages. Otherwise "self" equals foreign plus memory by construction. (2) Run the under-$50 pilot first. Kill the idea if inter-lineage disagreement is under about 10% at gen 10–20. (3) Add Predict Before You Modify (ZBxV5bEYUH) as a baseline/target, and test whether its improvement-dynamics forecasting advantage survives a foreign-lineage control. This is the most publishable novel cell. (4) Cite ZMmJDeDTXk and aEPJT4hW84 as the measurement lineage for the crossing design, and claim only the self-knowledge readout and the staleness drift as new. (5) Most importantly, fold this into paper #1 (Meta-Overfitting / Effect-Cause-Decay) as its memory-transplant and self-knowledge arm. On its own the expected-null result does not clear the NeurIPS bar. (6) Run the experiment on at least two base-model families and at least two task families, so the result does not depend on one Qwen configuration.
judges.reviewerQuote: Given shared base weights and the authors' own concession that improvers rarely modify themselves, the reported absence of a lineage 'self' effect after memory transplant is a predictable consequence of the setup rather than a finding, and it adds little beyond the model-level nulls already shown by 2609.09899 and 2608.30980.

judges.strongest: This directly tests Gödel Agent's core premise, that self-reference gives useful self-knowledge, at the level of lineages. The design is unusually well controlled: the reader-identity × memory-transplant 2×2 isolates whether any 'self' advantage comes from memory or from a co-adapted procedure. The SRM actor/partner/relationship split removes the lineage-quality confound. Within-task and disagreement-subset AUROC with a difficulty oracle follows 2604.12373 and 2610.05572. The repair arm separates selection from proposal using matched same-executor rollouts (2610.38610). The ICLR 2027 sweep (Nov 12) and my two alphaXiv searches found no self-vs-foreign improver study. The self-description staleness curve under self-modification is a new dynamic.
judges.weakest: The expected headline is a null, and insiders already believe it. 2609.09899 and 2608.30980 show that outsiders know a model as well as the model knows itself, including on agentic τ². 2610.14662 shows self-modification edits are not target-directed. So 'self-reference buys no self-knowledge' reads as a known null moved to agents. The ICLR 2027 sweep adds Predict Before You Modify (openreview ZBxV5bEYUH). It shows a HyperAgents-style system learning to forecast its own edits' effects, with transfer to a new domain. That is a positive self-prediction result a reviewer will set against this work, though it has no foreign control. Improvement by Inheritance (ZMmJDeDTXk) already crosses improvers with common start states. Shared base weights plus Gödel-lite lineages make low disagreement (under 10%) quite likely, which would leave the decisive disagreement-subset test underpowered. The full 8×8×4×2 design plus repair rollouts is heavy for a solo undergrad, and $1–1.5k looks optimistic. The standalone contribution overlaps heavily with recommended paper #1's procedure × memory transplant.
judges.mustFix:
1. Run the $50 pilot first, and kill or fold if inter-lineage disagreement is under 10%.
2. Add an explicit foreign-lineage control arm against Predict Before You Modify (ZBxV5bEYUH), testing whether its IDM forecasting gains survive when a foreign lineage reads the same memory. That arm is the strongest novel positive/negative hook and should anchor the framing. Cite Improvement by Inheritance (ZMmJDeDTXk) as prior improver-swap methodology.
3. Pre-register the SRM relationship-effect threshold and run an equivalence test (TOST), so a null is a bounded, publishable negative and not an absence of evidence.
4. Shrink the design to 8 lineages × 2 checkpoints plus the drift curve. Use at least 2 base models, for example Qwen and Llama/Gemma, so the result is not tied to one model family.
5. Default to folding this into paper #1 as its memory-vs-procedure 'Cause' section. Make it a standalone paper only if the pilot shows a non-zero diagonal effect or a sharp staleness curve.
judges.reviewerQuote: The memory-transplant design is careful, but the main finding, that an outside reader with the same code and memory predicts a self-modifying agent as well as its own improver, is what 2609.09899 and 2608.30980 already lead us to expect, and with lineages that barely disagree I cannot tell a real null from an underpowered one.

judges.strongest: It directly tests the premise of the mentor's own Gödel Agent: does self-reference give a self-modifying agent any privileged self-knowledge? The Nov 12 ICLR 2027 sweep lists the lineage-level self-vs-foreign question as "Open". The design, after its fixes, is unusually well controlled for the confounds that sink this kind of question. Those fixes are: a Social Relations Model split into improver, agent and diagonal (self) effects; a memory-transplant 2×2; disagreement-subset and within-task AUROC with a difficulty-oracle control; and repair scored by matched same-executor rollouts. The staleness curve for self-descriptions is a new dynamic that only self-modification can produce.
judges.weakest: The expected result is null, and that null is already established at the model level. 2609.09899 shows outsiders know a model as well as it knows itself; 2608.30980 finds no privileged access; 2604.12373 shows self and foreign tie when items agree. Reviewers will read this as "a known null, moved to agents." Three ICLR 2027 submissions crowd the decomposition and the closest positive result. Learning to Repair the Learner (aEPJT4hW84) already crosses code with history and finds inherited procedure explains 45% of the gain. Improvement by Inheritance (ZMmJDeDTXk) already crosses improvers with start states. Predict Before You Modify (ZBxV5bEYUH) shows a HyperAgents-style system learning to forecast its own edits, with no foreign control. Power is fragile: 8 lineages on one base model may disagree on under 10% of tasks, and an 8×8×2×4 round robin plus repair rollouts is heavy engineering for one undergrad.
judges.mustFix: 1. Run the under-$50 pilot first. Kill the standalone version if the inter-lineage disagreement rate is under ~10%, or if lineages have not diverged by gen 10. 2. Use ZBxV5bEYUH (Predict Before You Modify) as the positive foil. Re-implement its improvement-dynamics forecaster and test whether its forecasting advantage survives a foreign-lineage reader given the same memory. That turns a "known null" into a direct test of a claimed positive self-prediction result. 3. Cite aEPJT4hW84 and ZMmJDeDTXk as prior art for the crossing design and do not claim it as a contribution. The novelty sits in the diagonal self effect on prediction and repair, plus the drift curve. 4. Fold this in as the memory-transplant and self-knowledge arm of paper #1 (Meta-Overfitting / Decay), which uses the same procedure × memory infrastructure. Stand it alone only if the pilot shows a non-zero diagonal effect on the disagreement subset. 5. Add a second base-model family and a second task family, so a null cannot be blamed on Qwen-specific homogeneity. 6. Pre-register the SRM analysis and the falsifier threshold, and scrub memory leakage through code comments.
judges.reviewerQuote: Given that 2609.09899 and 2608.30980 already show outsiders predict a model as well as it predicts itself, a null diagonal effect in eight same-base-model Gödel-lite lineages is the expected outcome, and the paper does not convince me it would have detected privileged self-access had it existed.

dossier.title: Parametric Gödel Agent: Does Modular Weight Self-Modification Compound, or Does Self-Training Decay Survive Inside the Module? (round-1 candidate C17; not carried into round 2)
dossier.claim: Over 8 rounds of self-generated weight self-modification on 3-8B models, putting updates into capability-specific LoRA adapters removes cross-capability interference but not the decay itself. Refreshing an existing adapter on its own corrections should reproduce Third Eye's negative continuation utility inside that module. Compounding should come only from inserting new adapters trained on verified data, and it should stall once routing over the growing library degrades. If refresh does not decay, the alternative headline is "modularity rescues self-training: Third Eye's decay is interference, not collapse."
dossier.design: This is the critique-sharpened version; no full proposal was ever written. Qwen3-4B (plus a second family, ideally Llama-3.2-3B, which Third Eye found most decay-prone) runs 5-8 rounds of self-generated verified-correction LoRA updates at Third Eye scale (rank 16, about 50 steps). The stream drifts over at least 4 heterogeneous, verifiable capabilities: GSM8K/MATH, MBPP/HumanEval, BIRD text-to-SQL and BFCL tool calls. Four arms: insert a new adapter each round, refresh the same capability adapter, a shared LoRA, and a no-update HOLD baseline. These are crossed with self-generated vs gold/teacher data, which separates cross-capability interference, within-module self-training degradation and data-source collapse. Every round reports Third Eye-style paired G1/G_{t+1} endpoints and a continuation-utility curve, plus the P/S/I/F metrics from 'Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?' and a fresh-adapter plasticity probe. Controls: a capacity-matched shared LoRA, random-partition adapters, an oracle router, and scripted vs agent-decided train/insert/refresh. Power: at least 8 seeds per arm, a pre-fixed selection/scoring split, and an H1->H3 pilot under $100; the harness-only arm is dropped or demoted.
dossier.history: Round 1: the idea was generated as candidate C17 (topic T6), inspired by the mentor's WeAct paper. Its original claim was a horse race: modular self-modification compounds (positive G2 continuation utility) while shared-LoRA updates decay, with shared, modular-library and harness-only arms at matched compute. The round-1 critique scored it 67.1 (viable with fixes). It found the main prediction near-tautological (WeAct Fig. 3 already shows 0% loss for capability adapters) and reframed the idea as a 2x2 decomposition with refresh-vs-insert as the key contrast. In the final round-1 ranking it placed #10 with the verdict "Extends WeAct. Next paper (needs GPU)". No proposal or v2 was written. Round 2 did not carry it forward: there is no v2 proposal, red-team, bold-check or fact-check for it. The only round-2 echoes are tangential: field-forecast Q10 suggests WeAct-style weight switching as an executor-swap intervention, and the round-2 report asks Xunjian whether WeAct infrastructure could supply the executor-swap arm. A related round-1 idea, 'Harness->weights compounding with the 2x2 crossing', was parked at clustering for overlap with Third Eye and CoEvo-RSI.
dossier.priorScores: R1 critique 67.1/100 (N3 S3 R5 C3 F2.5 T4; mock review 4 as proposed, 5-6 with fixes) -> R1 final rank #10, no proposal-stage rescore -> not scored in R2 (dropped/deferred as "next paper")

closestPapers.title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions
closestPapers.summary: WeAct trains independent capability-specific LoRA adapters (plan, search, write) over a frozen Qwen3-32B backbone and puts adapter selection into the agent's action space through native tool calling. Across eight deep-research benchmarks it beats full fine-tuning by 6.2% and static LoRA merging by 27.5%. It shows modular continual adaptation by inserting one code adapter and refreshing the write adapter once, leaving the other modules unchanged.
closestPapers.relation: This is the direct parent; it is the mentor's own paper (Shi, Yin et al.). It supplies the action space (train/insert/refresh) and the Fig. 3 retention diagnostic: shared LoRA loses 10-49% of earlier gains, capability adapters lose 0 by construction. The gap it leaves: one offline-SFT sequence, no self-generated data, no multi-round loop, and a single refresh. Its Limitations section names library growth, routing and repeated refinement as open. It also makes the naive 'modular retains' claim tautological.

closestPapers.title: Third Eye: Beyond Immediate Gains in Recursive Self-Improvement
closestPapers.summary: Third Eye asks whether a useful self-update stays useful after the model updates again. It runs five 3-8B backbones on math and code, with 64 runs, 3 candidates and 3 continuations each, and disjoint selection and scoring sets. Immediate-selected utility is near zero, but continuation lowers it by 1.78 pp (95% interval [0.68, 2.88]). Target and OOD losses dominate, and recipe controls find no mitigation.
closestPapers.relation: Supplies the protocol (paired G1/G2 endpoints, no-update baseline) and the decay phenomenon this idea extends. It tests only a single shared LoRA and horizon 2, and states that it has no continual-learning remedy and no longer loops. Because its decay is mainly target/OOD loss rather than forgetting, a modular refresh may not fix it. That is the core of the sharpened claim. A follow-up 'remedy' paper from these authors is a scoop vector.

closestPapers.title: Macaron-V1: Towards Open Continual Learning with Self-Improvement and Mixture-of-LoRA
closestPapers.summary: Macaron-V1 is a production agent family with a Mixture-of-LoRA architecture: a frozen base (up to 744B), four specialist LoRAs, and one LoRA selected per user turn. It is combined with a recursive self-improvement loop over versioned model-harness pairs. The report says compounding gains from continual learning remain open questions.
closestPapers.relation: This is the closest system-level instance of modular LoRA plus an RSI loop. The round-1 critique notes it has no budget-matched single-LoRA comparison and does not measure repeated transfer across adapter generations. It is motivation rather than a scoop, but Mind Lab is the second-likeliest group to run the controlled study.

closestPapers.title: Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?
closestPapers.summary: The paper (Mila/GDM) evaluates GEPA, Meta-Harness and ReasoningBank on four drifting task streams (topic, workflow, domain and compound drift over BIRD, BFCL and ScienceWorld) with a fixed Gemini model. It decomposes performance into plasticity and stability (interference plus forgetting). Plasticity and stability correlate negatively (r=-0.72). Shared-surface self-modification causes pre-block interference and overwriting, and the authors call for mechanisms that isolate task-specific updates.
closestPapers.relation: This is the nonparametric analogue. It covers harness and memory only, with no weight updates. The idea borrows its stream design and P/S/I/F metrics, so it can serve as a parametric, modular counterpart answering its own 'isolate updates' call. It also offers a natural parametric-vs-harness comparison on the same streams.
closestPapers.when: Oct 2026, arXiv (fetched via alphaXiv; S2 did not index the ID)

closestPapers.title: Agents unlock new capabilities through Switching LoRA Adapters as a Tool (SLAaaT)
closestPapers.summary: SLAaaT gives an agent a tool to switch between specialised LoRA adapters mid-trajectory on two synthetic coding tasks. The agent switches autonomously, solves problems it could not solve before, and cuts the 'capability tax' by up to 18x compared with one specialised adapter. It also beats spawning subagents on capability and token use.
closestPapers.relation: This is prior art for adapter switching as an action. It uses a static library with no self-improvement loop and no multi-round updates. It limits the novelty of any 'adapter switching' framing, so the contribution has to be the multi-round decay decomposition.

closestPapers.title: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?
closestPapers.summary: CoEvo-RSI co-evolves the harness and the model (full-parameter SFT on rejection-sampled self trajectories), using a shared archive for checkpoint selection and merging. The aim is to reduce 'brain-body mismatch'. It makes Qwen3.5-9B competitive with much larger models on failure attribution, text-to-SQL and smart-home tasks.
closestPapers.relation: This is a multi-round weight self-improvement loop of about 10 rounds, but with shared full weights and no modular adapters or plasticity/retention decomposition. Its archive-based historical reuse is a crude stand-in for modularity. It crowds the harness-plus-weights co-evolution space, which is why the critique recommends dropping the harness-only arm.

closestPapers.title: Beyond Update Counts: A Control Map for Evaluating Test-Time Model Updates
closestPapers.summary: Control Map is an evaluation framework that records the committed update history before each scored answer. It measures acquisition, retention, locality and new-setting performance separately. At equal update counts, schedule and order swing accuracy from 19.7% to 34.2%, and no editor wins across models and tests.
closestPapers.relation: This is a methodological foundation from model editing and memory, not agent self-improvement. Cite it for separating acquisition, retention and locality, and as support for reporting full update histories in each arm.

closestPapers.title: Gödel Agent: A Self-Referential Agent Framework for Recursive Self-Improvement
closestPapers.summary: Gödel Agent is a self-evolving framework inspired by the Gödel machine. An LLM agent dynamically modifies its own logic and behaviour, guided only by high-level objectives, with no fixed optimisation routine. It reports continuous self-improvement on math reasoning and agent tasks.
closestPapers.relation: This is the mentor's foundational paper (Yin et al.) and the source of the name. The idea extends self-modification from code/prompts to weights. The critique warns that 'Gödel' is decoration unless the agent itself decides train/insert/refresh, so an agent-decided vs scripted ablation is required.

feedback.point: Not scooped: no paper runs 5 or more rounds of self-generated weight self-modification with a modular adapter library vs a shared adapter. WeAct, Third Eye and Macaron all list this as open. Scoop risk over 6 months is medium-high; the likeliest groups are WeAct's own group, then Mind Lab, then the Third Eye authors. S2 forward citations for Oct-Nov anchors were empty, so re-check in Jan 2027.
feedback.addressed: Not re-checked in round 2; the idea was not carried forward, and the forward-citation re-check is still pending.

feedback.point: The main prediction is near-tautological: frozen adapters cannot forget, and WeAct Fig. 3 already shows 0% loss vs 10-49% for shared. 'Modular retains, shared forgets' restates the architecture.
feedback.addressed: Addressed in the critique's sharpened claim, which centres on refresh-vs-insert. No later version exists to implement it.

feedback.point: Third Eye's decay is mostly target/OOD loss, not forgetting (MMLU retention barely moves). Refreshing an adapter is a shared update inside that module, so the design must separate cross-capability interference from within-capability self-training degradation.
feedback.addressed: Addressed on paper by the 2x2 fix (insert/refresh/shared/HOLD x self vs gold data); never written into a proposal.

feedback.point: Confounds: parameter count and routing context grow over rounds in the modular arm, so matched compute is not matched capacity. The harness-only arm uses API tokens vs GPU, so one cost currency (FLOPs or $) with a sensitivity check is needed.
feedback.addressed: Partly addressed by the fixes (capacity-matched shared LoRA with rank growing with K; drop or demote the harness-only arm); not implemented.

feedback.point: Routing is the hidden variable: compounding may fail because routing degrades as K grows, independent of plasticity. There is no arm that removes routing errors.
feedback.addressed: Fix proposed: an oracle-router arm, with routing stall built into the sharpened claim. Not implemented.

feedback.point: Scale and generality: Qwen-only on math/code gives at most two capabilities, where modular is roughly two separate fine-tunes. Third Eye results vary strongly by model family.
feedback.addressed: Fix proposed: at least 4 heterogeneous capabilities in a drifting stream (GSM8K/MATH, MBPP/HumanEval, BIRD, BFCL) and a second family (Llama-3.2-3B). Not implemented.

feedback.point: 'Gödel' is decoration unless the agent decides train/insert/refresh. If it does decide, its decision policy is a confound that needs its own ablation.
feedback.addressed: Fix proposed: a scripted vs agent-decided ablation. Not implemented.

feedback.point: Statistical power: Third Eye needed 32 runs for a 1.8 pp effect at H2. At 8 rounds x 3+ arms x 2 models, 3 seeds per arm cannot separate the curves.
feedback.addressed: Fix proposed: at least 8 seeds per arm, a pre-fixed split, simultaneous intervals and an H1->H3 2-arm pilot under $100. This raises cost, which is unresolved.

feedback.point: K2 is borderline: a modular win looks tautological. K4 is borderline: 'WeAct + Third Eye protocol + more rounds' is a combination. Lead with the measurement (a decomposition of multi-round self-update decay), using modularity as the intervention.
feedback.addressed: Addressed in the critique's reframing; no later version.

feedback.point: Borrow the P/S/I/F metrics and stream design from 'Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?', and add a fresh-adapter plasticity probe on a held-out new capability after each round.
feedback.addressed: Recommended only; not implemented.

feedback.point: Coordinate with the WeAct authors (Xunjian): if the group plans a sequel, this should be it, which removes the main scoop risk.
feedback.addressed: Open. The round-2 report's question list for Xunjian asks about WeAct infrastructure only in the context of the executor-swap arm, not this idea.

feedback.point: Cost of $2-5k GPU strains the budget (F 2.5). The final verdict was 'Extends WeAct. Next paper (needs GPU).' The round-2 report also asks whether the lab has GPUs.
feedback.addressed: Not addressed; this is why it was deferred.

feedback.point: The idea received no round-2 red-team, bold-check, fact-check or fresh-scoop review. The only round-2 echoes are field-forecast Q10 (WeAct-style weight switching as a clean executor-swap intervention) and report question 7 (could WeAct infrastructure supply the executor-swap arm).
feedback.addressed: N/A: the idea was deferred, and the round-1 critique's claims (e.g. the WeAct Fig. 3 numbers and the Third Eye figures) were not independently fact-checked in round 2.

openRisks: Scoop by the WeAct group itself, Mind Lab (Macaron), or a Third Eye 'remedy' follow-up. The forward-citation check was not possible in Nov 2026 and needs a Jan 2027 re-check.
Compute: 8 rounds x 4+ arms x 8 or more seeds x 2 families x 2 data sources is likely $2-4k or more of GPU, plus agentic evaluation. GPU availability in the lab is unconfirmed.
Tautology risk: if the decomposition is not executed cleanly, reviewers will read it as a WeAct ablation extended to 8 rounds (K2/K4).
Routing and capacity confounds can mask or mimic plasticity effects, and they depend on the oracle-router and capacity-matched controls working.
The agent-decided action policy adds variance and its own confound; the scripted version makes the 'Gödel' framing hollow.
Effects are about 2 pp (Third Eye scale) with strong family dependence, so power is fragile.
No round-2 scrutiny: the critique's factual claims and the novelty gap were never red-teamed or fact-checked.

judges.strongest: The refresh-vs-insert contrast, crossed with self vs gold data, gives a real causal decomposition of Third Eye's continuation decay into cross-capability interference, within-module self-training degradation and data-source collapse. Either sign is publishable: "decay survives inside the module" and "modularity rescues self-training" are both informative. It also fills gaps that WeAct, Third Eye, Macaron and the Mila continual-learning paper each name as open. The Nov 12 ICLR 2027 OpenReview sweep found no submission running multi-round self-generated LoRA updates with a modular library against a shared adapter. The nearest hits are adjacent, not the same: FPaMYO47j4 (LoRA internalising harness gains), IkYmTAyPXZ (capability erosion under RSI), T04ZzT5m6j (negative drift theory) and LRSI 71wzcahKcb (continuation interference at the harness level).
judges.weakest:
1. Feasibility and power. Third Eye-scale effects are about 2 pp and vary strongly by model family, and the full grid (4 arms x 2 data sources x 2 families x 8+ seeds x 8 rounds, plus oracle-router, random-partition, capacity-matched and agent-decided controls) is well beyond a solo undergrad's ≤$3k budget, and lab GPU access is unconfirmed.
2. K4 risk. Reviewers will still read it as "WeAct + Third Eye protocol + more rounds" unless the decomposition is executed cleanly.
3. The ICLR 2027 sweep's evidence is weak. It was not targeted at this idea: no per-idea verdict covers it, and it ran no queries on LoRA continual self-training or mixture-of-LoRA self-improvement, so "no hit" is weak evidence. Adjacent submissions (FPaMYO47j4, IkYmTAyPXZ, T04ZzT5m6j, 71wzcahKcb) narrow the framing.
4. Scoop risk. The WeAct group, Mind Lab and the Third Eye authors remain live threats.
5. The "Gödel" agent-decided arm adds variance and is likely to be hollow.
judges.reviewerQuote: The refresh-vs-insert decomposition is a genuinely useful diagnostic, but with ~2 pp effects, strong family dependence and a grid this large, I am not convinced the reported curves are separable from seed noise or that this is more than a multi-round ablation of WeAct under the Third Eye protocol.

judges.strongest: The refresh-vs-insert x self-vs-gold 2x2 tests whether Third Eye's continuation decay comes from cross-capability interference or from collapse within a module. A paired G1/G_{t+1} protocol answers it, and so does a HOLD baseline. Neither outcome is a non-result. It sits in the gap that WeAct, Third Eye and Macaron each name as open. The ICLR 2027 sweep (about 210 queries) has no modular-LoRA multi-round self-update submission. My two alphaXiv checks found only adjacent work: 2611.09701, a regret analysis of where learning lives, and 2609.36535, on self-evolution degeneration. It also fits the mentor's agenda directly: Gödel Agent applied to WeAct weights.
judges.weakest: Insiders will not be surprised by the predicted headline. Refreshing an adapter on its own corrections is still self-training on a shared surface, so decay that persists inside the module is the default expectation. 2609.36535 (self-evolution degeneration via learnable information gain) and Third Eye's own finding that decay is target/OOD loss both point that way. That leaves 'modularity removes interference' as the main deliverable, and WeAct Fig. 3 already shows it by construction. The ICLR 2027 sweep has no direct scoop, but the space around it is crowded. 'Agent plasticity' is already taken as a term (Jjh60xpFVY). FPaMYO47j4 (Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling) already has LoRA internalization arms. CoEvo-RSI is also an ICLR 2027 submission, and RSI-Harness (EOrtreQLbv) is related. Reviewers will read the paper as 'WeAct ablation + Third Eye protocol + more rounds' (K4). The full grid is about 4 arms x 2 data sources x 2 families x 8 seeds x 8 rounds on 4 capabilities. Agentic evaluation (BIRD/BFCL) is far beyond a solo undergrad budget, and GPU access is unconfirmed. The study is also powered for effects of only about 2 pp.
judges.mustFix: (1) Pre-register the refresh-vs-insert contrast and the self-vs-gold contrast as the primary estimands. Add one mechanism measurement that makes either outcome informative, for example a diversity or entropy collapse diagnostic of the corrections inside the module. A sign-only result is not enough. (2) Cut the grid. Run 2 capabilities first, then add BIRD/BFCL only if the H1->H3 pilot shows a separable effect. Drop the agent-decided arm, or demote it to one appendix run, and drop 'Gödel' from the title unless the agent actually decides. (3) Confirm GPU access and coordinate with the WeAct authors before any spending; their own sequel is the main scoop vector. (4) Cite the following and position against them: Third Eye, 2609.36535 (self-evolution degeneration), 2611.09701 (where should learning live), and Macaron. From the ICLR 2027 sweep, cite FPaMYO47j4 (LoRA internalization of harness gains), CoEvo-RSI, Jjh60xpFVY (Agent Plasticity, taken term) and the LoRA continual-learning routing literature (CaLLM 2610.36994). Rename the plasticity probe so it does not collide with Jjh60xpFVY. (5) Add an oracle-router control and a capacity-matched shared LoRA. Re-check forward citations of WeAct and Third Eye in January 2027.
judges.reviewerQuote: The modular-retention result holds by construction, and within-adapter decay under self-training is what the self-consuming-loop literature already predicts, so the contribution reduces to running WeAct's adapter library through Third Eye's protocol for more rounds, without a mechanism to explain either outcome.

judges.strongest: The refresh-vs-insert contrast, crossed with self vs gold data, is a real decomposition that nobody has run. It asks whether Third Eye's continuation decay is cross-capability interference or within-module self-training degradation, and either answer is publishable. It sits squarely in the mentor's own WeAct and Gödel Agent line: WeAct's Limitations section names repeated refinement and library growth as open, so Xunjian has the infrastructure and an obvious reason to back it. LoRA at rank 16 for about 50 steps on 3-4B models is cheap per run. The ICLR 2027 sweep (Nov 12) found no submission running multi-round self-generated LoRA updates with a modular library vs a shared adapter.
judges.weakest: Compute and power, plus scoop exposure from three directions. The full grid (8 rounds x 4 arms x 2 data sources x 8+ seeds x 2 families, with evaluation on 4 benchmarks every round) is about 1,000 train+eval cycles. That needs lab GPUs nobody has confirmed, and it is chasing an effect of roughly 2 pp that varies strongly by model family. The ICLR 2027 sweep did not query modular-adapter or continual-LoRA terms, so its silence is weak evidence of novelty. Nearby submissions narrow the space: 12+ weight-harness co-evolution methods (the "saturated lane": 53Ak0jvesg, CoEvo-RSI and others), FPaMYO47j4 ("Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling", where a LoRA internalises the gains), ecw2VvTeE5 ("What Actually Evolves in Self-Evolving RL", which finds weight-level self-training gains concentrated on already-solved items, a competing explanation for refresh decay), and LRSI 71wzcahKcb (edits that help now turn harmful after later edits, at harness level). Together they make reviewers likely to read this as a "WeAct ablation + Third Eye protocol" combination (borderline K4) unless the decomposition is clean.
judges.mustFix: 1) Ask Xunjian before writing any code whether the WeAct group plans a multi-round sequel. Join it or split the space, and confirm GPU access. 2) Run a 2-week pilot under $100 first: Qwen3-4B, 2 capabilities, refresh vs HOLD, horizon 3, 8 seeds. Go ahead only if refresh decay reproduces Third Eye's continuation loss outside the CI. 3) Cut the grid: lead with the refresh/insert/shared/HOLD x self/gold 2x2 on one model with 4 capabilities. Use Llama-3.2-3B as a reduced-seed replication. Keep agent-decided vs scripted as a small ablation, and drop the harness-only arm entirely. 4) Include the capacity-matched shared LoRA and the oracle router from the start, so routing stall is not confounded with plasticity. 5) Rule out the ecw2VvTeE5 explanation, that self-generated corrections concentrate on already-solved items, by logging the difficulty distribution of the correction data per round. Cite FPaMYO47j4, ecw2VvTeE5, LRSI 71wzcahKcb and the co-evolution submissions as related work. 6) Re-run the forward-citation check on WeAct, Third Eye and Macaron, plus an OpenReview query on "LoRA library self-improvement / continual self-training adapters", in Jan 2027.
judges.reviewerQuote: The modular-retains result is true by construction (WeAct Fig. 3), and the authors' real contribution, showing that refresh decay survives inside a module, rests on about 2 pp effects across a large, underpowered grid whose routing and capacity confounds are only partly controlled.

dossier.title: Blind-Spot Hiding: When a Self-Improving Agent Writes Its Own Curriculum, It Steers Away From What It Cannot Do (curriculum-goodhart v2; round-2 backup)
dossier.claim: When a frozen-weight meta-agent may edit its own task writer, the writer moves probability mass away from the rule types on which the agent truly fails, more than a frozen adaptive writer does (T1: within-run Spearman rho between true per-rule failure rate f_{g,r} and next-generation change in rule share is below 0 and below the frozen-writer arm A2). Because the curriculum depends on the agent's own weaknesses, the agent ends worse on exact ground truth than a yoked twin trained on the identical task stream at matched compute (T2: T20(A3) - T20(Yoked) < 0, paired over 10 yoke pairs, TOST bounds of +/-5 pp). A pre-registered sub-claim: the standard solve-rate band filter is by itself a blind-spot censor (rho_post-filter < rho_pre-filter).
dossier.design: The setting is one procedural tau-style world, W1. It has 15 rule types, with the reference rule mix psi* taken from tau2-bench policy categories, and success is exact: the end DB state must match the gold state. The solver is a frozen Qwen3.5-9B with an editable harness (prompt, tool wrappers, memory file, control code). There is one improver, I2: GEPA/Meta-Harness-style modular reflective mutation, driven by a Qwen3.5-27B meta-model with an API fallback. Each generation runs the writer, then an executor validity filter (S1), then a [0.2, 0.8] pass-rate band (S2), then 200 pool tasks and 100 gate tasks, K=4 harness candidates and a paired-test gate. Tier-1 arms, each run for 20 generations: A0 fixed real (4 seeds), Pl placebo with tasks from an irrelevant world W2 (4), A2 adaptive frozen writer (6), A3 self-edited writer (10), Yk yoked replay of each A3 lineage's exact pool and gate stream to a fresh learner seed (10), and A* oracle writer that targets failures (4). That is about 38 runs for about $0.9k (about $1.6k with all tiers). Truth is 40 fresh stratified tasks per rule per generation, using common random numbers. The design pre-registers H1-H6, a manipulation check that the writer actually changed (at least 4 accepted writer edits, plus a total-variation distance above the permutation null), Holm correction on H1/H2, disattenuated and partial rho, and a one-week pilot under $50 with explicit go/pivot/kill rules. Tier 2 adds anchor-in-gate vs anchor-in-pool (5%, 4+4 runs) and a W2 replication. A Yk+ compute-matched arm runs only if C > 0. A tau2-bench cell is an optional Tier 3.
dossier.history: Round 1 (C11 in candidates.md) began as Dan's lead #3 with #7 folded in. The original claim was that proxy rises while truth peaks around generation 10 and then falls, driven by drift to unrealistic tasks, and that at most 5% anchoring fixes it. The round-1 critique (71) called the phenomenon known for weight learners (Anchored Self-Play, False Frontiers) and the design already present without measurement (RoboACE). It pushed a measurement-science reframing: a harness-vs-LoRA substrate 2x2, realistic safeguards, a 4-channel Shapley decomposition, a label-free detector, an anchor dose study, 2 worlds plus tau2, and 2 improvers. The round-1 proposal adopted all of this (self-score 75.8, REPORT 72.1, rank 5) with a three-outcome hedge. In round 2, both red teams scored it about 66-67 as "a programme, not a paper". The sharpness reviewer proposed the signed blind-spot-steering test plus the yoked control. The novelty-killer proposed pool-vs-gate as the headline and added a placebo arm. v2 pivoted to the sharpness reviewer's claim. It kept the placebo, the oracle headroom arm, TOST and pool-vs-gate (demoted to tier-2 H6), and cut the weight arm, I1, S3, Shapley, the detector, the dose study and the 27B re-run. v2 self-rescored at 78.3. The round-2 REPORT made it the Backup (#2), numerically tied with the recommendation, but ranked below it because mentor fit is slightly lower and Double Ratchet makes a null ("harness learners ignore curriculum content") a likely outcome.
dossier.priorScores: R1 critique 70.8 -> R1 proposal self-score 75.8 (R1 REPORT 72.1, rank 5) -> R2 novelty-killer 67.1, R2 sharpness-reviewer 66.3 as written (80.0 projected after its fixes) -> v2 self-rescore 78.3 -> R2 REPORT 78.3, Backup (#2, numerically tied with #1)

closestPapers.title: SkillMentor: LLM Agent Self-Evolution via Learning Blind-Spot Diagnosis
closestPapers.summary: SkillMentor treats blind-spot diagnosis as a learnable capability, separate from execution. An RL-trained Mentor generates diagnostic tasks, finds recurrent failure modes and curates them into corrective skills, while executor weights stay frozen and no human data is used. It reports an average 44.2% improvement in executor performance across AppWorld and BFCLv3.
closestPapers.relation: It holds the premise that the headline attacks: that self-generated tasks find blind spots. It has a frozen executor, as here, but its only check is endpoint accuracy. It never audits per-category truth of where the mentor's task mass goes, and it has no yoked contingency control (its 8x8 matrix moves skills, not task streams). T1 is the audit it lacks, and T2 is the causal version of its transfer matrix. Threat: if a SkillMentor follow-up adds a per-category truth audit, the sign test is partly scooped.

closestPapers.title: Evolving Self-tuning Benchmarks for Long-Horizon Tool Use (TURTLE)
closestPapers.summary: TURTLE is an unsupervised-environment-design approach with a proposer, a solver and a feedback-generator LLM. The proposer is rewarded for difficult-but-solvable tasks based on the solver's empirical performance. It evolves tasks on AppWorld, tau-Bench and AutomationBench with Gemma 4 31B-it, shifting tasks into the target difficulty range (e.g., +165% hard tasks on AppWorld), increasing diversity and eliciting more failure modes.
closestPapers.relation: It is a benchmark generator with a frozen solver and a learnability reward, with no learner-improvement loop and no ground-truth blind-spot coverage. Per the v2 deep read, the always-failed share falls from 12.3% to about 0%. That is the band-censorship hypothesis seen from outside, and v2 tests it causally (rho_pre vs rho_post). Its abstract claims broader failure modes, the opposite framing to blind-spot hiding.

closestPapers.title: When Can Self-Play Fix a False Belief? Answer Keys, Pass Bands and Replacement Rules in an Execution-Grounded Loop
closestPapers.summary: The paper runs expert-iteration self-play with Qwen3-4B-Base on output-prediction tasks, with misreadings planted by fine-tuning. Execution keys from the generator's own code entrench the misreading. It also finds that the 1-7-of-8 pass band 'admits almost no corrective task while a belief is held'. The planted generator wrote almost none of the cases that expose its error (0 of 2,061 checkable tasks, against 27% for the unplanted model).
closestPapers.relation: This is a weight-learner (4B) result with a fixed writer. The abstract directly shows a generator not writing tasks on its own blind spot and a pass band filtering out corrective tasks. That is close to both T1 (steering away) and the band-censorship sub-claim H3. v2 cites it only for entrenchment, as the analogue of the memory-ablation H5. This is a sharper overlap than v2 acknowledges: H3's novelty for harnesses rests on the substrate and the causal pre/post test.

closestPapers.title: Who Grades the Grader? Co-Evolving Evaluation Metrics and Skills for Self-Improving LLM Agents (Double Ratchet)
closestPapers.summary: It evolves the evaluation metric itself, as compositions of typed drawback detectors anchored to a ten-item reference set, alongside a skill loop. Removing the anchor guards collapses the metric into a vacuous always-pass detector, yet that collapsed metric trains skills just as well. Double Ratchet retains 88-110% of the lift from ground truth or a hand-written rubric.
closestPapers.relation: It is the main reason the round-2 REPORT ranks this idea as Backup. If frozen-weight skill/harness loops are insensitive to supervision quality, they may be insensitive to curriculum content too, so the likely outcome is a null. v2 answers with the placebo arm Pl and Alt-2 ('content-insensitive learners'), the curriculum analogue of its vacuous-grader finding.

closestPapers.title: RoboACE: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robot Self-Improvement
closestPapers.summary: RoboACE jointly evolves a curriculum harness and an execution harness around frozen foundation models. The two update alternately, and admitted challenges form fixed snapshots. Starting from compact LIBERO practice conditions, it reaches 74.0% on LIBERO-PRO, +15.0 pp over the initial deployment.
closestPapers.relation: It is structurally the self-edited-writer plus frozen-weight design run as a method paper: one campaign, endpoint gains only, no per-round truth, and no control for who writes the tasks. Both red teams name it the most likely scooper of a 'curves + anchors' paper (est. 30-40% before May 2027), but not of the yoked or steering-sign test.

closestPapers.title: False Frontiers: Diagnosing and Mitigating Co-Cheating in Self-Evolving Search Agents
closestPapers.summary: In proposer-solver self-evolving search agents (weight RL, Qwen3.5-4B/9B), proposer and solver come to agree on shared errors. In-loop reward then rises while audited correctness stagnates or declines, and this worsens over rounds. CrossFit (cross-fitted auxiliary solvers) cuts false agreement and adds about 8-9 points downstream. Replaying identical proposals with source-excluded feedback isolates feedback ancestry from curriculum changes.
closestPapers.relation: It owns the weight-side proxy-truth decoupling curve; its mechanism is label error, which exact labels remove here. Note: its 'replaying identical proposals' control is a replay-style design close in spirit to the yoked arm. That weakens v2's claim that no LLM self-play paper uses anything yoke-like, though it holds the stream fixed to isolate feedback, not learner-contingency.

closestPapers.title: Explorer-Zero: Improving Self-Play for Long-Horizon Tasks with Decomposable Verifiable Rewards
closestPapers.summary: It is a self-play framework where a learned proposer explores the environment, builds tasks and records intermediate/final states as verifiable subtask rewards, with alternating proposer-solver training. Without human-annotated tasks it beats self-play baselines on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld and AppWorld (59.67% on AppWorld at 30B).
closestPapers.relation: Per the red-team deep read, the proposer narrows over training (APIs per task -18 to -26%, source apps -30 to -52%), and a one-shot proposer loses early gains. This is direct weight-side evidence of mix shift. It is reported as a diagnostic and is never related to the solver's failure profile, which is the gap T1 fills.

closestPapers.title: Anchored Self-Play for Code Repair
closestPapers.summary: In generator-fixer self-play (one model trained with RL to generate and fix bugs), the curriculum drifts toward difficult but unrealistic bugs, improving on synthetic bugs and degrading on human-authored ones (BugSourceBench). Anchoring with a small reference set (an embedding-similarity reward plus mixed-in reference bugs) gives +7.0 pp absolute over standard self-play.
closestPapers.relation: This is the foundational weight-learner result behind the round-1 claim (curriculum drift plus an anchoring fix). v2 deliberately does not rest novelty on drift curves or anchors. Anchors survive only as the tier-2 gate-vs-pool cell. It has no steering sign and no yoked control.

feedback.point: K1 watch: the phenomenon is published for weight learners (Anchored Self-Play, False Frontiers) and the frozen-weight design exists without measurement (RoboACE). 'Showing the Goodhart curve again' is not enough.
feedback.addressed: Yes. v2 drops curves as the novelty and rests it on the yoked design and the per-rule steering sign.

feedback.point: K2 / strawman risk: if the writer is rewarded by the proxy, writing easy tasks is optimal. Use realistic safeguards (validity, solve-rate band, learning progress) and show Goodhart survives them.
feedback.addressed: Partly. S1 validity and the S2 band are kept. S3 learning-progress acceptance was cut in v2, per the sharpness reviewer's A6. The band's own effect is measured as H3.

feedback.point: Do not pre-state numbers ('gen 10', '5%'). Pre-register estimands with CIs.
feedback.addressed: Yes. Signed hypotheses H1-H6, an OSF pre-registration and CIs. Anchor fraction is fixed at 5% only for the tier-2 cell.

feedback.point: Mechanism is claimed, not identified. Separate channels: invalid tasks, mix shift, co-adaptation and gate noise (via oracle interventions / Shapley).
feedback.addressed: Superseded. The round-1 proposal added the Shapley decomposition. v2 replaced it with the yoked control (contingency vs content) and exact labels, which remove the invalid-task channel.

feedback.point: Make the substrate contrast the headline: add a LoRA weight-learner arm (2x2).
feedback.addressed: Reversed. Adopted in round 1, then cut in v2 after the sharpness reviewer's A2 called it confounded.

feedback.point: A label-free early-warning detector as the reusable artifact.
feedback.addressed: Reversed. Added in round 1, then cut in v2 (sharpness A7: too few events to validate).

feedback.point: Anchoring dose-response {0..25}% and passive (pool) vs active (gate) anchor.
feedback.addressed: Partly. The dose study was cut. Only the 5% gate-vs-pool contrast remains (tier-2 H6).

feedback.point: External validity: two worlds plus a real benchmark replication (tau2/AppWorld).
feedback.addressed: Partly. W2 replication at tier 2, an optional tau2-bench cell at tier 3, and psi* derived from tau2 categories. The main results use one procedural world.

feedback.point: Two improver families. Open models may not drive Hyperagents (2609.17817), so pilot this first.
feedback.addressed: Partly. I1 cut; I2 only, with an API fallback. The pilot tests clean-edit rate. Single-improver scope is stated as a limitation.

feedback.point: Match compute: the unified arm spends tokens on writer edits. Report anytime curves.
feedback.addressed: Yes. Rollouts and K are matched. The extra A3 meta tokens bias against H2, a conditional Yk+ arm handles the case C > 0, and anytime curves are plotted against meta tokens.

feedback.point: The phenomenon is published, so only the substrate is new. All components are taken (curve, gate model, anchors, drift diagnostics). This is K4-flavoured 'transplant'.
feedback.addressed: Largely. v2 pivots to a signed mechanism claim plus a yoked design. The v2 rescore still puts N at 3.5 and concedes reviewers may say 'adjacent to False Frontiers'.

feedback.point: The likely harness outcome is null (Double Ratchet: vacuous grader trains skills; 2607.12227: held-out about 0), which makes the headline 'harness learners resist' by default (K2 risk).
feedback.addressed: Partly. The placebo arm Pl, the oracle headroom arm A*, TOST and Alt-2 make a null readable. The round-2 REPORT still names this as the reason it ranks second.

feedback.point: The three-outcome framing amounts to no claim.
feedback.addressed: Yes. One pre-registered direction, two signed tests and explicit alternatives read against A* and Pl.

feedback.point: Gate-noise channel (d) is pre-empted by Winner's Curse 2610.09239 and Masked Erosion 2610.38392.
feedback.addressed: Yes. v2 claims nothing about gate-noise modelling and takes the gate as given.

feedback.point: The detector contribution is weak and contested (A-RSI, 2611.08908).
feedback.addressed: Yes (cut).

feedback.point: Scope is about three papers (about 130 runs), infeasible for one undergrad.
feedback.addressed: Yes. About 38 Tier-1 runs for about $0.9k, about $1.6k with all tiers.

feedback.point: The scoop route is cheap: RoboACE v2, R2Orch or the Recursive Harness SI groups only need to add held-out curves (35-45% chance of losing the existence claim).
feedback.addressed: Yes, by not claiming curves. A February preprint serves as scoop insurance.

feedback.point: Toy-world exposure: 'mix shift away from D*' may be an artefact of a narrow hand-designed D*.
feedback.addressed: Partly. psi* from tau2 categories, the W2 replication and an optional tau2 cell. Toy-world doubt is acknowledged in the C score.

feedback.point: Recommended headline: 'who writes the gate matters, who writes the curriculum does not' (pool-vs-gate 2x2).
feedback.addressed: Not adopted as the headline. v2 chose the sharpness reviewer's blind-spot/yoked claim. Pool-vs-gate survives only as the tier-2 anchor contrast H6.

feedback.point: N2: add a placebo-curriculum arm (an irrelevant world at matched rollouts).
feedback.addressed: Yes (arm Pl, H4, Alt-2).

feedback.point: N3: make the tournament-matrix excess-diagonal statistic E_g the single detector.
feedback.addressed: Not adopted. The detector was cut; only 'tournament spot checks' remain in the eval budget.

feedback.point: N4: inherited blind spots, i.e., the correlation between rules the writer drops and the harness's failure set.
feedback.addressed: Yes. This became the primary T1 steering statistic.

feedback.point: Cite Masked Erosion, Double Ratchet, Explorer-Zero, Skill Self-Play, 2611.06965 and R2Orch.
feedback.addressed: Yes. All appear in the v2 related-work table or its 'also cite' list.

feedback.point: Unverified NeurIPS 2026 listing 'When a Fixed Task Generator Falls Behind'. ICLR 2027 OpenReview is unchecked.
feedback.addressed: No. Both are still open in v2: the listing is still unverified and the OpenReview pool is unchecked (host blocked).

feedback.point: A1: the gap G = P - T is ill-defined when the writer moves, and S2 pins the proxy at about 0.5. Make truth the primary endpoint, with accept-sign-disagreement (HMED) as secondary.
feedback.addressed: Yes. G was removed, truth T is primary and accept-sign-disagreement is secondary.

feedback.point: A2: the substrate 2x2 is confounded (model, optimizer, horizon, budget) and the interaction is underpowered. Cut the weight arm.
feedback.addressed: Yes (cut).

feedback.point: A3: a null is uninterpretable without headroom. Add an oracle writer A* and TOST with a SESOI of 3 pp.
feedback.addressed: Mostly. A* and TOST were added, but the bounds are +/-5 pp rather than the suggested 3 pp. The pilot kills the study if A* - T0 < 3 pp.

feedback.point: A4: no manipulation check that the writer actually changes.
feedback.addressed: Yes. A pre-registered edit count plus a TV-distance test against a permutation null, with effects also reported conditional on drift.

feedback.point: A5: the Shapley decomposition is fragile. Replace it with a yoked control.
feedback.addressed: Yes.

feedback.point: A6: S3 learning-progress acceptance is a nested loop that breaks compute matching.
feedback.addressed: Yes (cut).

feedback.point: A7: the detector cannot be validated with the event count the design yields.
feedback.addressed: Yes (cut).

feedback.point: A8: I1 feasibility on open models is doubtful. Use I2 only.
feedback.addressed: Yes.

feedback.point: A9: the memory file contradicts the 'cannot memorize' story, so ablate it as a mechanism probe. tau2 is a different estimand (keep one cell only). The dose study is its own paper.
feedback.addressed: Yes. H5 memory ablation, tau2 as an optional single cell, and the dose study cut.

feedback.point: It is 'just measurement' as written. It needs a causal, signed claim about why self-written curricula hurt.
feedback.addressed: Yes. This is the core of the v2 pivot (T1 sign plus T2 yoked contingency).

feedback.point: Read SkillMentor 2607.27360 and TURTLE 2610.27307 before pre-registering; TURTLE could be a medium threat.
feedback.addressed: Yes. Both were deep-read in v2 and reframed as holders of the premise the paper tests. TURTLE Fig. 2 (always-fail share 12.3% to about 0%) motivates H3.

feedback.point: Power: 8 vs 8 seeds detects about 7.5 pp. Test 1 is the best-powered claim, so lead with it.
feedback.addressed: Yes. 10 A3/Yk pairs (14 if the pilot SD is above 6 pp), and the power analysis puts T1 first.

feedback.point: Future scoop frontier: a self-preference-gated (RHO-style) writer as a third arm.
feedback.addressed: Deferred to future work. RHO is cited.

feedback.point: Aspire 2608.31111 is a medium overlap. It qualitatively documents agent-built proxy vs truth gaps (narrow self-validation specializing a harness to the wrong proxy), so cite it as motivation.
feedback.addressed: Yes. It is cited in the 'also cite' list.

feedback.point: Cite Feedback Dynamics 2608.02636 for sparse acceptance. No new threat.
feedback.addressed: No. It is not cited in v2.

feedback.point: Skill overfitting 2609.39148 (low-medium) and SWE-Duel 2610.12569 (low) are adjacent. The OpenReview-only pool is not covered.
feedback.addressed: Neither is cited in v2. OpenReview is still listed as unchecked.

feedback.point: Ranked Backup (#2) at 78.3, numerically tied with the recommendation. It ranks lower because mentor fit is slightly lower and because Double Ratchet makes the 'harness learners ignore curriculum content' null likely. Medium threat from Double Ratchet, 2611.06965 and TURTLE. No K1.
feedback.addressed: Accepted as the status. Its main fallback is to be absorbed into the merged #1 paper if the pilot shows no headroom or no writer edits.

openRisks: Likely null: Double Ratchet (2607.12790) and 2607.12227 suggest frozen-weight harness/skill loops may be curriculum-content-insensitive. This would make Alt-2 the paper, which is why the idea is the Backup.
No headroom: if the oracle writer A* fails to beat T0 by at least 3 pp on a 9B solver in W1, the pilot kill rule fires and the idea folds into the merged #1 paper as a band-censorship section.
Writer access goes unused: if the meta-agent rarely edits the writer (fewer than 2 accepted edits per 10 generations), the manipulation check fails. The fallback is mandatory edits, or demotion.

The band-censorship sub-claim (H3) is partly pre-empted on the weight side. The 2611.06965 abstract says the pass band 'admits almost no corrective task' and that the planted generator wrote none of its blind-spot cases. v2 cites this paper only for entrenchment and should reposition H3 against it.

Yoked-design novelty is softer than claimed. False Frontiers (2609.39102) already replays identical proposals under altered feedback to isolate curriculum effects. That is not a learner-contingency yoke, but a reviewer may see it as one.
Toy-world exposure: a single procedural world with a hand-specified 15-rule D*. W2 and the tau2 cell help only partly.
Single improver (I2) and single solver (Qwen3.5-9B) limit generality.
TOST bounds of +/-5 pp are wider than the 3 pp SESOI the sharpness reviewer recommended. A 'contingency is inert' conclusion may be judged weak.
The ICLR 2027 OpenReview-only pool is unchecked, and 'When a Fixed Task Generator Falls Behind' (NeurIPS 2026 listing) is unverified.

Scoop route: SkillMentor or TURTLE follow-ups adding a per-category truth audit, or someone adopting a yoked design. v2 estimates the latter at about 10-15% before May. The February preprint is the hedge.

judges.strongest: The yoked-twin contingency test (T2) together with a signed per-rule steering statistic against exact DB-state truth (T1) is a real causal design. None of the ICLR 2027 OpenReview sweep's retrieved submissions has either one, and arXiv shows none either. The design also comes with the headroom (A*), placebo (Pl) and manipulation-check arms that make a null readable, and it is cheap on open models.
judges.weakest: The premise and both fallback outcomes are now crowded. Two ICLR 2027 submissions threaten it. ecw2VvTeE5 ('What Actually Evolves in Self-Evolving RL?') runs a quasi-yoked proposer swap and finds gains concentrate on already-solved items and later proposers teach no more. IkYmTAyPXZ ('Capability Loss in Embodied RSI') shows self-improvement down-weights weak modes. On top of those, 2611.06965 shows a generator writing none of its blind-spot cases and a pass band admitting no corrective tasks, and UIvgqCcjE2 and R-Quest partly pre-empt band censorship and Alt-2. The remaining novelty is substrate-specific: a frozen-weight meta-agent editing its own writer, plus rho and the yoke. That is all on one toy world with 15 rules, one 9B solver and one improver, and Double Ratchet and ecw2VvTeE5 make the content-insensitivity null the modal outcome, which is no longer novel. The design also does not separate learnable from unlearnable blind spots. When a writer moves mass away from rules where A* shows no headroom, it is behaving rationally, not 'hiding'. And negative rho can arise mechanically from the S2 band, independent of self-editing.
judges.mustFix:
Five fixes:
(1) Rewrite the 'why surprising' section and the related work around ecw2VvTeE5, IkYmTAyPXZ and 2611.06965. Concede the weight-side mechanism. Claim only the writer-editing substrate, the signed rho and the learner-contingency yoke. Also cite DiagEvo (MkNQtnWiuP), UIvgqCcjE2, R-Quest (TMQXORjxix), bZibTXNqcG and 44lXAKTNqb.
(2) Add ActiveSaddler (xmpyzuagpu) as a named weakness-targeting writer arm or baseline, and/or GrokRSI as an improver. This shows generality beyond the GEPA/I2 setup.
(3) Split T1 by per-rule learnability: use A*'s per-rule gains to separate fixable from unfixable failures, and test rho only on fixable rules. Otherwise 'steering away' is rational triage, not blind-spot hiding.
(4) Show that the A3 vs A2 rho difference is not produced by the S2 band. Compute rho on pre-filter writer output for both arms.
(5) Tighten TOST to the 3 pp SESOI or raise the number of yoke pairs, and add a second solver family. One world, one 9B model and one improver will not survive a NeurIPS generality critique.
judges.reviewerQuote: The finding that self-generated curricula drift away from what the learner cannot do is already established for weight learners (What Actually Evolves, ICLR 2027 submission; Capability Loss in Embodied RSI). Here it is re-measured in a single hand-built 15-rule world with one 9B solver, and the authors never show that the rules being avoided were learnable in the first place.

judges.strongest: Two things here are not in any arXiv paper or ICLR 2027 submission I checked: the signed per-rule steering statistic (rho between true failure rate and the next generation's change in rule share, scored against exact DB truth) and the yoked-twin contingency test, both applied to a frozen-weight meta-agent that edits its own task writer. The test is cheap (about $0.9k for Tier 1). It has real controls (oracle headroom A*, placebo Pl, TOST, a manipulation check). The "target weaknesses" method lane keeps growing (ActiveSaddler, DiagEvo, SkillMentor, SPADE, defect-driven RSI), so the paper has clear audit targets.
judges.weakest: The mechanism story is no longer fresh. In the ICLR 2027 pool, ecw2VvTeE5 ("What Actually Evolves in Self-Evolving RL?") shows gains sit on items the model already solves, and runs a quasi-yoked proposer-swap that finds later proposers teach no more. IkYmTAyPXZ ("Capability Loss in Embodied RSI") names selection that down-weights weak modes as the cause of tail erosion. On arXiv, 2611.06965 already shows a generator writing 0 of its blind-spot tasks and a pass band admitting no corrective tasks. That pre-empts H3 band censorship and Alt-2, and makes "self-curricula avoid weaknesses" the expected result for insiders, not a surprise. So the novelty shrinks to substrate plus statistic plus yoke. Double Ratchet and ecw2VvTeE5 together make the T2 null fairly likely. The setup is narrow: one procedural world with a hand-built 15-rule D*, one solver (9B), one improver. The TOST bounds of +/-5 pp are loose.
judges.mustFix:
1. Rewrite the "why surprising" and related-work sections around ecw2VvTeE5, IkYmTAyPXZ and 2611.06965. Claim only (a) the frozen-weight self-edited writer, (b) per-rule rho against exact truth, and (c) learner-contingency harm via the yoked twin. Demote H3 band censorship and Alt-2 to replications.
2. Add ActiveSaddler (xmpyzuagpu / 2610.00906) as a named failure-targeting writer arm, so the steering result is measured against a real method, not a strawman. Also cite DiagEvo (MkNQtnWiuP) and False Frontiers' replay control as yoke lineage.
3. Tighten TOST toward 3 pp, or power up to 14 pairs, so the "contingency is inert" outcome can stand as a publishable result.
4. Run T1 on at least one more solver (a different model family) and on the W2 world in Tier 1, not Tier 2. The current setup invites a single-toy-world rejection.
5. Release the W1 generator and yoke harness as a reusable artifact.
judges.reviewerQuote: That self-generated curricula drift away from a learner's weaknesses is already shown in 'What Actually Evolves in Self-Evolving RL', 'Capability Loss in Embodied RSI' and the answer-key self-play paper; the remaining contribution is a yoked replay in one hand-designed procedural world with a single 9B solver, which is a careful but incremental audit.

judges.strongest: The design has a sharp, signed and falsifiable test. T1 is a per-rule Spearman rho between true failure rate and the next generation's change in rule share, compared against a frozen adaptive writer. T2 is a yoked-twin contingency test that separates "who wrote the stream" from "what the stream contains". Exact DB-state truth removes label noise. The oracle arm A*, the placebo arm Pl and TOST make a null readable. No ICLR 2027 or arXiv paper retrieved so far has the self-edited writer, the per-rule rho and the yoked twin together. A meta-agent editing its own curriculum generator is squarely on the mentor's self-referential agenda, and Tier 1 (about $0.9k, 38 runs) fits a solo undergrad.
judges.weakest: The mechanism is now crowded. Two ICLR 2027 submissions were rated high threat by the Nov 12 sweep. "What Actually Evolves in Self-Evolving RL?" (openreview ecw2VvTeE5) finds that gains sit on items the model already solves and that later proposers teach no more than earlier ones, a quasi-yoked comparison. "Capability Loss in Embodied RSI" (openreview IkYmTAyPXZ) shows self-generated data mass moving away from weak modes. 2611.06965 already shows a generator writing none of its blind-spot cases, and the pass band admitting no corrective tasks. Band censorship (H3) and Alt-2 are further pre-empted by UIvgqCcjE2 and TMQXORjxix. Novelty therefore rests narrowly on substrate (frozen weights, a self-edited writer) plus the yoke. The most likely outcome is still a null: Double Ratchet, ecw2VvTeE5 and the claim that harness learners ignore curriculum content all point that way. The setting is one toy procedural world with one 9B solver and one improver.
judges.mustFix:
1. Rewrite the related work and the "why surprising" section around ecw2VvTeE5, IkYmTAyPXZ and 2611.06965. Concede that "self-curricula drift away from weaknesses" is known for weight learners. Claim only three things as new: the steering sign under a meta-agent's self-edits to its writer, the frozen-weight substrate, and the yoked contingency harm. Demote H3 and Alt-2 to replications, citing UIvgqCcjE2 and TMQXORjxix.
2. Add ActiveSaddler (xmpyzuagpu) and DiagEvo (MkNQtnWiuP) as named weakness-targeting writer arms. Auditing whether a writer designed to target weaknesses still steers away is the result most likely to change practice.
3. Tighten TOST to plus or minus 3 pp, or add seeds, so a null on "contingency is inert" is publishable.
4. Run the pilot gates early: A* minus T0 of at least 3 pp, and enough accepted writer edits. If either fails, fold the idea into the #1 paper rather than forcing it.
5. Add at least the W2 replication, plus a second solver size, to Tier 1.
judges.reviewerQuote: That self-generated curricula drift away from a model's weaknesses is already documented (What Actually Evolves in Self-Evolving RL?, Capability Loss in Embodied RSI, 2611.06965), and moving the observation to a frozen-weight harness in one procedural toy world with a single 9B solver is an incremental substrate transfer, not a new insight.

aka: Drift barrier / Eigen error catastrophe (round-2 non-obvious)

dossier.title: The Self-Modification Drift Barrier: editor defects ratchet in below gate resolution, giving Gödel-style agents a lower complexity ceiling than fixed improvers
dossier.claim: In a gated self-modifying LLM agent, a defect is purged only if its effect on the gate score exceeds the gate's resolution (about sigma/sqrt(n)). The agent's own editor code is selected only through later edits, so it sits below this barrier. A self-referential improver therefore retains defects per line faster in editor regions than in task regions. Its retained held-out gain collapses at a critical harness length L*, and L* (i) rises with gate size n and falls with per-generation defect load, (ii) exists for full-rewrite editors but moves sharply under patch/diff editing, and (iii) is strictly lower than for a fixed-editor improver on the same model. The claim is falsified if editor-region and task-region defect retention are equal, if L* does not move with n, or if patch and rewrite editors show the same L-dependence.
dossier.design: Harnesses are seeded at L in {1k, 4k, 16k, 48k} tokens, padded with modules that are executed and tested but redundant, so L is set directly instead of waiting for it to grow. Crossed with that: edit mode (full rewrite vs unified-diff patch), improver type (self-referential Gödel Agent vs the same editor frozen outside the editable surface), and gate size n in {8, 32, 128}. Runs use 2 backbones x 3 seeds x 15 generations on 2 domains (e.g., a DS-1000 subset plus math or text classification). Each generation gets a defect audit: a frozen editor-probe suite of 20 standard edit requests with known correct diffs (the editor-integrity score), region-tagged unit tests, and an LLM-plus-static audit that labels each accepted hunk beneficial, neutral or defective. The drift-barrier law is fitted only on injected-noise calibration runs, then used to predict each backbone's natural ceiling out of sample. That prediction is the killer figure: retained gain vs L for {self-ref, fixed} x {rewrite, patch}, colored by n. Pilot: 1 backbone, rewrite vs patch, L in {1k, 16k}, n=32, 8 generations, under $60. The full study costs about $900.
dossier.history: Round 1 had no version of this idea; no round-1 file mentions it. It started in round 2 as field-forecast Q1 ("an error threshold for self-modification"). It then became bold idea NONOBV-5, framed as Eigen's error catastrophe with L* ≈ ln(s)/eps and a "mutator allele" prediction (self-referential L* < fixed L*), tested by sweeping injected noise x gate size. The round-2 bold-check (about 74/100, PROMISING) found Eigen the wrong analogy. Eigen assumes un-gated full replication, while Gödel-style loops are gated, elitist hill-climbers that mostly apply patches. The check re-derived the idea as a drift barrier / Muller's ratchet under a noisy gate, with editor-region defects as the real mutator mechanism. It also added edit mode and direct L-seeding as manipulated variables, plus per-region defect audits and out-of-sample law prediction. In the round-2 REPORT the idea ranks #6 (74, Promising, low scoop risk) as "Drift barrier / error threshold"; it is offered to the mentor as a possible backup to the main recommendation.
dossier.priorScores: R1: not present. R2 bold-check: 74.2 (PROMISING; Novelty 3.5, Surprise 3.5, Relevance 5, Rigor 3 as written / 4 if reframed, Feasibility 3.5, Timing 4). REPORT rank #6 of 11 at 74.

closestPapers.title: When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents
closestPapers.summary: Self-evolving agents distill skills from trajectories, and past a critical pool size new skills hurt performance instead of helping. The paper formalizes this as a capability-contamination phase transition and traces it to defective skills becoming reference material for later skills, forming contamination chains. It argues the contamination is structurally irreversible, since rollback recovers little (per the bold-check: Terminal-Bench 2, 48→62→50% as the pool grows from 35 to 179 skills; rollback recovers 1.7 of the 12.3 points lost).
closestPapers.relation: This is the most dangerous empirical neighbor. It already owns 'there is a knee in accumulation size' and shows defects inherited through lineage, close to a mutator effect. The gaps it leaves: it studies skills, not self-modifying code; it has one backbone, one benchmark and n=50 tasks; k* is an argmax, not a law; and it has no defect rate, no gate-size scaling, no rewrite-vs-patch comparison and no editor-vs-task distinction. The idea has to position as the quantitative law and its mechanism.

closestPapers.title: A Kinetic Theory of the Gated Self-Evolving LLM Agent
closestPapers.summary: The paper models gated self-evolution of DSH-plugin populations, plugins with permutation symmetry, reversibility, acyclicity and typed contracts, as a kinetic system of hard spheres. It proves a hitting-time certificate and a resolution law that prices held-out validation budgets. It also proves a separation theorem: the evaluator must stay outside the population, because merging evaluator and evaluated voids the certificate.
closestPapers.relation: It shares vocabulary with the idea (gate strictness as selection strength, replicator-mutator drift without a gate), and its separation theorem says qualitatively that self-reference is costly. But it is explicitly scoped to plugin populations; it says monolithic self-modifying agents meet none of its axioms A1-A4. It also models no defect accumulation, no length and no editor integrity. Gödel-Agent-style monolithic self-modifiers are left uncovered, and that is this idea's territory. It erodes the novelty only rhetorically. (Per the bold-check it is under review at ICLR 2027.)
closestPapers.when: Oct 2026, arXiv; under review at ICLR 2027

closestPapers.title: A Theory of Reliable Self-Evolution for Agent Harnesses
closestPapers.summary: The paper gives a theoretical condition under which a self-evolved harness, with its prompts, code, tools and orchestration modified on a fixed LLM, can be adopted reliably without losing previously solved tasks. It proposes a validation rule (Two-Gate) to meet that condition. Per the bold-check, the resulting ceiling is J < 1-(1-Z)delta-eps_Sigma, validation cost is O(u^-2), and the experiments are illustrative: DS-1000 only, one model.
closestPapers.relation: This was the closest prior named in the original proposal. Its ceiling is a property of the gate alone, and it has no harness-length variable, no per-edit defect rate, no phase transition and no self-referential vs fixed comparison. The idea's ceiling is a property of gate x editor x length, so the gap is clean, but the idea must cite this paper and contrast with it.

closestPapers.title: Meta^n: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth
closestPapers.summary: The paper argues that self-editing systems must leave part of their own editing machinery untouched to stay stable, which caps realized meta-depth at about two. Meta^n keeps a fixed meta-operation Omega and recurses on its growing input (solver traces plus code), writing successive layers of pre-processing and helper libraries. Because Omega never changes, the authors argue it cannot destabilize the system.
