Run a dedicated scoop check (ICLR 2027 OpenReview plus arXiv) on safeguard/guardrail/policy-compliance distillation, which the Nov 12 sweep skipped. Cite and position against TAME, Harness Annealing, Harness2Policy, SkillCore, Harness-Zero, MECA, yl1XFtnTn4 (the never-firing guard) and SEABench. 4. Add a short unidentifiability proposition, so the work is not "Masked Erosion + HERD" (K4). 5. Either commit to the multi-round HERD arm (margin decay per distill round) to earn RSI relevance, or target a safety venue.
judges.reviewerQuote: That trajectory-SFT cannot learn a safeguard that never changes the sampled behavior is true by construction; the paper's contribution therefore rests entirely on the logit-KL divergence predictor, which is evaluated on small LoRA students in a handful of synthetic lattices and reads as a Masked Erosion follow-up rather than a new mechanism.

judges.strongest: No paper, on arXiv or among the ICLR 2027 submissions, measures per-safeguard retention of redundant (masked) safeguards under harness-to-weights distillation. The ICLR sweep finds no Masked Erosion or HERD follow-up, and the nearest work (Harness-Zero rZ7eO7DZmc, Harness2Policy sUomzDTiu7, SkillCore 2EC98UmU1e, MECA AiTVmLVnt1, TAME IXnpSW8g3v) only scores visible behaviors or capability. The sampled-SFT vs logit-KL factorization with a teacher-divergence predictor computed before training gives a clean, cheap mechanistic contrast, with a pilot under $100 on Qwen3-4B.
judges.weakest: The headline is close to a definition. Trajectory-SFT dropping masked layers follows from the definition of masking. The logit-KL arm is now predictable from the late-2026 subliminal-learning and dark-knowledge wave: 2609.01091 (trait-direction drift), 2610.10657 (Beyond Owls), 2610.30884, 2610.26311 (selective transfer through sequence distillation) and 2610.07654 (OPD safety backdoors) all show that soft-label or on-policy distillation transmits traits absent from sampled text. So 'logit-KL carries masked safeguards in proportion to D_KL' reads to insiders as subliminal learning applied to Masked Erosion's lattice (K4). Two neighbors in the ICLR 2027 pool cover the audit and safety-drift framings without distillation: yl1XFtnTn4 (Auditing Harness Evolution; an accepted guard never fires in 3,960 checks) and SEABench X0eCGaNLsC (self-evolution induces safety failures). TAME IXnpSW8g3v owns 'capability retained after support removal'. Fit with the RSI agenda is weak, and it reads as a safety-venue paper.
judges.mustFix: (1) Before writing anything, pre-register a non-obvious prediction that subliminal learning does NOT already imply. For example: D_KL predicts retention better than token-level visibility, or logit-KL retention of masked layers fails under LoRA rank limits or for safeguards that act only in rare states. Cite and differentiate subliminal learning (2609.01091, 2610.10657, 2610.26311), OPD safety (2610.07654, 2610.27555) and Harness-Aware Distillation (2610.02858). (2) Validate the layer-targeted stress battery against the harness lattice in the pilot. Without that, masked retention is undefined. (3) Make the multi-round HERD-style arm, in which margin decays per evolve-then-distill round, central rather than optional. It is the only link to RSI, and it separates the work from yl1XFtnTn4, SEABench X0eCGaNLsC and TAME IXnpSW8g3v, all of which must be cited. (4) Contact the Masked Erosion authors or move fast: the scoop window is a few months.
judges.reviewerQuote: That sampled-trajectory SFT cannot learn a safeguard that never changes behavior on the training distribution is true by construction, and that logit-level distillation transmits such latent tendencies is already established by the subliminal-learning literature, so the contribution reduces to applying Masked Erosion's lattice to known distillation phenomena.

judges.strongest: The sharpened claim makes a real, testable prediction: sampled-SFT keeps about 0 of a masked safeguard's margin, while on-policy logit-KL keeps it in proportion to a teacher-divergence score you can compute before training. That turns a "follows from the definition" observation into a mechanism with a predictor. The Nov 12 ICLR 2027 sweep found no submission on safeguard retention under harness-to-weights distillation. Masked Erosion and HERD are not on ICLR 2027 either. Harness-Zero (rZ7eO7DZmc), Harness2Policy (sUomzDTiu7) and SkillCore (2EC98UmU1e) are all capability-only, with no safety, redundancy or audit analysis. So the precise gap is still open, and the pilot costs under $100 and takes a week.
judges.weakest: The headline result is predictable. A masked layer leaves no behavioral trace, so SFT will drop it, and "logit-KL transfers what the teacher's distribution encodes" is close to definitional too. If the divergence predictor is only moderately correlated, what remains is "Masked Erosion applied to distillation", which is borderline K4. The setting is also getting crowded. The ICLR 2027 sweep lists three harness-distillation submissions (Harness-Zero rZ7eO7DZmc, Harness2Policy sUomzDTiu7, SkillCore 2EC98UmU1e), saturated weight-harness co-evolution work (12+ submissions, including MECA AiTVmLVnt1, which consolidates memory into weights), and safety-drift-in-self-evolution work: SEABench (X0eCGaNLsC) and Auditing Harness Evolution (yl1XFtnTn4, where an accepted guard never fires in 3,960 checks, i.e. a masked-guard phenomenon on the harness side). Any of these groups, or the Masked Erosion authors, can add a "safety retention" appendix. Mentor fit is weak (safety/oversight rather than self-referential improvement), and a solo undergrad has to build a stress battery whose validity is the whole paper.
judges.mustFix: (1) Before anything else, run the 1-week pilot to test whether the logit-KL arm keeps masked margin at all and whether D_KL(teacher_with || teacher_without) predicts it (target rank correlation of at least 0.6 across lattice states). If both come back roughly zero, kill the idea. (2) Validate the layer-targeted stress battery against the harness lattice. It must reproduce one-layer-ablation margins, or masked retention stays undefined. (3) Position the work explicitly against the ICLR 2027 submissions Harness-Zero (rZ7eO7DZmc), Harness2Policy (sUomzDTiu7), SkillCore (2EC98UmU1e), SEABench (X0eCGaNLsC) and Auditing Harness Evolution (yl1XFtnTn4), and contact the Masked Erosion authors early. (4) Make the multi-round arm central, not optional, to fit the mentor's RSI agenda: margin spent per distill round inside an evolve-then-distill loop. (5) Keep the avoidance and base-prior controls (paired permitted/forbidden contexts, no-rule teacher) as primary results.
judges.reviewerQuote: Because a masked safeguard by construction produces no behavioral difference on the training distribution, it is unsurprising that trajectory SFT fails to retain it; the paper's contribution therefore rests entirely on whether the teacher-divergence predictor works, and on only small Qwen students across synthetic lattices the evidence for that is too thin for a main-track claim.

dossier.title: Recursive Gain vs Frontier Hardening: First Identified Micro-Estimate of R_AI from Controlled Self-Improvement Loops (rsi-elasticity)
dossier.claim: Same-start swap tests run on a full improver × artifact-state grid, in log-cost units at matched token budget, show that later improvers are measurably better (recursive gain g > 0) but frontier hardening σ outweighs that gain. R_AI = g/σ is about 0.2–0.5 on the loop's own search tasks and indistinguishable from 0 on fresh held-out tasks, with CIs excluding 1, and trajectory-only (diagonal) estimates mis-estimate both g and σ by large factors. This is the sharpened claim from the round-1 critique. The original claim was simply that the "self-feedback elasticity is well below 1, lower on held-out than search tasks."
dossier.design: Take improver checkpoints I_0/I_10/I_20/I_40 and solver/artifact states S_0/S_10/S_20/S_40 from the same lineage, plus a second lineage for cross-fitting. Run every improver×state pair at a matched token/$ budget: a 4×4 grid × ≥5 seeds. Do this in 3 systems: a Gödel-Agent-style self-referential loop, a Hyperagents/DGM-H-style archive loop, and a fixed-improver GEPA-style placebo where g≡0. Measure capability in log-cost units (Burtsev eq. 1: log of the tokens a reference solver needs to reach a target success rate on a fixed panel), with robustness checks in accuracy and logit. Fit log Δ = a·log c(I) − σ·c(S) to identify g and σ, giving R_AI = g/σ. Report narrow (search-set) vs broad (fresh procedural held-out) estimates as Cunningham et al.'s narrow/broad superelasticity. Add a frozen-knowledge arm (procedure from g_k with memory from g_0, and the reverse), out-of-sample re-scoring of checkpoints to correct selection bias, a pre-registered H0: R_AI ≥ 1, and a simulated power analysis. Pilot first: a 2×2 grid (I_0/I_20 × S_0/S_20), one system, 5 seeds, about $50. The full grid costs under $2k on Haiku/Qwen-class models.
dossier.history: The idea started as "Idea 3 / G3" in the round-1 frontier-trends sweep, a reframing of Dan's improver-scaling idea (#1) around the economics estimand ε_{Ȧ,A}. It became candidate C3 `rsi-elasticity` (T1). The round-1 critique scored it 64.6 as written (74.6 with fixes). It found three problems: the estimand is ill-defined in accuracy units, the fresh-artifact swap identifies only g and not σ, and the result is underpowered. The critique recommended against a standalone paper and suggested making the off-diagonal grid plus R_AI the headline estimand of C1. The round-1 REPORT ranked it #12 (65) and marked it "→ #1 estimand", folded into the merged paper "Effect, Cause, Decay" (75.8). In round 2 the merged paper was cut to the Decay claim alone ("Meta-Overfitting", 77.9). Effect, the swap curve this estimand lived in, was demoted to a pre-registered gate, because MetaRSI, RSIFlow, FreeEvolve and SelfSearch already own same-start swaps. The elasticity/R_AI estimand does not appear in any round-2 proposal. In effect it was dropped, and the field forecast flags the "improver × state swap actually run" paper as a likely scoop (75%, roughly Feb–Apr 2027).
dossier.priorScores: R1 critique 64.6 as written (74.6 projected with fixes); R1 REPORT ranking 65 (#12, folded into #1 merged paper at 75.8); not separately scored in R2 (the #1 successor Meta-Overfitting scored 77.9 without this estimand)

closestPapers.title: Auditing the Product, Not the Recursion: The Evaluation Evidence Behind Recursive Self-Improvement Claims
closestPapers.summary: A full-text census of 114 RSI studies (90 self-described RSI) that separates product claims from process claims. Only 22% audit two or more reruns of the full loop. Of 26 studies claiming a better improvement procedure, few run a same-start, matched-budget swap (4 of 26 per round-1 deep read). It defines claims C1–C5, with C5 compounding (repeated swap tests with growing improver gain) listed as unmeasured.
closestPapers.relation: It names exactly the missing experiment (the C5 swap test) and, per the round-1 critique, Proposition 3 on diagonal non-identification, which motivates the off-diagonal grid. It runs no experiments. It is both the strongest motivation citation and the biggest scoop vector, since anyone reading it can run C5.

closestPapers.title: MetaRSI / RSI2: A Meta-Recursive Self-Improving System for Recursive Self-Improving Systems Themselves
closestPapers.summary: A loop composing Data-, Harness- and Model-RSI operators with a meta-level schedule policy, run with no external teacher on an open model (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B). Per the round-2 fact-check, §5.4 runs a same-start, same-budget swap: the meta-updated improver adds +7.2 vs +4.9. A 5-term compounding curve gives +26.2 vs +20.7 over 5 seeds, and per-term gain decays in both arms.
closestPapers.relation: This is the closest empirical competitor. Its decaying per-term gains are effectively a diagonal diminishing-returns measurement and already show g > 0 in-domain. It leaves open the off-diagonal improver×state grid (one S1, one fork), log-cost units, an R_AI/elasticity estimate, multiple loop families and narrow-vs-broad.

closestPapers.title: Recursive Criticality of AI Self-Improvement
closestPapers.summary: A model of AI R&D feedback that derives a recursive reproduction number R_AI comparing recursive feedback strength to the rate at which progress gets harder. R_AI>1 means improvements compound across cycles. Per the critique, capability is defined via log resource cost on a fixed task panel, and the parameters are not yet empirically constrained.
closestPapers.relation: Supplies the estimand (R_AI = g/σ) and the unit (log-cost) that the fixed design adopts. Pure theory with no measurement, so it is a foundation rather than a competitor.

closestPapers.title: The Economics of Recursive Self-Improvement
closestPapers.summary: Builds graph-based models of AI progress in which net acceleration depends on the product of elasticities around each feedback loop. It distinguishes narrow (AI-R&D benchmark) from broad capabilities, and publishes a wish list of measurable empirical objects. A back-of-envelope calibration finds feedback loops are not currently strong enough for self-sustaining acceleration but appear to be strengthening.
closestPapers.relation: The original motivation: it asks for elasticities that controlled loops could supply. Its narrow/broad split maps onto the search vs held-out arms. It uses macro/lab data only, with no micro-estimates.

closestPapers.title: Audit the Scaffold, Not the Checkpoint: A Stationarity Dichotomy for Recursive Self-Improvement in Agentic Coding
closestPapers.summary: Argues that iterative self-modification hits strict diminishing returns whenever the reachable edit set stays fixed, and can escape only if scaffolding rewrites expand it. It reads refinement as gradient boosting on residual error and measures saturation, including per-round improvement decay on SWE-bench tasks and failure overlap across same-family workers.
closestPapers.relation: Makes the original headline (elasticity < 1) a predicted result, which is the main source of the low-surprise critique. It does not measure improver-to-improver elasticity or run swap tests.

closestPapers.title: Recursive self-improvement of AI research agents (AIDE^2)
closestPapers.summary: AIDE^2 runs an RSI loop on a frontier AI research agent's own code, keeping rewrites that score best on hidden evaluations. An 8-day run found seven successive improvements that generalize to four held-out benchmarks, including an OOD weather task. Per the round-1 critique, its ignition (swap) test is inconclusive at 3 seeds.
closestPapers.relation: Established the ignition/swap framing and explicitly motivates RSI as countering diminishing returns to R&D. It has a single underpowered contrast, no elasticity, and no off-diagonal grid.

closestPapers.title: Efficiency vs Capability in the Intelligence Explosion
closestPapers.summary: A task-automation model in which a software intelligence explosion requires both capability and efficiency margins to improve fast enough, and neither substitutes for the other. Calibrated on recent AI-progress data, it finds an SIE in 49% of Monte Carlo draws, with efficiency progress the largest source of uncertainty.
closestPapers.relation: Another macro paper naming returns parameters nobody has measured in a controlled loop. It motivates reporting the elasticity per unit cost (the efficiency leg). Macro only.

closestPapers.title: The Singularity Has a Distribution: Exact Timing Laws and Detection Limits for a Stochastic Intelligence Explosion
closestPapers.summary: Models a stochastic intelligence explosion where multiplicative improvements arrive at a rate proportional to a power of capability, and derives the explosion-time distribution. It gives a fixed-sample test between constant and geometrically increasing idea rates, with minimum sample size ~ (12 z_α^2)^(1/3) ℓ^(-2/3).
closestPapers.relation: Provides the power warning behind the critique: a few checkpoints × 5 seeds likely cannot distinguish elasticity 0.5 from 1. Its detection law can be borrowed for the pre-registered power analysis. A foundation for the power analysis, not a competitor.
closestPapers.when: Oct 2026, working paper (verified via alphaXiv full text)

feedback.point: The estimand is not scooped, but the same-start swap design is common (AIDE², MetaRSI, Hyperagents imp@k). 2610.27610 publicly names C5 compounding as the unmeasured gap, so the novelty has a short half-life: move fast and pre-register.
feedback.addressed: Partially. The fixed design pre-registers H0: R_AI ≥ 1. In round 2 the estimand was dropped along with the Effect section, so the scoop risk was avoided by abandonment rather than speed.

feedback.point: The estimand is ill-defined in accuracy units. Elasticities are not invariant to monotone transforms, so the threshold of 1 is a unit artifact. Use log-cost units (Burtsev eq. 1) or a compute-equivalent scale, with robustness checks.
feedback.addressed: Yes, in the critique's fixed design (log-cost units plus accuracy/logit robustness). This was never carried into a round-2 proposal.

feedback.point: A fresh-artifact swap identifies only the improver gain g, not frontier hardening σ, so 'not self-sustaining' does not follow. An off-diagonal improver × state grid is needed.
feedback.addressed: Yes, in the fixed design (4×4 grid, R_AI = g/σ). This was the key fix, but no round-2 proposal implements the grid. Round-2 fact-check and field forecast list the off-diagonal grid as the gap MetaRSI leaves, and as a likely scoop by ~Feb–Apr 2027.

feedback.point: The result is foreseeable: 2609.34924 proves diminishing returns under bounded metrics, and Hyperagents and AIDE² show n.s. compounding. 'ε < 1' is the boring outcome, so the null risks K2.
feedback.addressed: Partially. It was reframed around the g-vs-σ decomposition, narrow-vs-broad superelasticity and the diagonal-vs-off-diagonal methods result. Surprise is projected at 3.5.

feedback.point: Underpowered: 4 checkpoints leave about 2 df per system, so the CI likely spans 0 and 1 (cf. 2610.18445 detection law). No power analysis.
feedback.addressed: Yes, in the fixed design (simulated power/MDE and a $50 pilot to measure seed variance). The round-2 sharpness reviewer of the successor paper went further, arguing that 'a curve from correlated checkpoints is a figure, not a test'. Lineage-level tests (n≥10) were adopted for Decay, not for this estimand.

feedback.point: Winner's curse: checkpoints selected on noisy dev scores inflate accumulated improvement, biasing the slope downward.
feedback.addressed: Yes, in the fixed design (re-score on a fresh audit set and use a second lineage as an instrument).

feedback.point: Compute matching: later improvers use more tokens per proposal, so matching by iterations confounds quality with spend.
feedback.addressed: Yes, in the fixed design (match on tokens/$ and report the elasticity per unit cost).

feedback.point: What carries the improvement, procedure or memory/archive? A frozen-knowledge control (2610.29677 R2) is missing.
feedback.addressed: Yes, as a procedure-vs-memory arm. This concern became central to the round-2 lead paper (scrubbed, memory-wiped procedure Pk^s+∅), though for Decay rather than this estimand.

feedback.point: Scope overreach: 'today's RSI loops are not self-sustaining' generalizes from harness-level frozen-weight loops.
feedback.addressed: Yes. The framing is restricted to 'harness-level loops with frozen weights'.

feedback.point: Do not ship it alone, because alone it reads as 'C1 swap tests + an econ regression'. Make it the headline estimand of C1.
feedback.addressed: Followed in R1: folded into #1 as its estimand. In R2 the Effect section was demoted to a gate and the estimand disappeared.

feedback.point: Macro models lack micro estimates; no ML paper has estimated an elasticity from a self-improvement loop. The idea also gives #1 an economics-grounded estimand that policy readers care about.
feedback.addressed: This is the idea's origin and still holds as of R1 (critique confirmed it is unscooped).

feedback.point: MetaRSI 2609.06396 is stronger than round 1 said: a same-start swap (+7.2 vs +4.9), a 5-term compounding curve (+26.2 vs +20.7) with per-term decay, 5 seeds, open model. The remaining gap is off-diagonal grids, generality across loop families, independent audit and replication.
feedback.addressed: Not addressed for this idea. The R2 lead paper conceded Effect to MetaRSI. The listed gaps are exactly what the fixed rsi-elasticity design would fill.

feedback.point: Effect (the same-start swap) is effectively taken by MetaRSI, RSIFlow, FreeEvolve and Skill∞. A powered in-domain swap paper is expected by the ICML 2027 deadline, so 'do not anchor on Effect'. A 5-point checkpoint curve is a figure, not a test. Index generations by accepted edits.
feedback.addressed: Addressed by demotion. The swap/Effect part, which carried this estimand, became a gate in Meta-Overfitting v2.

feedback.point: 'RSI evaluation/auditing' is saturating. The next obvious paper is the 'swap test actually run': improver × state at matched compute. Scoop risk is high (~Feb–Apr 2027, 75% by May).
feedback.addressed: Not addressed. This is the strongest argument that the standalone version of this idea will be scooped before NeurIPS 2027.

openRisks: Scoop: the field forecast gives 75% odds of a powered improver × state swap paper by May 2027 (likely follow-ups to 2610.27610 or Flex-RSI, ~Feb 2027). MetaRSI already holds in-domain g > 0 with a compounding curve.

Low surprise: diminishing returns (ε < 1 / R_AI < 1) is predicted by 2609.34924 and by MetaRSI's decaying per-term gains. Only a locally supercritical narrow regime or a large diagonal-vs-off-diagonal disagreement would surprise.
Power: even a 4×4 grid × 5 seeds may not give CIs that exclude 1. Lineage-level variance (σ ≈ 4 pp per R2 red team) makes slopes from correlated checkpoints weak tests.
Feasibility: per SelfImprove-Bench 2611.02797, 0% of retained edits touch the improver unless forced, so later improver checkpoints may barely differ from I_0 and g may be undetectable.
Unit choice: log-cost capability requires a reference-solver cost curve per state, which adds cost and makes results depend on the reference solver chosen.
Orphaned status: the estimand appears in no round-2 proposal. Reviving it means either a standalone paper (flagged K4-ish) or re-adding it to Meta-Overfitting as a secondary analysis.
Some claims about MetaRSI §5.4 and the 2610.27610 C4 counts and Proposition 3 rest on the round-1/round-2 deep reads, not on the abstracts fetched here.

judges.strongest: The estimand is new and policy-relevant. Fitting R_AI = g/sigma in log-cost units from an off-diagonal improver x state grid, separating narrow from broad and diagonal from off-diagonal estimates, gives the macro RSI models (2609.00137, 2609.15802, 2610.33447) the first micro-calibrated parameter they explicitly ask for. No arXiv or ICLR 2027 submission reports an elasticity or g/sigma decomposition. The diagonal-vs-off-diagonal mis-estimation result could also stand as a methods contribution.
judges.weakest: The ICLR 2027 sweep shows the measurement design is already taken. "Improvement by Inheritance: Measuring RSI in Coding Agents" (openreview ZMmJDeDTXk) runs nested replay that crosses candidate improvers with common start states, which is the improver x state swap the field forecast predicted for Feb-Apr 2027, arriving months early. "Learning to Repair the Learner" (aEPJT4hW84) runs a code x history crossing (procedure vs memory, with inherited procedure explaining 45% of the gain), and MetaEvoForge (0b4wysHrzh) runs a same-root evolved-vs-unevolved improver test. What is left is an econometric regression on top of a now-published assay, which is K4. Improvement by Inheritance also finds the improver almost never edits itself (child quality goes from 0.48 to 0.86 while successor quality does not move). That makes g likely indistinguishable from 0 without forced improver edits, and then R_AI is just 0/sigma: a foreseeable null. That null is already predicted by 2609.34924 and by MetaRSI's per-term decay. A 4x4 grid from correlated checkpoints in one lineage still gives few effective degrees of freedom, so CIs excluding 1 are plausible but CIs excluding 0 on g are not.
judges.mustFix:
1. Stop claiming the swap or grid design. Cite ZMmJDeDTXk, aEPJT4hW84, 0b4wysHrzh, AnN0NpAVWL (HMED) and MetaRSI as measurement lineage, and put all novelty in the identified estimand (g, sigma, and R_AI in log-cost units) and in the result that diagonal (trajectory) estimates are biased.
2. Gate on improver edits: require at least 1 accepted improver edit per 4 iterations, or force improver edits, and include a fixed-improver placebo. Otherwise g is unidentifiable.
3. Show identification and power before the full grid: simulate whether a 4x4 grid x 5 seeds x 2 lineages can separate R_AI of 0.3 from 1, and from 0, using the 2610.18445 detection law. Use lineage-level replication (10 or more lineages at small scale) rather than checkpoint curves.
4. Re-estimate on the released Hyperagents history that ZMmJDeDTXk uses, so the R_AI number is directly comparable.
5. Do not ship this standalone. Make it the secondary-estimand section of the Meta-Overfitting/Decay paper, or of a short econ-facing workshop note.
judges.reviewerQuote: The improver x state crossing is already published (Improvement by Inheritance; Learning to Repair the Learner), and dividing a near-zero improver gain by a hardening term to report "R_AI is about 0.3, not self-sustaining" re-labels a result everyone predicted rather than measuring anything new.

judges.strongest: The estimand itself is still unclaimed. No 2026 arXiv paper or ICLR 2027 submission I could find (sweep plus an alphaXiv check) gives a micro-identified R_AI = g/σ in log-cost units, separates recursive gain from frontier hardening with an off-diagonal improver × state grid, or contrasts narrow and broad estimates. It also answers the empirical wish lists in 2609.15802, 2609.00137 and 2610.33447 directly, which gives it reach beyond ML into policy.
judges.weakest: The design itself is already taken. "Improvement by Inheritance: Measuring RSI in Coding Agents" (ICLR 2027, openreview ZMmJDeDTXk) runs nested replay that crosses improvers with common start states. That is the improver × state swap the field forecast predicted for Feb–Apr 2027, and it has arrived three months early. It also reports that improvers almost never edit themselves, so successor quality stays flat and g ≈ 0 in-domain. Learning to Repair the Learner (aEPJT4hW84) adds a code × history crossing, and MetaRSI already reports in-domain g > 0 with decaying per-term gains. With g near zero, R_AI ≈ 0 is a foregone result, and σ is poorly identified when g has no variance. What remains is "IbI's grid plus a Burtsev/Cunningham regression in log-cost units", which is K4 almost word for word. On top of that, the log-cost unit needs a reference-solver cost curve for every state, and the CIs from a 4×4 grid × 5 seeds will probably be wide.
judges.mustFix: 1. Stop presenting this as a standalone paper. Make R_AI/elasticity a secondary, pre-registered analysis inside Meta-Overfitting/Decay, and cite Improvement by Inheritance (ZMmJDeDTXk) and aEPJT4hW84 as the source of the measurement method. 2. Make g identifiable by design. Use forced improver edits plus the pilot gate (at least 1 accepted improver edit per 4 iterations), or the R_AI estimate is just 0/σ. 3. Make the one new contribution a methods result: diagonal (trajectory) estimates vs off-diagonal grid estimates of g and σ in log-cost vs accuracy units. Show the bias on IbI's released Hyperagents history and on MetaRSI's curve, and re-analyse public lineages where possible to save cost. 4. Use lineage-level n ≥ 10 rather than 5 seeds on correlated checkpoints, and run the 2610.18445 detection-law power analysis before spending more than the $50 pilot.
judges.reviewerQuote: The improver × state swap is already in Improvement by Inheritance, which shows the improver barely changes. Fitting an economics elasticity to a recursive gain that is essentially zero gives a number, not a finding.

judges.strongest: The estimand is still unclaimed. The ICLR 2027 sweep (about 210 queries) found no submission that estimates an elasticity, R_AI = g/σ, or frontier hardening σ from a controlled loop. The METR, GovAI and Recursive Criticality macro papers explicitly ask for exactly this micro-parameter, so a log-cost R_AI estimate with narrow-vs-broad CIs would be the first number policy and econ readers could plug into those models. The diagonal-vs-off-diagonal bias result is a reusable methods point, and it fits the mentor's Gödel-Agent lineage directly.
judges.weakest: The design is now the scooped part. The ICLR 2027 submission "Improvement by Inheritance: Measuring RSI in Coding Agents" (openreview ZMmJDeDTXk) already crosses candidate improvers with common start states (nested replay) and separates child quality from successor quality. It finds that successor quality does not move because the improver almost never edits itself. "Learning to Repair the Learner" (aEPJT4hW84) already runs a code × history crossing, which covers this idea's procedure-vs-memory arm, and MetaRSI holds in-domain g > 0 with a decaying compounding curve. What is left is putting an economics regression on top of someone else's assay, which is K4. The most likely outcome is that g is not significantly different from 0, because improvers do not self-edit. Then R_AI ≈ 0 holds trivially, ZMmJDeDTXk has already said so, and the 2609.34924 bound predicts it, which is the K2 risk. Power is also a problem: a 4×4 grid from correlated checkpoints in one lineage per system is unlikely to give σ CIs that exclude 1 within $2k. Reference-solver log-cost curves for every state add cost and make the result depend on which reference solver is chosen.
judges.mustFix: Do not ship this as a standalone paper. Fold R_AI = g/σ in log-cost units into Meta-Overfitting/Decay as a secondary, pre-registered estimand, computed on the improver × state grid that paper already needs. Cite ZMmJDeDTXk (nested replay), aEPJT4hW84 (crossing), AnN0NpAVWL (HMED), MetaRSI and 0b4wysHrzh as the measurement lineage, and claim only (a) the σ identification plus R_AI and (b) the narrow-vs-broad split. Make g detectable by gating on at least 1 accepted improver edit per 4 iterations and by adding a forced-improver-edit arm. Index generations by accepted improver edits and use at least 10 lineages, not 4 correlated checkpoints. Run the $50 2×2 pilot first. If seed variance means the simulated MDE cannot separate R_AI = 0.5 from 1, drop the estimand entirely.
judges.reviewerQuote: The improver × state crossing is already in Improvement by Inheritance, and with improvers that barely edit themselves, dividing a gain indistinguishable from zero by a noisily estimated hardening term to get 'R_AI ≈ 0.3' adds an economics label but no new empirical insight.

dossier.claim: Self-improvers do not learn a model of themselves. On sealed, noise-corrected edit pools, forecast skill does not rise across improver checkpoints once edit-distribution shift is controlled, the improver forecasts its own edits no better than a fresh outsider given the same archive, and shuffled forecasts at matched revisions recover most of the predict-before-modify (IDM) gain. If forecast skill does rise, it predicts swap-test improver gain, which would make it a cheap, validated metric for "improving at improving". This is the round-1 critique's sharpened version; it was never developed further on its own.
dossier.design: This is the reframed audit design from the round-1 critique, since no v2 proposal was written. (1) Leakage-free re-analysis of IDM's "forecast improves" claim: later checkpoints are tested only on sealed edits generated after their last update, with at least 5 re-evaluations per edit to set a noise ceiling and disattenuate skill. (2) Checkpoint × edit-pool crossing: freeze forecaster/improver checkpoints at generations {0,10,20,40}, and have each forecast the same sealed pools of sibling edits drawn from early, mid and late depths. Score with a skill score vs. climatology (parent-mean gain) and sibling-ranking AUC, which are robust to range restriction. (3) Privileged-self-knowledge test: the improver's forecast of its own edits vs. a fresh-context same-model outsider given the identical archive vs. a different-family model. (4) Online placebo ladder at matched revisions and tokens: true / shuffled-across-siblings / constant base-rate / inverted / no-forecast reflection. (5) Predictive validity: regress small same-start swap-test improver gain on forecast skill across checkpoints, loops and seeds. Scope is 2 loops (GEPA plus a Hyperagents-lite/Gödel-style self-editor) × 2 open model families, with DGM public logs as the offline set. The pilot is under $50: GEPA, 200 sibling edits, 5× re-evaluation, and a check that the noise ceiling is at least 0.3 R² before anything else.
dossier.history: Round 1: the idea was created as candidate C16 by merging the frontier-trends sweep's Idea 2 (self-forecast skill as a probe of meta-learning) with the world-model sweep's Idea 2. The first pitch had four claims: flat forecast skill means "RSI gains are search"; a shuffled-forecast placebo recovers the IDM gain; calibration collapses with depth and environment shift; rising skill would be "the first direct evidence of meta-learning". The critique scored it 66 (viable with fixes). It found the niche partly scooped by IDM (2610.13991, which claims forecast accuracy improves) and BCO (2609.01861, which already runs a scrambled-content placebo). It recommended reframing as a leakage-free, noise-corrected audit with checkpoint × edit-pool crossing, a privileged-self-knowledge test and swap-test predictive validity. The round-1 panel then demoted it to "→ #1 readout": a diagnostic inside the lead paper (Effect/Cause/Decay). There was no standalone proposal. Round 2: the idea did not continue on its own. The bold-ideas file explicitly excludes it as a round-1 repeat, and the v2 of the lead paper (Meta-Overfitting, 77.9) has no forecast readout; it uses an "introspective drift" readout instead. The critique's privileged-self-knowledge fix came back independently as the round-2 bold idea sharp-no-privileged-self-access (73, "Promising / fold" into #1 as a memory-transplant arm). Its bold check found the model-level null (no privileged self-access) is already established.
dossier.priorScores: R1 critique 66.3 (N 2.5, S 3.0, R 4.5, C 3.0, F 3.5, T 4.5) → R1 panel: folded into #1 as a readout (no standalone score) → R2: not re-scored. The related spin-off sharp-no-privileged-self-access was scored 73 (≈77 after fixes) and also marked "fold into #1".

closestPapers.title: Predict Before You Modify: Learning Improvement Dynamics for Self-Evolving Agents (IDM)
closestPapers.summary: Adds an editable Improvement Dynamics Model to HyperAgents. Before evaluation, the IDM predicts task-level outcomes of each proposed modification and can trigger a revision; after evaluation, observed outcomes are used to update it. It beats HyperAgents in four domains (coding, paper review, robot reward design, Olympiad grading), by up to 46%, under matched token budgets. It reports that forecast accuracy improves as the IDM evolves and that the predictive knowledge transfers to a new domain.
closestPapers.relation: Near-scoop that makes the opposite headline claim (forecast skill rises). It already logs forecasts on every candidate and has a revision-only control. Gaps per the critique: no shuffled-forecast placebo, a likely contaminated fixed-case test (gen 1–5 records seen during updates), no noise ceiling, a forecaster separate from the improver, no link from forecast skill to improvement rate or swap tests, and 5 runs on one system. The idea survives only as a rigorous audit of this paper's claim.

closestPapers.title: Belief-Calibrated Optimization: An Explicit World Model for Agentic Optimization (BCO)
closestPapers.summary: Turns the coding-agent optimizer's implicit belief about how the environment responds to scaffold edits into a persistent in-context 'world model' document, revised after each evaluated candidate. Adding it to an otherwise standard loop beats a matched control without the world model on five benchmarks (memory QA, tool-use QA, code-as-action app agents and more).
closestPapers.relation: Already has a predict→observe→correct world model of edits and, per the critique's deep read, an offline content placebo (None < Scrambled < Intact). Gaps: one trajectory per method, a 4-run placebo (p=0.125), forecast skill not tracked over iterations or tied to gain rate, no online shuffled-forecast arm, and no noise-ceiling correction.

closestPapers.title: Language Models as AI Research World Models
closestPapers.summary: Evaluates LMs as Research World Models that predict the outcomes of candidate interventions, using over 2,600 experiment records from nine research environments (171k H100 GPU-hours). Experience from real records improves prediction of unseen interventions within an environment (Spearman +0.27), and knowledge transfers across environments, reducing selection regret.
closestPapers.relation: Shows that 'forecast improves with records' is ordinary in-context surrogate learning. This undercuts reading a rising forecast curve as meta-learning, so the idea needs the self-vs-outsider and checkpoint-crossing controls. It does not study self-editing improvers or link forecast skill to improvement rate.

closestPapers.title: Can LLMs predict the outcomes of machine learning experiments?
closestPapers.summary: Builds 288 LLM-proposed ideas on eight MLE-bench tasks and asks five frontier LLMs to predict each idea's impact before training. The best model reaches R²=0.49, all models underestimate effect magnitudes, quality varies by task, the implementing harness matters little, and there is no evidence of self-preference.
closestPapers.relation: The static, single-step version of the probe, and the direct basis for the round-1 idea. It leaves open forecast skill across improver generations and the noise ceiling (one run per idea). Its 'no self-preference' finding already points toward the idea's self ≈ outsider null.

closestPapers.title: Does Failure Feedback Direct Agent Self-Modification?
closestPapers.summary: Compares repair of a randomly chosen target failure with repair of the parent's other failures across 145 modifications in public Darwin Gödel Machine logs, and finds no target-specific advantage. Controlled small-model experiments show relevant feedback can raise target repair (+20pp for Qwen3-4B), but target repair does not reliably mean held-out improvement.
closestPapers.relation: Supports the 'search, not meta-learning' framing (DGM edits are undirected), which also makes that framing less novel. It does not test forecasting, so a forecast-skill probe complements its directedness probe. Its use of DGM public logs shows the offline data source exists.

closestPapers.title: Strangers to Themselves: What Language Models Say About Themselves Is Generic
closestPapers.summary: Turns self-knowledge into a prediction test across nine behavioral evaluations. Self-report is weak (r=+0.04), and item-informed questions about 'AI agents in general', or other models' self-reports, predict a model at least as well as its own self-prediction. Fine-tuning on a model's own record teaches narrow self-predictions but also changes the behavior being predicted.
closestPapers.relation: A model-level scoop for the idea's privileged-self-knowledge test, surfaced in the round-2 bold check for sharp-no-privileged-self-access. It makes 'self forecasts no better than an outsider' the expected null, so that arm needs lineage-level and memory-transplant framing to be surprising.

closestPapers.title: Auditing the Product, Not the Recursion: The Evaluation Evidence Behind Recursive Self-Improvement Claims
closestPapers.summary: Full-text codes 114 studies (90 self-described RSI) against a claim-indexed evidence codebook. Only 22% audit two or more full-loop reruns, and of 26 studies claiming a better improvement procedure only 4 compare earlier and later procedures from identical starts at matched budget.
closestPapers.relation: Foundation: it supplies the swap-test (same-start, matched-budget) vocabulary that the idea's predictive-validity arm uses. The idea positions forecast skill as a cheap proxy for that expensive swap test.

closestPapers.title: Evaluating and Improving LLM Self-Modeling
closestPapers.summary: Introduces a benchmark of verifiable self-modeling questions, such as whether a prompt edit would change the model's answer, and finds current models have limited skill with systematic counterfactual errors. RL on synthetic self-modeling data improves aggregate skill with some transfer, but the gains may not reflect privileged introspective access.
closestPapers.relation: Foundation: object-level self-forecasting. The idea lifts it to the improver level (forecasting the effects of one's own self-edits). Its cross-model finding of no own-model advantage also anticipates the self-vs-outsider null.

feedback.point: Novelty vs IDM (2610.13991) and BCO (2609.01861): IDM already logs forecasts on every Hyperagents candidate and claims forecast accuracy improves, with a revision-only control. BCO already ran a scrambled-content placebo. The pitch 'first direct evidence of meta-learning' overclaims and is partly scooped (K1 partial).
feedback.addressed: Addressed on paper by the critique's own sharpened claim, which reframes the idea as an audit of IDM/BCO-style claims (leakage-free, noise-corrected). No later version was written to implement it.

feedback.point: Construct validity: with frozen weights, rising forecast skill is just in-context surrogate learning from the archive (as RWM 2610.12235 shows). Flat skill does not imply 'gains are search', because of the generation-vs-verification gap.
feedback.addressed: Partly addressed by the sharpened claim: the privileged-self-knowledge test (self vs fresh outsider with the same archive) and dropping the 'meta-learning' headline. Not developed further.

feedback.point: Range restriction / non-stationarity: later edits are smaller and more alike, so R²/rank correlation fall mechanically. 'Calibration collapses with depth' is the default expectation, not a finding.
feedback.addressed: Addressed in the fix list: checkpoint × sealed edit-pool crossing, skill vs climatology and sibling-ranking AUC, and demoting calibration-vs-depth to a figure.

feedback.point: Noise ceiling: single-edit held-out gains are often below evaluation noise, and 3 seeds is probably too few. Without disattenuation a flat result cannot be interpreted.
feedback.addressed: Addressed in the fix list: at least 5 re-evaluations per edit, disattenuated skill, and a pilot gate (switch benchmark if the ceiling is below about 0.3 R²).

feedback.point: Data availability: Hyperagents/AHE/GEPA archives with per-candidate held-out outcomes may not be public, which would break the '$200 offline' claim. Only DGM logs are confirmed.
feedback.addressed: Partly: the fix says to use DGM public logs and confirm the other archives before promising them. Not resolved.

feedback.point: Statistical power: 8 seeds × 4 arms × 3 loops is expensive, and IDM-scale effects (~10% AUBC at 5 runs) may be undetectable.
feedback.addressed: Partly: scope cut to 2 loops × 2 model families. No power analysis was done.

feedback.point: Too many claims (flat skill, placebo, calibration collapse, environment shift, predictive validity) read like five workshop papers.
feedback.addressed: Addressed in the fix list: drop environment shift and make calibration-vs-depth a figure, not a claim.

feedback.point: K2 risk: if forecast skill rises and the placebo loses, the paper is just 'IDM replicated with more seeds'. Make predictive validity (forecast skill vs swap-test improver gain) and the self-vs-outsider test the core so every outcome carries information.
feedback.addressed: Addressed in the sharpened claim, which has both branches. Unimplemented.

feedback.point: Placebo should be a full online ladder (true / shuffled / base-rate / inverted / no-forecast reflection) at matched revisions and tokens, going beyond BCO's offline scramble.
feedback.addressed: Included in the critique's design. Not developed further.

feedback.point: Ranked #11 (66). Merged into the lead paper (Effect/Cause/Decay) as a 'readout' rather than a standalone paper.
feedback.addressed: Accepted. No standalone proposal followed.

feedback.point: In round 2 the lead paper (Meta-Overfitting, 77.9) has no forecast-skill readout. Its mechanism readout is 'introspective drift' (share of edits spent on self-inspection), and bold_ideas.md explicitly excludes self-forecast as a round-1 repeat.
feedback.addressed: Not addressed: the self-forecast readout was effectively dropped from the latest lead design.

feedback.point: The privileged-self-knowledge component (self vs outsider) is the expected null at model level: Strangers to Themselves 2609.09899, Masked by Consensus 2604.12373, Self-Modeling 2608.30980 and Repairs for Whom? 2610.38610. Pooled AUROC ties by construction (2610.05572), so within-task or disagreement-subset scoring and a memory-transplant arm are needed.

openRisks: Scooped headline: IDM (2610.13991) already claims forecast accuracy improves. The paper must show that IDM's evidence is fragile (leakage, noise, range restriction), or it reads as incremental.
The self-vs-outsider null is already expected from model-level work (2609.09899, 2608.30980, 2610.22599 'no self-preference'), which lowers Surprise.
The noise ceiling may be too low on agent benchmarks (single-edit gains below evaluation noise), making forecast skill unmeasurable. The pilot gate is untested.
Archive availability: per-candidate held-out outcomes exist publicly only for DGM logs, so other offline data may need costly re-runs.
Power: IDM-scale online placebo effects (~10% AUBC) may be undetectable at affordable seed counts with Hyperagents-lite.
Orphaned status: folded into #1 in round 1 but absent from the round-2 v2 lead design, so as it stands no plan carries it forward.
Rising forecast skill can be explained by in-context surrogate learning (2610.12235) rather than meta-learning, which leaves the positive branch's interpretation contested.
dossier.title: Does the Improver Learn a Model of Itself? A Leakage-Free Audit of Self-Forecast Skill in Self-Improving Agents

judges.strongest: This is the only design that runs a leakage-free, noise-ceiling-corrected crossing of checkpoints against sealed edit pools, together with predictive validity against same-start swap-test gain. It audits a live, visible positive claim: IDM is now both on arXiv (2610.13991) and an ICLR 2027 submission (ZBxV5bEYUH). Either branch is informative, because a rise that predicts swap gain gives a cheap "improving at improving" metric, and a collapse under controls deflates a headline result. The pilot is cheap and gated (under $50, noise ceiling R² of at least 0.3), and DGM public logs supply an offline set.
judges.weakest: Novelty is squeezed from three directions. IDM (ICLR 2027 ZBxV5bEYUH / arXiv 2610.13991) owns the "forecast skill rises" claim, and BCO already ran a content placebo. Strangers to Themselves, the Self-Modeling benchmark and the MLE-bench prediction paper already make the self-vs-outsider null the expected result. Research World Models (2610.12235) makes a rising curve explainable as ordinary in-context surrogate learning. The ICLR 2027 sweep adds a further problem: Improvement by Inheritance (ZMmJDeDTXk) shows that the Hyperagents-style improver almost never edits itself. "Improver checkpoints" are then nearly identical, so "does the improver model itself" collapses into "does a frozen LLM learn a surrogate from a growing archive". Without forced improver edits, the self-model construct is not identified. As an audit, the realistic outcome is a workshop-grade critique of one paper, and the idea is orphaned from the lead design.
judges.mustFix:
1. Position the paper explicitly as a replication and audit of IDM (ICLR 2027 ZBxV5bEYUH) using its released Hyperagents setup. Show leakage or noise fragility on IDM's own fixed-case test, or concede it.
2. Address Improvement by Inheritance (ZMmJDeDTXk). Add a pilot gate on improver self-edit rate, or force improver edits, so the checkpoints actually differ as improvers. Otherwise drop the "model of itself" framing.
3. Replace the pooled self-vs-outsider comparison with disagreement-subset or within-task scoring plus a memory-transplant arm (the archive from lineage A given to the improver of lineage B). This is what separates lineage-level self-knowledge from archive surrogate learning.
4. Run a power analysis for the online placebo ladder, at a minimum of 8 seeds, before committing to two loops × two model families.
5. Most realistically, fold this into the lead Meta-Overfitting paper as a forecast-skill readout with a swap-test validity check, rather than writing it as a standalone NeurIPS paper.
judges.reviewerQuote: Once one accounts for IDM's own results, the known absence of privileged self-knowledge in LLMs, and the observation that these improvers rarely edit themselves, this audit mostly re-measures in-context surrogate learning from an archive, and I do not see a standalone contribution beyond a careful replication note.

judges.strongest: It has a clean, falsifiable audit design: sealed post-update edit pools, a disattenuated noise ceiling, checkpoint × pool crossing scored against climatology, and an online shuffled/inverted placebo ladder at matched tokens. Together these directly test the one positive 'forecast skill rises' claim in the RSI literature (IDM). The predictive-validity arm (forecast skill vs swap-test improver gain) would give a cheap proxy metric if it holds, and the pilot costs under $50.
judges.weakest: The novelty depends entirely on rebutting one paper, and the ICLR 2027 sweep shows that paper, Predict Before You Modify (OpenReview ZBxV5bEYUH = arXiv 2610.13991), is now a live ICLR 2027 submission. Its headline (forecast accuracy improves and transfers) may well be peer-reviewed and accepted before NeurIPS 2027, so this paper reads as 'a rigorous critique of IDM' rather than a new question. The self-vs-outsider arm is already the expected null at model level (2609.09899, 2608.30980, 2610.22599). Improvement by Inheritance (ICLR27 ZMmJDeDTXk) shows improvers almost never edit themselves, so 'improver checkpoints' at gens 0/10/20/40 may be nearly identical. That makes the checkpoint-crossing and self-forecast constructs close to vacuous unless improver edits are forced. Finally, rising skill has the known in-context surrogate explanation (2610.12235), and there is no current host plan: it was dropped from the v2 lead.
judges.mustFix: 1. Position the paper explicitly as a pre-registered audit of ZBxV5bEYUH/2610.13991 and BCO, and get IDM's released runs or code to reproduce its forecast-improves curve before re-analysing it under the leakage and noise controls. 2. Following ZMmJDeDTXk, gate on actual improver self-edits: require at least one accepted improver edit per few generations, or force them. Otherwise the 'improver models itself' construct is undefined. 3. Replace the plain self-vs-outsider arm with a lineage/memory-transplant design scored on within-task disagreement subsets, since the model-level null is already known. 4. Run the noise-ceiling pilot (R² ≥ 0.3) and a power analysis for the online placebo ladder before committing. 5. Since the standalone paper is thin, fold it as the forecast/predictive-validity readout into the lead Meta-Overfitting/swap paper, which already runs the swap tests needed for arm (5).
judges.reviewerQuote: This is a careful re-analysis of a single concurrent paper's claim (Predict Before You Modify), and its central null, that improvers forecast their own edits no better than outsiders, is what prior self-modeling work already predicts. The submission does not show why the community should care beyond correcting IDM's evaluation protocol.

judges.strongest: The sealed checkpoint × edit-pool crossing with a noise ceiling and disattenuation is a real methodological contribution. No 2026 paper or ICLR 2027 submission measures forecast skill across improver checkpoints on shared held-out edits that later checkpoints never saw. The self-vs-foreign-lineage control is also still open: the ICLR sweep marks the 'self-knowledge' idea as open and finds no self-vs-foreign arm in Predict Before You Modify (ZBxV5bEYUH). The design also fits the mentor's Gödel Agent and meta-agent agenda.
judges.weakest: The headline is a rebuttal of one paper, and that paper is now a live ICLR 2027 submission. IDM, which is ZBxV5bEYUH on OpenReview (arXiv 2610.13991), already claims forecast accuracy improves and transfers. BCO already has a content placebo. RWM (2610.12235) already explains a rising forecast curve as in-context surrogate learning. Model-level work (2609.09899, 2608.30980, 2610.22599) already establishes the self ≈ outsider null. Two further ICLR 2027 submissions weaken the 'self' framing. Improvement by Inheritance (ZMmJDeDTXk) shows Hyperagents-style improvers almost never edit themselves, so improver checkpoints may barely differ and 'self' becomes the archive rather than the model. And if the null holds (flat skill, self = outsider, the placebo recovers the gain), a reviewer reads it as "audit of one Sep-2026 method with expected nulls". That is publishable at a workshop and hard to land at NeurIPS. The noise-ceiling gate (R² ≥ 0.3 on single-edit gains) is untested and may fail on agent benchmarks.
judges.mustFix: 1. Do not run this as a standalone paper. Fold it into the lead paper (Meta-Overfitting/Decay) as one diagnostic arm: forecast skill on sealed pools vs swap-test gain. Its pairing with self-vs-foreign-lineage overlaps the round-2 sharp-no-privileged-self-access memory-transplant arm, so merge the two. 2. Cite and directly re-analyze ZBxV5bEYUH (IDM, ICLR 2027). Show concretely that its fixed-case test leaks gen 1–5 records and how much of its forecast gain survives noise correction. Without that the audit has no teeth. 3. Score self-vs-outsider within each task and on the subset where the forecasters disagree, with a memory-transplant / foreign-lineage arm, because pooled AUROC ties by construction. Cite ZMmJDeDTXk and add a pilot gate requiring at least some accepted improver self-edits, or 'checkpoint' just means 'archive length'. 4. Run the $50 GEPA noise-ceiling pilot before any further investment. If the ceiling is below 0.3 R², kill the idea. 5. Pre-register predictive validity (forecast skill vs swap-test gain) as the primary outcome, so the positive branch is more than 'IDM replicated'.
judges.reviewerQuote: This is a careful audit of a single recent method (IDM), whose main findings — forecast skill rising via in-context surrogate learning and models lacking privileged self-knowledge — were already expected from prior work, so it is unclear what new capability or insight the community gains.

dossier.title: Gate Dial: the acceptance gate as the stability-plasticity dial of self-improving agents (parked in round 1; reframed as gate-resolution law plus gate-vs-proposer attribution)
dossier.claim: Latest version (the sharpened claim from the round-1 critique; the idea was not developed further in round 2): in long, non-stationary self-improvement, most of a meta-agent's lost plasticity comes from its acceptance gate, not its proposer. A gate stops learning once the per-edit effect size falls below its statistical resolution (z_alpha*sigma/sqrt(n)), and this resolution law predicts in advance the round at which strict gates freeze and start losing to lax ones. Changing what the gate validates on (current family vs replay, fresh vs reused evidence) moves the stability-plasticity frontier more than changing alpha.
dossier.design: Testbed: Dan's procedural tau-style generator, a long task stream with hundreds of family switches, horizon checkpoints at 10/30/100/300 rounds, and anytime curves. Two evolvers (GEPA-style prompt evolver and a Godel/Meta-Harness-style code evolver) are crossed with a factorial on the gate: strictness (greedy / paired-alpha / e-process / TRUST-style FDR) x scope (current-family vs replay over all seen families) x freshness (reused vs re-drawn selection set). Oracle-gate and always-accept bounds are included, total evaluation compute is matched, and n is swept, with a resolution-matched arm where n grows each round. Every candidate is logged so the same candidate stream can be re-gated counterfactually. This separates gate freeze (good candidates rejected) from proposer exhaustion (Kinetic Theory Prop. 4.3), and decomposes gate regret into a false-accept part (inflation, forgetting) and a false-reject part (missed-opportunity metric from 2609.10873). Freeze rounds and the flip horizon are pre-registered from a pilot. Use 5-8 seeds on the main contrasts, plus one real drifting stream replicating 2610.25858's compound drift. Budget is $400-800.
dossier.history: Round 1: proposed as candidate C6 under topic T2. Original claim: gate ranking flips with horizon (strict statistical gates win at 10 rounds but freeze by 100+, lax gates forget), and a noise-adaptive gate dominates both. Design: 8-10 gates x 2 evolvers, 3 seeds. The critique scored it 62.9 (N2.5 S3 R3.5 C3 F3.5 T4.5) and found the qualitative tradeoff already stated by TRUST, Winner's Curse, 2609.10873 and 2610.25858. It proposed fixes: a predictive resolution law, gate-vs-proposer attribution, a scope/freshness factorial, matched compute, and demoting the adaptive gate to a baseline. Projected score with fixes: about 76. The round-1 REPORT ranked it #15 (score 63) and PARKED it ("TRUST 2611.10787 and Winner's Curse 2610.09239 are close"). Round 2: no v2 proposal and no red-team. Its core mechanism resurfaced in round-2 bold idea #6, 'Drift barrier / error threshold' (74, Promising): defects with effects below the gate's resolution ratchet in. Round 2 also noted a growing consensus that 'gate > artifact' (RSEA, TRUST, Winner's Curse), so improver studies must hold the gate fixed.
dossier.priorScores: R1 critique 62.9 (REPORT rank #15, score 63, parked); projected ~76 if all fixes applied; not re-scored in R2 (related bold idea 'drift barrier / error threshold' scored 74 in R2)

closestPapers.title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement with Statistical Guarantees (TRUST)
closestPapers.summary: The abstract frames RSI gating as a tradeoff: a greedy gate mistakes noise for progress and degenerates, while conservative statistical gates reject beneficial updates. TRUST adapts online multiple-hypothesis testing (FDR control) and uses an LLM to set evidence levels from history. It proves a bound on the share of accepted harmful updates and a lower bound on final gain. On HotpotQA, DROP and APPS, inferior accepts fall from 45.59% (greedy) to 2.78%. The SGM-B/H Bernstein/Hoeffding gates accept almost nothing (gain about 0) over 30 rounds.
closestPapers.relation: States gate-dial's core tradeoff in its abstract and already holds the 'better adaptive gate dominates both' slot. The tasks are stationary and the horizon is 30 rounds, with no drift, forgetting or plasticity attribution. This is why gate-dial was parked and why the 'noise-adaptive gate' arm had to be demoted to a baseline or competitor.

closestPapers.title: The Winner's Curse in LLM Self-Improvement Loops: Selection Noise, Lock-in, and Acceptance Rules
closestPapers.summary: Treats keep-if-better as selection under measurement noise and models correlated candidate errors. With Qwen models rewriting their own instructions and 600 held-out items, most proposals after the first are harmful. Pre-registered runs show greedy selection-set scores exceed held-out accuracy by 13-20 points at 16 selection items and 1-5 points at 256. No tested acceptance rule beat greedy over whole runs.
closestPapers.relation: Closest empirical gate comparison. It names lock-in but does not model its dynamics, uses a stationary distribution and T=20, and measures neither forgetting nor plasticity. Gate-dial's open slot is the long-horizon, drifting extension, plus the resolution-matched (n grows with the round) control that this paper's EB+RM arm suggests.

closestPapers.title: Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?
closestPapers.summary: Evaluates ReasoningBank, GEPA and Meta-Harness on four drifting streams (topic, workflow, domain, compound) built from BIRD, BFCL and ScienceWorld with Gemini 3.6 Flash. It decomposes outcomes into plasticity and stability (interference plus forgetting), and the two are negatively correlated (r=-0.72). Meta-Harness accepts an edit only if it improves validation accuracy on the active sub-block. Shared-prompt rewriting causes cross-task interference and overwrites earlier rules.
closestPapers.relation: Supplies the non-stationary stream and the plasticity/stability metrics gate-dial needs. Per the round-1 critique, its gate-freezing observation is a single ablation: gate strictness is never varied and streams have at most 4 blocks. Gate-dial proposes replicating its compound drift as the external-validity stream.

closestPapers.title: When Validation Stops Learning: Auditing Update Admission for Continual Embodied Agents
closestPapers.summary: Argues that update admission must be judged on both error control and retained learning opportunities at a stated budget. A range-based confidence gate cannot certify unchanged old-task behaviour within substantial budgets. On a constructed pushing diagnostic with 32 seeds, fresh paired checks admit 31.6% of updates versus 0% for the range gate, yet unconditional replay learns better. It proposes a round-level missed-opportunity metric.
closestPapers.relation: Already shows that 'a valid gate can freeze learning', in an embodied toy setting with no LLM. Gate-dial borrows its missed-opportunity metric for the false-reject term of gate regret, and must go beyond it with an LLM-agent, long-horizon, attribution study.

closestPapers.title: A Kinetic Theory of the Gated Self-Evolving LLM Agent
closestPapers.when: Oct 2026, arXiv (under review at ICLR 2027 per round-2 bold check)
closestPapers.summary: Models gated skill self-evolution in a production plugin-based agent as a kinetic system. Its rigorous layer gives an anytime hitting-time certificate, a 'resolution law that prices held-out validation budgets', and a separation theorem: the evaluator must stay outside the population. The kinetic layer is a master equation over plugin x version x task.
closestPapers.relation: Directly relevant to the sharpened claim. It already contains a gate resolution law tied to validation budget, and distinguishes proposal exhaustion from information exhaustion (Prop. 4.3), which gate-dial plans to use as its attribution diagnostic. Gate-dial must show its freeze-round law adds non-stationary, predictive, empirical content beyond this theory, which is scoped to DSH-class plugin populations.

closestPapers.title: Masked Erosion: How Acceptance Gates Lose Redundant Safeguards in Self-Improving Agents
closestPapers.summary: Runs 411 improvement loops under ten gate rules, plus GEPA runs. Gates scoring task success delete redundant safeguards unseen, because a deletion behind another working safeguard adds almost no observable harm. Larger batches let paired tests delete cheaper safeguards. A statistical model frozen before the runs predicts where each gate's protection breaks as safeguard cost and batch size vary.
closestPapers.relation: Methodological template: a frozen, pre-registered predictive law of gate failure versus batch size. That is exactly what gate-dial's resolution law would do for plasticity rather than safety. Its tasks are stationary, plasticity is not measured, and the long horizon is analytic only.

closestPapers.title: PID-Gated Continual Prompt Adaptation Under Noisy Feedback
closestPapers.summary: Introduces proportional, integral and derivative (rollback) gates that decide when an LLM editor rewrites a prompt under drifting tasks and label noise (eta 0-0.2). Tasks are Parity with rule flips, Guess-number and Track-moving-target, at T=120 with 5 seeds on Qwen3-14B/27B. The integral gate matches or beats TextGrad at 2.7-3.5x fewer editor calls and sits on a better cost-quality frontier than TextGrad and GEPA.
closestPapers.relation: Workshop-level version of gate-dial's 'noise-adaptive gate under drift' arm. It uses toy tasks, no statistical gates, no multi-family forgetting and only 3 drift events. It should be a competitor or baseline, and it confirms the method angle is already occupied.

closestPapers.title: Recursive Self-Evolving Agents via Held-Out Selection (RSEA)
closestPapers.summary: Per the round-2 leads file (not fetched this session): RSEA argues that reliability comes from the held-out selection gate, not the artifact. Removing the gate produces a 33-point overfit.
closestPapers.relation: Foundation for the 'gate > artifact' consensus that motivates treating the gate as the main dial. It is a single-point gate-removal ablation with no strictness sweep, horizon or drift.

feedback.point: The qualitative tradeoff 'strict gates freeze, lax gates degrade/forget' is not new: TRUST's abstract, TRUST SGM zero gain, Winner's Curse McNemar losing gain, 2609.10873 Hoeffding admitting 0%, and the 2610.25858 Meta-Harness gate freezing the workspace. A paper headlined on the tradeoff would be scooped in substance. Not a K1 kill.
feedback.addressed: Partly. The sharpened claim moves to the open slots: horizon x non-stationarity, a predictive freeze law, and gate-vs-proposer attribution. There is no v2 in round 2; the idea was parked.

feedback.point: The ranking flip may be trivial or artifactual. Freezing occurs when per-edit effects fall below z_alpha*sigma/sqrt(n), so the flip is a function of the tunable batch size n ('did you just pick n so McNemar freezes?'). It needs a resolution-matched control and an n sweep.
feedback.addressed: Addressed on paper. The resolution law becomes the claim, with an n sweep and a resolution-matched (n grows per round) arm. Not executed.

feedback.point: Evaluation budgets are confounded: sequential e-processes stop early and audits add runs, so rankings are uninterpretable unless total evaluation compute is matched.
feedback.addressed: Addressed in the design: compute-matched gates plus oracle and always-accept bounds.

feedback.point: 'Noise-adaptive gate dominates' turns it into a method paper against 4-6 concurrent methods (TRUST, SAGE, PACE, PID gates), underpowered at 3 seeds. It reads as a recombination of TRUST, PID and resolution matching.
feedback.addressed: Addressed: the adaptive gate is demoted to a simple baseline, TRUST and PID gates become competitors, and the paper is framed as analysis.

feedback.point: External validity: one procedural generator and two evolvers is close to a single benchmark.
feedback.addressed: Addressed on paper: add a real drifting stream (the 2610.25858 compound drift), 2 evolvers x 2 domains, and 5-8 seeds on main contrasts.

feedback.point: Lost plasticity is not attributed. It could be gate rejection, proposer degeneration (Kinetic Theory Prop. 4.3) or workspace bloat. Without counterfactual re-gating of the same candidate stream, the paper cannot claim the gate is the dial.
feedback.addressed: Addressed in the design via counterfactual re-gating under an oracle gate and every other gate. This became the headline of the sharpened claim.

feedback.point: Vary what the gate sees, not only its strictness: a strictness x scope (current vs replay) x freshness factorial. Hypothesis: scope matters more than alpha.
feedback.addressed: Adopted into the latest claim and design.

feedback.point: Partial risk: if no flip appears, the result restates existing 'use paired gates / report held-out' advice.
feedback.addressed: Partly. The fixes are meant to make both outcomes informative, but the null risk remains.

feedback.point: REUSE 2609.33180 was named by the synthesizer but not seen in tool results, so it is unverified.
feedback.addressed: Not resolved. It remains unverified.

feedback.point: Ranked #15 of 19 at score 63 and parked: 'TRUST 2611.10787 and Winner's Curse 2610.09239 are close.'
feedback.addressed: Not addressed. No round-2 proposal, red-team or bold-check exists for gate-dial.

feedback.point: The relevant mechanism is a drift barrier / Muller's ratchet under a noisy gate: defects with effect below gate resolution are invisible to selection. Kinetic Theory 2610.03243 already has a separation theorem; a quantitative law is still open.
feedback.addressed: Not linked explicitly. It overlaps gate-dial's resolution-law fix and could be merged with the round-2 drift-barrier idea (74).

feedback.point: 'Gate > artifact' (RSEA, Feedback Dynamics, TRUST, Winner's Curse) is becoming a consensus. Any improver-scaling claim must hold the gate fixed.
feedback.addressed: Supports gate-dial's premise but also raises crowding. Not acted on.

openRisks: Crowded lane: at least 6 gate-method papers appeared Jun-Nov 2026 (TRUST, PACE, SAGE, PID gates, Anytime-Valid Certificates, SkillEvoReg), and the core tradeoff is already stated in TRUST's abstract.

Kinetic Theory 2610.03243 already contains a 'resolution law that prices held-out validation budgets' and the proposal- vs information-exhaustion distinction. The sharpened claim must show clear empirical and predictive novelty beyond it.
A reviewer may still call it a hyperparameter study of n and alpha. The flip may be fully predictable from effect-size decay, which makes it unsurprising.
Null risk (K2): no horizon flip means the result restates 'use paired gates / report held-out'.
Power: Winner's Curse needed 8 pre-registered seeds and still saw differences within noise. Budget ($400-800) limits seeds and agentic domains.
No round-2 red-team or fact-check was run on this idea, so its novelty status is a round-1 judgement and may be stale. OpenReview-only ICLR 2027 submissions were unchecked in R2.
Possible overlap and merge with the round-2 'drift barrier / error threshold' bold idea, which needs a deliberate decision.

judges.strongest: Counterfactual re-gating of one logged candidate stream is a clean causal design. Combined with oracle and always-accept bounds and splitting gate regret into false-accept and false-reject parts, it can separate gate freeze from proposer exhaustion under long-horizon drift. None of TRUST, Winner's Curse, 2610.25858 or the ICLR 2027 gate papers does this. The scope-versus-alpha factorial is the one hypothesis here that could change practice.
judges.weakest: Each piece of the claim is already taken. Kinetic Theory (arXiv 2610.03243, ICLR 2027 submission 23VDi5bfRj) has the resolution law and the proposal-vs-information-exhaustion distinction. NxGP6PGiaU (Theory of Reliable Self-Evolution) proves that the evaluation cost sets the ceiling. VuzgEFCuwx (Measure First) shows the noise floor matters more than the accept rule and that e-process gates are invalid against a noisy baseline. T04ZzT5m6j proves eventual negative drift under any fixed acceptance rule. TRUST (wV4bK1dHpC) and Statistical Gödel Machines (0FWBc4gY08) take the method slot. The freeze-round prediction z_alpha*sigma/sqrt(n) is close to a tautology once effect-size decay is measured, so a reviewer will call it an n/alpha hyperparameter study. The only open slots left are the drift/plasticity attribution and scope/freshness, and the budget will leave both underpowered.
judges.mustFix:
Do not run this as a standalone paper. Fold it into the round-2 NONOBV-5 drift-barrier / L*(n, epsilon) idea, as the plasticity and non-stationarity arm with counterfactual re-gating. In that merged paper:
1. Make the headline a pre-registered, two-sided test of scope/freshness versus alpha. Do not headline the resolution law.
2. Show that the freeze-round prediction adds something Kinetic Theory 23VDi5bfRj and NxGP6PGiaU do not: out-of-sample prediction across evolvers and drift rates, frozen before the runs, in the style of Masked Erosion.
3. Use TRUST/wV4bK1dHpC, SGM/0FWBc4gY08, REUSE/cnaYLnpsAV and PID gates as baselines, and cite VuzgEFCuwx and T04ZzT5m6j.
4. Power the main contrasts with at least 8 seeds, cut the factorial accordingly, and match evaluation compute.
judges.reviewerQuote: The resolution law is Kinetic Theory's, the strict-gates-freeze tradeoff is in TRUST's abstract, and the noise-floor-dominates-accept-rule finding is ICLR submission VuzgEFCuwx; what remains is a well-instrumented sweep of n, alpha and validation scope on a procedural generator, whose headline prediction follows almost by construction from measured effect-size decay.

judges.strongest: This is the only design I can find that crosses gate strictness with gate scope (current family vs replay) and evidence freshness on a long, drifting stream with hundreds of switches. It also logs every candidate so the same stream can be re-gated counterfactually, which separates gate freeze from proposer exhaustion. TRUST, Winner's Curse, Measure First and Masked Erosion all use stationary tasks over 20-30 rounds. 2610.25858 never varies the gate. 2609.10873 has no LLM. The secondary claim that changing what the gate validates on moves the stability-plasticity frontier more than changing alpha can be tested, and either outcome would be useful.
judges.weakest: The headline mechanism is no longer new. In the ICLR 2027 OpenReview sweep, Kinetic Theory (23VDi5bfRj, 2610.03243) already has a resolution law that prices validation budgets and the proposal vs information exhaustion distinction. 'Theory of Reliable Self-Evolution' (NxGP6PGiaU) ties the self-evolution ceiling to evaluation cost. 'Measure First' (VuzgEFCuwx) shows the noise floor dominates the accept rule. TRUST (wV4bK1dHpC) and Statistical Gödel Machines (0FWBc4gY08) cover the strict-vs-lax tradeoff and the adaptive gate. That leaves a freeze-round law that is close to a restatement of z_alpha*sigma/sqrt(n) applied to effect-size decay, which reviewers will call predictable. The open part (drift x scope/freshness x attribution) is a mash-up of TRUST-style gates, 2610.25858's streams and 2609.10873's missed-opportunity metric (borderline K4). The full factorial (4 strictness x 2 scope x 2 freshness x 2 evolvers x n sweep x 5-8 seeds x 300 rounds, plus a real drift stream) does not fit $400-800 for a solo undergrad.
judges.mustFix:
1. Merge this with the round-2 drift-barrier / NONOBV-5 idea into one paper. The lead question becomes what the gate is blind to under drift: the false-reject term (plasticity) and the false-accept term (ratchet below resolution) as two sides of one resolution law. Do not keep it as a separate gate-strictness paper.
2. Drop 'strict gates freeze' and the resolution law itself as contributions. Cite them as Kinetic Theory 23VDi5bfRj, NxGP6PGiaU, VuzgEFCuwx and TRUST wV4bK1dHpC. Claim only (a) the scope/freshness > alpha result under non-stationarity, and (b) the counterfactual gate-vs-proposer attribution share.
3. Collapse the factorial. Use 2 strictness levels (greedy, TRUST/SGM-as-baseline) x scope x freshness, one cheap evolver (GEPA on an open model) as the main arm, and the code evolver as a single replication. Pre-register the attribution share and the scope-vs-alpha effect size. Match evaluation compute and use 8 seeds on the main contrast.
4. Show that the freeze round does not follow trivially from the measured effect-size decay. Otherwise do not present it as a prediction.
judges.reviewerQuote: The resolution law is z_alpha*sigma/sqrt(n) applied to a decaying effect size, which Kinetic Theory and the reliable-self-evolution theory already formalize. What remains is a well-run but incremental factorial combining TRUST-style gates with the drifting streams of 2610.25858.

judges.strongest: The one slot nobody holds is counterfactual re-gating of a logged candidate stream over a long horizon with hundreds of drift events. It separates gate freeze (good candidates rejected) from proposer exhaustion, and tests whether gate scope and freshness (current-family vs replay, reused vs fresh evidence) move the stability-plasticity frontier more than alpha does. It is cheap ($400-800), uses open models, and produces a reusable logged-candidate artifact.
judges.weakest: The lane is now crowded on both arXiv and ICLR 2027 OpenReview. TRUST (wV4bK1dHpC / 2611.10787) states the strict-vs-lax tradeoff in its abstract. Kinetic Theory (23VDi5bfRj) already has a 'resolution law pricing held-out validation budgets' and the proposal- vs information-exhaustion split. Five ICLR 2027 submissions take further pieces: 'A Theory of Reliable Self-Evolution for Agent Harnesses' (NxGP6PGiaU: the ceiling is set by evaluation cost, and stagnation is diagnosed), 'Measure First: The Noise Floor... Dominates Its Accept Rule' (VuzgEFCuwx: gate resolution is the binding constraint), 'When Self-Reinforcement Ends Self-Improvement' (T04ZzT5m6j: every fixed gate eventually drifts negative), 'Auditing Harness Evolution' (yl1XFtnTn4: an evolved lineage beats one audit-selected edit by nothing detectable at matched budget) and 'Mirage Discoveries' (da1Czy7foS). On top of these, 2609.10873 already shows valid gates freezing, and 2610.25858 already measures plasticity and stability under drift. What remains is the non-stationary extension of a law that is largely already stated. A reviewer can predict the freeze round from effect-size decay, so the result reads as a hyperparameter study of n and alpha.
judges.mustFix: Do not run this as a standalone paper. Merge it into the round-2 drift-barrier / error-threshold idea (74) as its plasticity half. The joint law covers false accepts (defects ratchet in below resolution) and false rejects (freeze below resolution) under one z_alpha*sigma/sqrt(n) account, and you should test it under drift. Make the headline the counterfactual re-gating attribution (gate vs proposer share of lost plasticity) plus the scope/freshness > alpha result, pre-registered from a pilot with frozen predictions in the style of Masked Erosion. Then show explicitly what the law predicts beyond Kinetic Theory (23VDi5bfRj) and NxGP6PGiaU: non-stationary freeze timing and its reset at family switches. Cite and benchmark TRUST, PID gates, REUSE, the 'Measure First' noise-floor audit (VuzgEFCuwx) and T04ZzT5m6j as arms or baselines. Run a pilot first to check that per-edit effect sizes on Dan's generator actually decay into the resolution band within 100-300 rounds. Use at least 8 seeds on the main contrast, since Winner's Curse saw differences within noise at 8.
judges.reviewerQuote: That strict acceptance gates stop admitting edits once effect sizes fall below z_alpha*sigma/sqrt(n) follows directly from power analysis and is already formalized by Kinetic Theory and the Reliable Self-Evolution theory; this paper mainly shows it again on a procedural stream with more drift events.

dossier.title: Cross-Play Audit of Verifier-Harness Co-Evolution: Does Anchoring Keep Co-Evolved Verifiers Honest?
