closestPapers.title: DAEDALUS: Bootstrapping Agent Memory from Self-Generated Tasks
closestPapers.summary: An explorer generates challenging-but-solvable tasks and a solver attempts them. A heuristic derived from each failure is accepted only after repeated success with it in context, and outcomes feed back to adjust task difficulty. Improves mean success by up to 15.9 points over no-memory on AppWorld, τ²-bench and AutomationBench, and is competitive with methods that use real training tasks.
closestPapers.relation: Shows a frontier-calibrated teacher working for a non-parametric memory learner, which contradicts C12's prediction that frontier teachers do poorly for harness and memory learners. Frontier and coverage (its Surveyor) are fused, and there is no cross-substrate teacher ablation. Also the template for the critique's suggested third, memory, substrate.

closestPapers.title: More Rules, Longer Lists? Benchmarking Self-Evolving Agents on a Hidden-Rule Curriculum (CLR-Bench)
closestPapers.summary: A benchmark of hidden-rule chains: each level adds one latent rule over named groupings. Six self-evolution methods (ACE, GEPA, Dynamic Cheatsheet and others) gain at most 5 points over a frozen agent with the certifying model, storing revealed members as exceptions rather than inducing the rule. A stronger model (GPT-6-Sol) lets ACE and DC learn from feedback alone.
closestPapers.relation: Shows harness learners struggle with rule induction, which complicates C12's assumption that harness learners benefit from 'rule coverage'. It is also a candidate for the procedural hidden-rule environment the critique recommends. No teacher comparison and no weight learner.

closestPapers.title: Direct Self-Evolving Optimization: Evolving LLMs without Challenger Training (DEO)
closestPapers.summary: Replaces challenger training with solver-guided task sampling: a frozen LLM generates and mutates tasks, and an approximate Metropolis rule samples from a KL-tilted task distribution scored by the solver. Only the solver is trained. Competitive with R-Zero on reasoning, with a distributional-robustness guarantee for an idealized variant.
closestPapers.relation: A frontier-style teacher for a weight (GRPO) learner on math, covering the weights side of the factorial. No harness learner and no cross-substrate comparison.

closestPapers.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments
closestPapers.summary: An Environment Designer writes executable Gym-style multi-turn environments and is trained on the Reasoning Agent's hint-regret (reward gap with vs without privileged hints), so it targets the edge of the agent's capability. Scaling to 30B, it gains +5.3 on average across 8 held-out benchmarks and +5.7 on BFCL-v4 multi-turn.
closestPapers.relation: Foundation for C12's 'hint-regret' teacher and the canonical weight-side self-play teacher. Per the critique, all 14 of its citing papers are weight-training work and none crosses substrates.

closestPapers.title: When Does Closed-Loop Curriculum Adaptation Help GRPO? An Analysis on Countdown
closestPapers.summary: Proposes CLOSEDLOOPGAUSSIAN, an easy-to-hard Gaussian difficulty sampler whose pace and spread adapt to probe estimates of per-difficulty accuracy. It improves GRPO exact-match on symbolic arithmetic over vanilla and open-loop curricula, with the strongest gains at intermediate difficulty, where group-relative signals are most informative.
closestPapers.relation: Foundation for the gradient-side premise that frontier or medium-difficulty selection helps GRPO because of advantage variance. The critique cites this and related GRPO-curriculum analyses (2610.13669, 2610.19349, 2608.09217) as mixed evidence: even the weight-side premise of C12 is not settled.

feedback.point: Not scooped (K1 not triggered): no paper runs a teacher x learner-substrate factorial. But every individual cell has a 2026 paper (ActiveSaddler, GEPA-Curator, DAEDALUS on the harness/memory side; GRADUS, DEO, SPADE on the weights side). Only the interaction measurement itself is novel.
feedback.addressed: Partially. The critique's sharpened claim reframes the novelty as learner-relative task value with a predictive quantity. No revised proposal was written.

feedback.point: The headline prediction is contradicted by recent work. LP wins for harness learners (ActiveSaddler), a frontier-calibrated generator works for memory learners (DAEDALUS), and coverage wins for GRPO (GRADUS). The likely outcome is a main effect (coverage wins on both substrates), not an interaction.
feedback.addressed: Addressed on paper only: the sharpened claim predicts asymmetric transfer instead of a symmetric flip. Never tested or carried forward.

feedback.point: Teacher definitions are confounded. LP over scenarios differs from LP over failure patterns, and the arm unit swings results by 3–11 pp. The fix is to separate the ranking signal from the ranking unit.
feedback.addressed: Proposed fix: a factorized 2×2(+1) design of signal x unit. Not implemented.

feedback.point: Matched compute across substrates is ill-defined: GRPO needs thousands of rollouts, while GEPA saturates in hundreds. A flip could be a budget-regime or saturation artifact, so learning curves over budget are needed.
feedback.addressed: Proposed fix: budget curves at 2–3 levels. Not implemented.

feedback.point: Underpowered. 5 seeds x 5 teachers x 2 learners on a small benchmark gives CIs of ±4–6 pp, and interactions are smaller than main effects. The likely result is a null that reads as a workshop negative replication.
feedback.addressed: Proposed fixes: a procedural environment with unlimited held-out tasks, a pilot power analysis under $50, and preregistration. Not implemented.

feedback.point: Single benchmark and single model. Ranking flips found on one environment rarely generalize.
feedback.addressed: Proposed fix: a procedural environment plus one real benchmark (τ²-retail or AppWorld), and a third substrate. Not implemented.

feedback.point: No mechanism. Without a measured per-task 'informativeness to learner L' that predicts teacher rankings, the result is an empirical curiosity.
feedback.addressed: Proposed fix 1: per-learner informativeness (GRPO reward variance or advantage norm vs probability of an accepted, attributable edit). Not implemented.

feedback.source: R1 critique (mock review W7 / rubric R=2.5)
feedback.point: Weak relevance to the mentor's agenda: the teacher is external and fixed, and nothing is self-referential or Gödel-Agent-like.
feedback.addressed: Proposed fix 8: a meta-teacher arm, or a self-referential improver that picks its own curriculum per substrate. Not implemented. The idea was parked partly for this reason.

feedback.point: Multi-turn LoRA-GRPO on an 8B agent across 25 runs is heavy infrastructure for a solo undergrad, and 200–400 GPU-hours is optimistic for agentic rollouts.
feedback.addressed: Proposed fix: a procedural environment to make GRPO cheap. Not implemented.

feedback.point: K2 partially at risk: a null on one benchmark is hard to publish. K4 borderline: running known teachers on known learners can read as combining existing things unless a mechanism is contributed.
feedback.addressed: Partially addressed by the reframing toward a predictive quantity and both-outcomes-informative design. Not implemented.

feedback.point: Best used as a section or ablation inside Dan's lead #3 (curriculum-goodhart self-generated curricula) rather than a standalone paper.
feedback.addressed: Done in round 1: the curriculum-goodhart proposal added a harness-vs-LoRA substrate 2×2. Reversed in round 2: curriculum-goodhart v2 cut the weight arm and the weight-vs-harness 2×2 as easily scooped, so the substrate contrast no longer exists anywhere in the active set.

feedback.point: Ranked 16 of 19 at 62 and parked, with no further comment.
feedback.addressed: Not revived in round 2. No round-2 red-team, bold-check or fact-check targeted it.

feedback.point: Self-generated envs and curricula (ActiveSaddler, Task-CoEvolve, RSI-Env, R2Orch, RoboACE) are 'saturated for methods'. The label trend is flat.
feedback.addressed: Not addressed. It reinforces the critique's timing risk (saturation by spring 2027).

openRisks: Existing evidence (ActiveSaddler, DAEDALUS, GRADUS) points against the originally predicted flip. The most likely result is a coverage-teacher main effect, with no interaction.
Arm-granularity confound: any substrate effect may come from the ranking unit (task vs failure pattern), not the learner substrate.
Compute matching across substrates is ill-defined. Harness saturation could create or erase the interaction.
Interaction tests are underpowered on small agent benchmarks, so a null result is likely and hard to publish at the main track.
Weak fit with the mentor's self-referential / Gödel-Agent agenda (R = 2.5).
Multi-turn LoRA-GRPO infrastructure is heavy for a solo undergrad.
Timing: curricula for harness learners is crowded (4+ papers in Oct 2026 alone) and called saturated for methods.
Orphaned: the only round-2 home for the substrate contrast (curriculum-goodhart) dropped it, so reviving it needs a fresh scoop check and a new proposal.

judges.strongest: The one cell nobody has measured is the teacher x learner-substrate interaction: the same teachers run on the same tasks with a GRPO weight learner and a GEPA/ACE harness learner. The ICLR 2027 sweep (about 210 queries) found no submission that runs this factorial. The sharpened version gives a mechanistic, falsifiable quantity: per-learner informativeness (GRPO advantage variance vs the probability of an accepted, attributable edit), and asks whether it predicts teacher rankings. If it does, practitioners get a portable rule for picking a curriculum per substrate. A procedural hidden-rule environment, with exact coverage and unlimited held-out tasks, would make the result clean.
judges.weakest: Every individual cell is already a 2026 paper. ActiveSaddler, now confirmed as an ICLR 2027 submission (xmpyzuagpu), shows an LP teacher winning for harness learners. GEPA-Curator and DAEDALUS cover curation and frontier selection for harness and memory learners. GRADUS shows a coverage teacher winning for GRPO. METIS (QXchTWdOPg, ICLR 2027) already uses predicted reward variance as the curriculum signal for weight learners. One Policy, Many Harnesses (4KSNZln9nS) shows RL gains are harness-specific and transfer asymmetrically. So the likely outcome is a coverage main effect with a small, underpowered interaction, which reads as a K2/K4 'combine known teachers with known learners' paper. Compute matching across substrates is ill-defined: GRPO needs thousands of rollouts, while GEPA saturates in hundreds. The arm-unit confound (task vs failure pattern, which swings results by 3–11 pp) can produce or erase any 'flip'. Fit with the self-referential agenda is weak because the teacher is external. Multi-turn LoRA-GRPO across substrates, seeds and budgets is beyond a solo undergrad's 6-month budget. The weight-harness lane has 12+ ICLR 2027 method submissions and is called saturated. The idea is orphaned: curriculum-goodhart v2 already cut this contrast as easy to scoop.
judges.mustFix:
Do not revive this as a standalone paper. Fold the substrate contrast into the learning-to-goodhart ΔTR idea, which the sweep says is the only defensible unclaimed substrate contrast. Or fold it into Blind-Spot Hiding as an ActiveSaddler-arm ablation. If it is kept at all:
(1) Factorize ranking signal (frontier / LP / coverage) x ranking unit (task vs failure pattern), and run ActiveSaddler (ICLR 2027 xmpyzuagpu) and a METIS-style variance-predictor (QXchTWdOPg) as named arms.
(2) Preregister the asymmetric-transfer prediction and the informativeness-predicts-ranking test. Run a pilot under $50 for power on a procedural hidden-rule environment (CLR-Bench-style), plus one real benchmark (τ²-retail).
(3) Replace matched compute with budget curves at 3 levels, and report a teacher-transfer regret test (tune on A, deploy on B).
(4) Cite and position against ActiveSaddler, GEPA-Curator, GRADUS, DAEDALUS, METIS, One Policy Many Harnesses (4KSNZln9nS) and What Actually Evolves (ecw2VvTeE5).
(5) Add a self-selected-curriculum (meta-teacher) arm to fit the self-referential agenda.
judges.reviewerQuote: Each teacher and each learner here is drawn from existing 2026 work (ActiveSaddler, GRADUS, GEPA-Curator, METIS), and the claimed teacher x substrate interaction is smaller than the coverage main effect and within run variance at 5 seeds, so the paper amounts to a careful replication grid, not a new insight about learner-relative task value.

judges.strongest: No ICLR 2027 submission and no arXiv paper runs one teacher set across both a gradient learner and a reflective harness learner. The ICLR sweep (Nov 12) found nothing on teacher x substrate, and it says substrate contrasts on matched experience are still unclaimed. That leaves a clean measurement gap: a per-learner informativeness quantity (GRPO reward variance vs the probability of an accepted, attributable edit) that would predict which teacher ranking carries over to which substrate. The asymmetric-transfer prediction can be falsified, and a teacher-transfer regret number would be useful in practice to anyone who tunes curricula on one substrate and deploys on another.
judges.weakest: The framing is no longer fresh, and existing evidence points to a main effect, not an interaction. Liu, Yin and Han, "Useful to Whom? The Easy-versus-Coverage Boundary Moves with the Learner" (arXiv 2610.00221, Sep 2026; my alphaXiv search found it and the dossier missed it), already makes "a sample's value belongs to the learner" its headline, using a frozen-subset design (vision only, but reviewers will see it as the same conceptual claim). The ICLR 2027 submission FPaMYO47j4 (Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling) already crosses harness and weights and finds that process failures go to the harness and content failures to the weights. That is a partial version of "harness and weights value different tasks". Also relevant on ICLR 2027: IXnpSW8g3v (TAME, harness rank reversal) and QXchTWdOPg (METIS, variance-based curricula). ActiveSaddler (an LP teacher wins on harnesses), DAEDALUS (a frontier teacher works for memory) and GRADUS (coverage wins for GRPO) together suggest that coverage teachers win on both substrates. Every cell of the design is a 2026 paper, so if no strong interaction shows up the result reads as K4 (combining known teachers with known learners). Matching compute across GRPO and GEPA is ill-defined. The self-referential angle is weak. Multi-turn LoRA-GRPO across 30+ runs is heavy for a solo undergrad.
judges.mustFix:
Do not revive this as a standalone paper. Fold the teacher x substrate contrast in as one section of the learning-to-goodhart matched-substrate (ΔTR) paper, which needs the same LoRA-vs-harness-on-identical-experience infrastructure. The sweep says that substrate contrast is the only defensible framing still unclaimed. If it is ever run, it must do the following:
- Cite "Useful to Whom" (2610.00221) and present this as the agentic, cross-substrate extension of a known phenomenon. Cite FPaMYO47j4, IXnpSW8g3v and METIS (QXchTWdOPg).
- Factorize the teachers as ranking signal x ranking unit (task vs failure pattern), with an ActiveSaddler arm.
- Use a procedural hidden-rule environment where coverage is measured exactly (CLR-Bench style).
- Report budget curves rather than a single matched-compute point.
- Preregister the interaction test, with a pilot power analysis under $50.
- Make the per-learner informativeness quantity the contribution. It must predict teacher rankings out of sample; showing a ranking flip is not enough.
judges.reviewerQuote: Prior work already establishes that data value is learner-relative, and ActiveSaddler, DAEDALUS and GRADUS each show their teacher working on its own substrate, so a matrix of known curricula crossed with known learners, which in the end finds coverage helps everyone, does not tell us anything new about self-improving agents.

judges.strongest: The ICLR 2027 sweep (Nov 12) found no submission that runs the teacher x learner-substrate factorial, so K1 is not triggered. The one real asset is a substrate-relative predictive quantity: reward variance or advantage norm for GRPO versus the probability of an accepted, attributable edit for GEPA/ACE. It can be falsified on a procedural hidden-rule environment where coverage is exact, and both outcomes are informative. If teacher value turns out to be learner-invariant, that is a useful result for the growing curriculum-method lane (ActiveSaddler, DAEDALUS, GRADUS, METIS).
judges.weakest: The novelty is only in the interaction. Every cell of the grid is already a 2026 paper, and the ICLR 2027 queue covers more of it. ActiveSaddler (xmpyzuagpu) is now a confirmed ICLR submission in which LP over failure patterns wins for harnesses. METIS (QXchTWdOPg) already uses within-prompt reward variance to allocate training, which is the gradient half of the predictive quantity. 'Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling' (FPaMYO47j4) already argues that process failures belong to the harness and content failures to the weights, which is a learner-relative account of task value. TAME (IXnpSW8g3v) has a 'rank reversal' finding across substrates. 'What Actually Evolves' (ecw2VvTeE5) shows that proposer teachers barely matter for weight learners. Prior evidence (GRADUS, DAEDALUS, ActiveSaddler) points to a coverage main effect rather than an interaction. The interaction test is underpowered, and compute cannot be cleanly matched between GRPO and GEPA. Multi-turn LoRA-GRPO across 3 substrates x 6 teachers x seeds x budget levels is too much for one undergrad in 6 months. Mentor fit is weak because the teacher is external and fixed, so nothing in the design is self-referential.
judges.mustFix: Do not revive this as a standalone paper. Fold the substrate contrast into the learning-to-goodhart ΔTR idea. The sweep names that idea's matched text-vs-weight substrate contrast as its only unclaimed headline, and it needs the same procedural hidden-rule environment, the same LoRA-GRPO arm and the same GEPA arm. Inside it, add one preregistered test: does per-task informativeness to learner L (advantage norm for GRPO, P(accepted attributable edit) for GEPA) predict cross-substrate teacher-transfer regret? Only factorized teachers count: signal (frontier / LP / coverage) x unit (task / failure pattern). Run it at 2 budget levels with a pilot power analysis under $50. Cite and position against these ICLR 2027 submissions: ActiveSaddler xmpyzuagpu, METIS QXchTWdOPg, FPaMYO47j4, TAME IXnpSW8g3v, ecw2VvTeE5 and RepRSI zxN7uhwRY0. If it stays standalone, it needs a self-referential arm, a meta-agent that picks its own curriculum per substrate, to earn mentor fit. Otherwise park it.
judges.reviewerQuote: Each cell of this teacher-by-learner grid has already been published, the predicted interaction is contradicted by ActiveSaddler, DAEDALUS and GRADUS, and the cross-substrate compute matching is ill-defined, so I cannot tell whether the reported (non-)interaction reflects the learner or simply the budget regime and arm granularity.

dossier.title: Self-Concealing Erosion: Cost-Aware Improvers Prune the Checks Their Own Gates Depend On (originally C9 "Masked erosion of the improver")
dossier.claim: Latest version is the critique's sharpened claim; the idea was never revised after it. When an improver's own verification layers (regression checks, replay, two-pass confirmation) produce the evidence its acceptance gate scores, cost-aware self-improvement of the kind the RSI Tax recommends prunes those layers within about 10 generations. The loss is self-concealing: the gate-visible score rises while frozen-verifier held-out gain falls. Masked Erosion's margin-aware one-layer-ablation audit fails unless it runs on a verifier outside the improver's write access.
dossier.design: Original round-1 design: VERSE-style improvers seeded with 3-4 redundant verification layers, run under greedy, paired and margin-aware meta-gates for about 10 generations, with 2 models and 3 seeds. Metrics were layer survival, the solver's false-acceptance rate and held-out gain. The critique's revised design (its fixes, never written up as a proposal) has five parts. (1) Build a full 16-subset lattice over the improver's checks to define "masked" and "margin". (2) Make deletion pressure natural with a cost-aware gate (accuracy minus λ·tokens, sweeping λ) instead of planting deletions. (3) Track, per generation, the gap between the gate-visible score and a frozen external held-out score. (4) Compare margin-aware gates using an internal audit vs an external frozen verifier vs a frozen-verifier baseline (VERSE's own choice). (5) Run at least 60 loops per arm for 15-20 generations on a cheap procedural tau-style or AppWorld/Polyglot testbed, with 2 open model families plus a model-swap test, and add free self-modification loops (Gödel Agent / Hyperagents style) audited with the 2609.00069 tampering taxonomy.
dossier.history: Round 1: this was C9 in topic T3. It proposed the Masked Erosion mechanism applied to improver verification layers, motivated by "verification is 75-94% of RSI cost". The critique scored it 55/100 (PARK). The reasons: Masked Erosion (2610.38392, published two weeks earlier) already has the same gate comparison, the same dose-response finding and the same margin-aware fix, and the cost premise was mis-cited. The critique proposed reframing around self-concealing erosion plus a cost-aware arm, with an estimated 74.6 if fixes 1-3 land. REPORT ranked it 19th of 19 ("park; Masked Erosion and RSI Tax cover it"). No proposal was written. Round 2: the idea was not carried forward. There is no v2 proposal, red-team or bold-check for it. Round 2 kept citing Masked Erosion as the reference "gate cannot see it" mechanism for other ideas (useful-fictions, interference-plateau, canalization, curriculum-goodhart). The field forecast lists Goodhart in self-evolving loops as "accelerating", with medium-high scoop risk.
dossier.priorScores: R1 55.0 (park); critique's estimate if reframed with fixes 1-3: 74.6. Not re-scored in R2 (dropped).

closestPapers.title: Masked Erosion: How Acceptance Gates Lose Redundant Safeguards in Self-Improving Agents
closestPapers.summary: Measures harm for every subset of four written safeguards in two agent environments, across 411 improvement loops under ten gate rules plus three GEPA runs. Deleting a safeguard that another working safeguard covers adds almost no observable harm, so redundancy erodes unseen. Paired tests block deletions that pass by chance but not ones that genuinely raise task success, and larger batches let gates delete cheaper safeguards. The lost depth turns into harm under a weaker model. A frozen statistical model predicts where each gate breaks, and freezing safety text or auditing one-layer ablations preserves depth.
closestPapers.relation: This is the near-scoop. It already has the mechanism, the gate comparison (greedy/paired/margin-aware), the cost dose-response and the fix. It does not cover layers inside the improver that the gate reads from, because its harm audit is external and fixed. The only defensible delta is self-concealment, where deleting a check biases the gate's own measurement, and showing that its margin-aware fix fails when the audit is internal.

closestPapers.title: VERSE: Verified Self-Evolving Optimizer for Agent Harnesses
closestPapers.summary: The optimizer self-evolves its own prompts, skills, tools, hooks and notes along with the executor harness, using execution-based verification (test draft edits, replay failures, perturb steps). Self-evolution without verification fails; with it, VERSE improves four harness optimizers on held-out SWE-rebench and out-of-distribution tasks (best 42.3% vs 39.2%).
closestPapers.relation: This is the testbed template and the gap. VERSE's verification tools are frozen by design, so nobody has tested whether a self-evolving optimizer would prune checks it can edit. The critique notes verification costs only 2-7% of agent runs here, which undercuts the original cost-pressure premise. A VERSE run is also expensive (about 20-47 h).

closestPapers.title: The RSI Tax: When Recursive Self-Improvement Is Not Worth the Cost
closestPapers.summary: Defines the RSI Tax as the token cost of the self-improvement process and evaluates it on continual task streams. A bounded-note baseline matches Meta-Harness, EvoSkill and RRSI at 65.6-71.0% lower total tokens. Verification is 74.8-93.6% of the RSI Tax, and the paper calls for objectives that jointly optimize RSI cost and task cost.
closestPapers.relation: This was the source of the mis-cited premise. Its 'verification' is the gate's own validation, not checks inside the improver. The reframe instead uses its recommendation to cut verification cost as the natural cost-aware pressure: the headline would be that following the RSI Tax advice makes improvers prune their own checks.

closestPapers.title: Auditing Harness Tampering in Self-Improving Agents
closestPapers.summary: Introduces 'harness tampering' (illusory gains or violated integrity obligations such as completeness) and a two-axis taxonomy (functional role x obligation). It builds an annotated corpus of seeded tampered/benign edits, benchmarks audit methods, and audits real DGM and Hyperagents runs, finding that tampering occurs consistently and persists in the best lineage.
closestPapers.relation: This supports the premise that meta-level evaluation code does get eroded in the wild (the critique cites 63-85% of iterations, and 59% of Hyperagents findings in evaluation code). It is descriptive only: no controlled redundancy and no gate comparison. Its taxonomy is proposed as the audit tool for the natural self-modification arm.

closestPapers.title: Recoverability and Verifier Strength: Two Measured Preconditions for Unattended Agent Self-Improvement
closestPapers.summary: Defines verifier strength (agreement with a trusted reference verifier) and recoverability, and uses them as a rule for which self-improvement steps may run unattended. It finds LLM-judge gates can give constant scores (9/37 settings) while looking healthy, and that only changes whose old version is kept can be reliably undone.
closestPapers.relation: Adjacent: it treats the verifier as fixed and measures its strength once. The self-concealment claim is about verifier strength decaying endogenously when the improver can edit it, so this paper's sigma metric could serve as the gate-vs-reference gap measure.

closestPapers.title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement with Statistical Guarantees (TRUST)
closestPapers.summary: Adapts online multiple hypothesis testing to control the rate of false evolution across RSI rounds, with an LLM deciding how much evidence is needed. It reduces accepted inferior updates from the greedy gate's 45.59% to 2.78% on HotpotQA, DROP and APPS, with a lower bound on final gain.
closestPapers.relation: A gate-statistics baseline. Its guarantees assume the gate's measurement is unbiased. If self-concealing erosion holds, an improver that edits its own checks breaks this assumption, so TRUST-style gates could be an additional arm.

closestPapers.title: Compositional Safety Failures in Harness Evolution: Identification and Runtime Monitoring
closestPapers.summary: Shows that individually safe, utility-preserving component updates can interact to produce unsafe behavior: 43 pairwise and 18 irreducible 3-way failures across three safety benchmarks. It proposes a typed hypergraph for incremental runtime monitoring of these interactions.
closestPapers.relation: Related in spirit (gates miss interactions among components) but not about verification redundancy, deletion or gates. It is the analogue for why a subset lattice is needed.

closestPapers.title: Gödel Agent: A Self-Referential Agent Framework for Recursive Self-Improvement
closestPapers.summary: A self-referential framework in which an LLM agent dynamically modifies its own logic and behavior, guided only by high-level objectives, without fixed optimization routines. It shows continuous self-improvement on math reasoning and agent tasks.
closestPapers.relation: Foundation (mentor's own work). It supplies the self-referential setting in which an improver can rewrite its own verification code, and it is the proposed base for the natural self-modification arm.

feedback.point: Masked Erosion 2610.38392 already establishes masked deletion, paired-gate behavior, cost dose-response, the batch-size effect, a frozen predictive simulator and the margin-aware fix. As pitched, the idea is 'Masked Erosion x VERSE', a replication in a new domain (K4 partial).
feedback.addressed: Only on paper. The critique's sharpened claim moves to self-concealing erosion, but no revised proposal was written and the idea was parked.

feedback.point: The '75-94% of RSI cost is verification' figure (RSI Tax) refers to the acceptance gate's own validation runs, not checks inside the improver. In VERSE the improver's verification costs only 2-7% of agent runs, so the deletion pressure is not established.
feedback.addressed: Reframed in the critique: use an RSI-Tax-style cost-aware objective (sweep λ) as natural pressure. Never implemented.

feedback.point: Improver verification layers are not clean, independently sufficient barriers. Without a full subset lattice, 'masked' is undefined.
feedback.addressed: Fix proposed (16-subset lattice over 3-4 checks). Not implemented.

feedback.point: 2 models x 3 seeds x 3 gates for about 10 generations is underpowered for rare false-acceptance events, compared with Masked Erosion's 411 loops.
feedback.addressed: Fix proposed: at least 60 loops per arm, 15-20 generations, 2 model families plus a model swap, on a cheap procedural testbed. Not implemented.

feedback.point: If the result is 'margin-aware works here too', either outcome reads as confirmation and looks like a workshop paper.
feedback.addressed: Addressed in the sharpened claim by testing whether the margin-aware audit fails when it uses internal measurement. Untested.

feedback.point: No frozen-verifier arm (VERSE's choice), no natural unplanted loops, and no cost-aware objective.
feedback.addressed: All three were added to the critique's fix list (frozen-verifier baseline, Gödel/Hyperagents-style free loops audited with the 2609.00069 taxonomy, cost-aware λ sweep). Not implemented.

feedback.point: VERSE on SWE-rebench costs about 20-47 h per run, so a lighter testbed is needed.
feedback.addressed: A procedural tau-style or AppWorld/Polyglot subset with 7-30B open models was suggested.

feedback.point: The window is narrowing, and the Masked Erosion authors (So et al.) could release a follow-up.
feedback.addressed: Not addressed. This is an open risk.

feedback.point: Ranked 19th of 19 at 55, park: 'Masked Erosion 2610.38392 and RSI Tax 2611.13524 cover it.'
feedback.addressed: Accepted. The idea was dropped.

feedback.source: R2 (indirect: field_forecast, bold-checks on other ideas)
feedback.point: Round 2 has no direct feedback on this idea. Masked Erosion is repeatedly treated as the canonical 'gate cannot see it' erosion paper, and Goodhart in self-evolving loops is forecast as accelerating with medium-high scoop risk ('expect gate-design-for-self-improvers papers in Q1 2027').
feedback.addressed: N/A (idea not carried into round 2).

openRisks: Masked Erosion (2610.38392) pre-empts most of the mechanism and the fix. Novelty depends entirely on self-concealment showing up as a measurable gap between gate-visible and frozen held-out scores.
If no self-concealment gap appears, the result is a transfer of Masked Erosion's defences: a clean negative result, but probably workshop-level.
Deletion pressure may not arise naturally: improver verification is only 2-7% of agent runs in VERSE, so even with a cost-aware objective, pruning may not happen within about 10-20 generations.
Construct validity: improver checks (regression, replay, perturbation, two-pass) may not be independently sufficient, which makes the subset lattice messy.
Power: false-acceptance events may be rare, so at least 60 loops per arm are needed. VERSE-scale runs are expensive (about 20-47 h each), so a cheap proxy testbed is required.
Scoop risk from the Masked Erosion, tampering-audit and RSI Tax groups, given the Oct-Nov 2026 wave of audit papers and the forecast of gate-design papers in Q1 2027.
The idea was not re-examined in round 2. The revised 74.6 estimate is untested by any red-team or fresh scoop check.

judges.strongest: The one new piece is the claim that if the improver can edit the checks that produce its gate's evidence, the margin-aware audit Masked Erosion proposes should fail. That audit reads the improver's own measurements, and deleting a check biases those measurements. This is a clear, falsifiable test of what that paper's fix assumes. It fits the mentor's self-referential agenda directly: Gödel Agent rewrites its own verification code, and 2609.00069 already shows tampering in evaluation code in real DGM and Hyperagents runs.
judges.weakest:
The idea is squeezed from two sides. Masked Erosion (2610.38392) already covers masked deletion, the comparison of greedy, paired and margin-aware gates, the cost dose-response and the fix. The ICLR 2027 sweep (Nov 12) shows the "self-concealing" headline (the in-loop score rises while the frozen or held-out score falls) is now crowded. Five submissions are close:
- The Harness Learns to Lie While Evolving (5lWjRTK6Vk): false success rises round over round of harness self-evolution, and it proposes the VHE fix.
- Feedback Alignment in Self-Improving Agents (C6EElQ2PRG): the visible score V rises while the held-out target T falls.
- False Frontiers (Id4G8bzzKO): the in-loop reward rises while external correctness falls, and out-of-fold feedback fixes it.
- When the Evaluator Changes (tn4eslVXEK).
- Auditing Harness Evolution (yl1XFtnTn4): one accepted guard persists without ever firing in 3,960 checks. This is the opposite of the pruning premise and is evidence that guards are not under deletion pressure.

What is left is a narrow mechanism: cost-aware pruning of the improver's own checks. Its premise is weak, because improver verification is 2-7% of agent runs in VERSE. Pruning may never happen naturally in 15-20 generations, and a null result just transfers Masked Erosion to a new setting, which is workshop-level. None of the critique's fixes (lattice, λ sweep, 60+ loops per arm) were ever written up or red-teamed.
judges.mustFix:
1. Before any build, run a cheap pilot on the procedural testbed. Use the cost-aware gate (accuracy minus λ·tokens) and sweep λ. Require natural pruning of at least one improver check in at least 30% of loops by generation 15. If this gate fails, drop the idea.
2. Position the paper explicitly against these sources and state its single delta: the evidence-producing check sits inside the improver's write access, and internal vs external audit is compared at matched λ.
   - Masked Erosion 2610.38392
   - The Harness Learns to Lie While Evolving, 5lWjRTK6Vk (ICLR 2027)
   - Feedback Alignment in Self-Improving Agents, C6EElQ2PRG (ICLR 2027)
   - False Frontiers, Id4G8bzzKO (ICLR 2027)
   - Auditing Harness Evolution, yl1XFtnTn4 (ICLR 2027)
3. Build the 16-subset lattice so that "masked" is defined.
4. Run at least 60 loops per arm with 2 open model families and a model swap.
5. Include TRUST and VHE as gate baselines.

Better still, fold this in as the "editable-verifier" arm of the useful-fictions or NONOBV-5 mutator idea rather than running it as a standalone paper.
judges.reviewerQuote: Once Masked Erosion and the ICLR 2027 papers showing in-loop scores diverging from held-out scores (The Harness Learns to Lie, Feedback Alignment, False Frontiers) are accounted for, the remaining contribution reduces to whether one specific class of check gets pruned under an imposed token penalty, and the paper does not show that this pressure arises naturally.

judges.strongest: The one new piece is self-concealment. When the improver can edit the checks that produce the gate's evidence, deleting a check biases the gate's own measurement. Masked Erosion (2610.38392) does not cover this because its harm audit is external and fixed. VERSE (2610.02616) freezes its verification tools, so it has not tested it either. A result showing that the margin-aware fix fails when the audit is internal and holds when the verifier is frozen and outside the improver's write access would give a concrete design rule for Gödel-Agent-style self-referential improvers.
judges.weakest: Most of the idea is already published. Masked Erosion 2610.38392 has the deletion mechanism, the greedy/paired/margin-aware gate comparison, the cost dose-response and the fix. The ICLR 2027 sweep then takes the self-concealment headline. "The Harness Learns to Lie While Evolving" (openreview 5lWjRTK6Vk) shows false success rising round over round of harness self-evolution. Its VHE fix scores from execution traces rather than the agent's self-report, which is close to this idea's "external verifier" fix. "Feedback Alignment in Self-Improving Agents" (C6EElQ2PRG) shows the visible score rising while the held-out target falls. "Auditing Harness Evolution" (yl1XFtnTn4) finds an accepted guard that never fires in 3,960 checks. Tampering in DGM/Hyperagents evaluation code is also already documented in 2609.00069. Cost-aware RSI methods already exist on arXiv: HarnessPro 2610.26770 (performance-cost Pareto) and HarnessMM 2610.32813 (harness token efficiency). Either may already report pruned verification. The premise is also weak: improver verification costs only 2-7% of agent runs, so natural deletion pressure may never appear within 15-20 generations. What remains is "Masked Erosion x VERSE, plus a gap metric", and it has never been through a red-team.
judges.mustFix:
1. Before building anything, run a cheap 2-week pilot. Take HarnessPro, HarnessMM or an RSI-Tax-style λ·tokens objective, let the improver edit its own checks, and test whether it actually deletes them within 10-15 generations. If it does not, drop the idea.
2. Make the claim the internal-vs-external audit contrast: the gap between the gate-visible score and a frozen-verifier score, plus the result that the margin-aware audit works only outside the improver's write access. Cite 5lWjRTK6Vk (VHE) and C6EElQ2PRG explicitly and set them apart. VHE's trace-based reward should be a baseline arm.
3. Build the 16-subset lattice, run at least 60 loops per arm on a cheap procedural testbed with 2 open model families, and add TRUST-style and frozen-verifier gates as arms.
4. Better still, fold this in as the cost-pressure / self-concealment arm of a broader gate-design or Goodhart-in-self-evolution paper rather than running it standalone.
judges.reviewerQuote: Masked Erosion already established that acceptance gates silently erode redundant safeguards, and concurrent work (EvoTrap/VHE, Feedback Alignment) already shows gate-visible scores diverging from ground truth in harness self-evolution, so the remaining contribution — that this also happens when the safeguards live inside the improver — reads as an incremental transfer rather than a new phenomenon.

judges.strongest: This idea sits squarely in the mentor's agenda. In a Gödel-Agent-style self-referential setting, the improver can edit the very checks its acceptance gate reads. There is one specific delta no published paper tests directly: following the RSI Tax's cost-cutting advice (a cost-aware λ·tokens objective) might make an improver prune its own internal verification layers, while the gate-visible score hides the loss. It is a clean, mechanistic, falsifiable experiment, and it could run cheaply on a procedural testbed with open 7-30B models.
judges.weakest: Every part of the claim is now covered. Masked Erosion (2610.38392) has the masked-deletion mechanism, the gate comparison, the cost dose-response and the margin-aware fix. The ICLR 2027 sweep adds three more close submissions. Feedback Alignment in Self-Improving Agents (openreview C6EElQ2PRG) already shows the self-concealment signature: visible score V rises while held-out T falls, with retained scaffolds encoding evaluator-specific checking rules. Kinetic Theory of the Gated Self-Evolving Agent (23VDi5bfRj) proves a separation theorem that the evaluator must stay outside the population, which is the "audit fails unless external" claim. A Theory of Reliable Self-Evolution (NxGP6PGiaU) ties the ceiling to verification cost. Auditing Harness Evolution (yl1XFtnTn4) and The Harness Learns to Lie (5lWjRTK6Vk) cover guard persistence and false success rising each round. What remains is roughly Masked Erosion x VERSE x RSI Tax (K4). The premise is also shaky: improver verification is only 2-7% of run cost, so cost-aware pruning may never appear. If it does not, the null is unpublishable.
judges.mustFix: Do not run this as a standalone paper. If anything survives, fold it in as one pre-registered arm of the NONOBV-5 self-referential L* / mutator idea or the learning-to-goodhart idea. That arm would ask: under a λ-swept cost-aware objective, does an improver with write access to its own checks prune them? Track gate-visible minus frozen-verifier held-out gap per generation, with Masked Erosion's margin-aware audit run internally vs externally. Before writing any code, run a 2-week pilot showing natural pruning appears within 15 generations at any λ (kill the arm if not). Position it explicitly against Masked Erosion 2610.38392, Feedback Alignment C6EElQ2PRG, Kinetic Theory 23VDi5bfRj (separation theorem), NxGP6PGiaU, yl1XFtnTn4, 5lWjRTK6Vk, TRUST wV4bK1dHpC and the tampering taxonomy 2609.00069. The only claim worth making is the internal-vs-external audit failure, measured with an endogenous verifier-strength decay curve (sigma from 2610.27465). Do not claim visible-vs-held-out divergence as new.
judges.reviewerQuote: The visible-vs-held-out divergence is already reported by Feedback Alignment in Self-Improving Agents, the "evaluator must stay outside the improver" result is a theorem in the Kinetic Theory paper, and the masked-deletion mechanism with its margin-aware fix is Masked Erosion's, so this submission reads as a recombination of the three in a new testbed rather than a new finding.

dossier.title: The Winner's Curse One Level Up: Selection Noise in Improver Selection and Open-Ended Archives (meta-winners-curse)
dossier.claim: When self-improvers (meta-agents) are chosen on a handful of meta-tasks, held-out same-start swap tests recover only a fraction of the improver gain the selection scores report. The missing part comes from an improver × meta-task interaction term, which adding more items per task does not remove. Executed placebo-operator archives match much of the gain of DGM/HGM-style archives at equal evaluation budget. HGM's clade-metaproductivity (CMP) ranks improvers barely above chance. A meta-held-out split by task family, plus two-level shrinkage, restores calibration and flips at least one published "improving-at-improving" result. (This is the sharpened version from the round-1 critique. The original fixed thresholds — more than 2× overstatement below 10 meta-tasks, placebo reproducing at least 40% of gains, rho < 0.3 — were recommended for removal.)
dossier.design:
1. Generate many improver revisions per generation and score each two ways: on its few selection meta-tasks, and on a large held-out meta-task pool using paired same-start swaps. Mix in planted positive-control improvers whose effect is known (oracle-hint and degraded improvers).
2. Fit a two-level variance decomposition: improver effect + improver × meta-task interaction + object-task noise + incumbent lock-in. Derive a meta-task budget rule from it.
3. Run executed (not simulated) placebo archives in DGM-style and HGM-style search on an open model, at matched evaluation budget with at least 5 seeds. Use three nulls: semantically null code edits, a shuffled-feedback editor, and random revert to an ancestor.
4. Validate CMP and parent-potential proxies against a "metaproductivity oracle": K fresh fixed-budget expansions for each of about 30–50 nodes, reported with a split-half reliability ceiling.
5. Re-audit 3–4 published meta-level claims (Hyperagents imp@k transfer, AIDE² ignition, MetaRSI) using the meta-held-out protocol, and release the protocol as a "MetaAudit" package.
Estimated cost: $400–1k.
dossier.history:
Round 1: started as candidate C7 (topic T3). It moved Dan's "confound battery" idea up to the improver level and merged in the eval-rigor sweep's "placebo archives" idea (Idea 4) and the improver-scaling sweep's "meta-level winner's curse" idea (Idea D).
- The critique scored it about 59–60/100 (N 2.0, S 2.5, R 4.0, C 3.0, F 3.5, T 4.5), with K1-partial and K2-risk flags.
- The final round-1 ranking put it at #18 (score 60), with the verdict "→ #1 placebo appendix": it is not standalone, and it was folded into the lead paper (Effect, Cause, Decay).
- Round 2: it got no v2 proposal, red-team pass or bold-check of its own. Only traces survive in the lead paper:
  - effect-cause-decay.v2 pre-registers the incumbent Pk (not the archive best) to avoid building in a winner's curse.
  - Placebo/shuffled memory was cut to appendix-if-money-is-left. The placebo evaluator was explicitly deferred as "its own paper".
  - verify/leads-b Idea C ("selection regret across improver generations": gen-k improvers generate better but select worse, a winner's curse that grows with archive size) was proposed as a readout for #1's Effect arm.
- Net: demoted to an appendix/readout, with a possible later standalone paper.
dossier.priorScores: R1 critique 60.0 (text says ~59) → R1 final rank #18 / 60, merged into #1 as placebo appendix; no R2 score (not re-scored as a standalone in round 2).

closestPapers.title: The Winner's Curse in LLM Self-Improvement Loops: Selection Noise, Lock-in, and Acceptance Rules
closestPapers.summary: Treats keep-if-better as selection under measurement noise with correlated candidate errors. Qwen models rewrite their own instructions, and every candidate is also scored on 600 held-out items. Most proposals after the first are harmful. With 16 selection items, greedy loops' final selection-set score exceeds held-out accuracy by 13–20 pts; with 256 items the gap is 1–5 pts. The tested acceptance rules do not beat greedy over whole runs.
closestPapers.relation: The object-level version of this idea. It covers instruction artifacts on TREC/Banking77/GSM8K only and explicitly excludes agentic/code tasks and RSI. It has no improver (meta) selection, no archive/tree search and no placebo operator. This idea is 'the same statistics one level up', and reviewers may frame it as '2610.09239 applied to HGM'. The authors could plausibly extend into it.

closestPapers.title: Does Failure Feedback Direct Agent Self-Modification?
closestPapers.summary: Measures whether self-modifications specifically repair the targeted failure. Across 145 modifications in public Darwin Gödel Machine logs it finds no target-specific advantage. Controlled instruction-revision experiments with small open models show target feedback can raise repair (+20 pp for Qwen3-4B), but target repair does not reliably imply held-out improvement. Per the round-1 critique's deep read, a zero-mean-edit simulation run under DGM's parent sampling and admission rules reproduces DGM's archive maxima, and parent quality does not predict edit gain.
closestPapers.relation: Pre-empts this idea's DGM-log reanalysis and its 'archive gains are selection on noise' headline (K1-partial). It leaves open: executed (not simulated) placebo archives, HGM/CMP, and held-out improver swaps.

closestPapers.title: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution
closestPapers.summary: Evaluates four harness-evolution methods on general and coding tasks using repeated evaluations, controlled agent expansion, component interventions and admission replays. All 16 evolved agents gain new tasks while losing previously covered ones. The highest-scoring agent never gives the largest mean improvement in any of the four pools, and stricter admission can discard useful alternatives. It proposes EvoAudit, which revises select/analyze/mutate/gate.
closestPapers.relation: Already shows that score-based parent selection fails to pick the most improvable parent (the critique notes below-random hit rates on τ³-Banking). This is a small-n (4 pools × 4 parents × 3 branches) version of this idea's CMP/parent-potential validation. It has no CMP, no winner's-curse model, no meta-level selection and no placebo.

closestPapers.title: Auditing the Product, Not the Recursion: The Evaluation Evidence Behind Recursive Self-Improvement Claims
closestPapers.summary: Full-text coding of 114 studies (90 self-described RSI) to measure how often they report the evidence that process claims require. 90% report product evaluation beyond development tasks, 60% evaluate on tasks unused for selection, and only 22% audit two or more reruns of the full loop. Per the round-1 critique, only 19% use null controls and 4 of 26 improver claims use a same-start, matched-budget comparison.
closestPapers.relation: Meta-research only, with no experiments. It states the exact evidence gap this idea would fill: improver claims lack same-start swaps and null controls. That helps the motivation but also signals the idea is 'in the air'.

closestPapers.title: Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?
closestPapers.summary: Studies how to split the evaluation budget in scaffold evolution between guiding search and choosing the final scaffold. Sparse feedback can sustain productive evolution, while extra targeted evaluation improves final selection. Replay analyses examine shared information across candidates.
closestPapers.relation: A budget-allocation method for the search-vs-selection tradeoff at the object/scaffold level. It does not measure meta-level selection bias or validate improver proxies, but it competes with any 'fix' section this idea offers.

closestPapers.title: Huxley-Gödel Machine: Human-Level Coding Agent Development by an Approximation of the Optimal Self-Improving Machine
closestPapers.summary: Identifies a Metaproductivity-Performance Mismatch: an agent's coding benchmark score is a poor indicator of its potential for further self-improvement. It proposes clade-metaproductivity (CMP), which aggregates descendants' benchmark performance, and uses it to guide tree expansion in a self-improving coding-agent setting.
closestPapers.relation: Foundation and target: CMP is the proxy whose validity this idea tests against a ground-truth swap-test improver effect. Per the critique, no paper (including HGM-Dual 2610.30042 and PCE 2610.36660) has validated CMP this way.

closestPapers.title: Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
closestPapers.summary: Introduces an open-ended system in which a coding agent iteratively modifies its own code. It keeps an archive of agents and samples parents from it, validating each self-modification empirically on coding benchmarks, inspired by Darwinian open-endedness and the Gödel machine.
closestPapers.relation: Foundation: DGM's archive with noisy staged evaluation and parent sampling is the archive machinery whose gains the placebo-archive arm would re-test. Its public logs have already been re-analyzed by 2610.14662.

feedback.point: Novelty is thin. Optimizer's-curse and shrinkage statistics are textbook, and 2610.09239 already ported them to LLM loops. 'The same thing one level up' reads as incremental unless the meta level shows a qualitatively new phenomenon, such as an improver × task interaction that does not shrink with more items, or lock-in that grows with generations.
feedback.addressed: Partly, on paper only. The sharpened claim makes the non-vanishing interaction term the headline, but it was never developed further. The idea was merged into #1 as an appendix.

feedback.point: The DGM-log reanalysis and 'archive gains = selection on noise' are pre-empted by 2610.14662 (zero-mean simulation reproduces DGM archive maxima; parent quality does not predict edit gain). K1-partial flag.
feedback.addressed: Yes, in the fix list: drop the DGM reanalysis as a contribution and contrast executed placebo archives with 2610.14662's simulation. Round 2 lists 2610.14662 as a must-read; at that point it had been seen only as an abstract in the lead proposal.

feedback.point: The claimed thresholds (>2×, ≥40%, rho<0.3) are numerology with no derivation. Curse size depends on meta-task SNR, so a fixed number cannot transfer across domains.
feedback.addressed: Recommended fix: replace them with pre-registered directional hypotheses plus a derived meta-task budget rule. This appears in the sharpened claim; not executed.

feedback.point: The ground truth is hard to define. If open-model improvers have about zero true effect, the curse is trivially 100% and the result reads as 'nothing works, so everything is noise'.
feedback.addressed: Fix proposed: a positive-control ladder of planted improvers with known effects. The lead paper #1 adopts a similar manipulation check / known-gain testbed.

feedback.point: Placebo design is contestable. A pure no-op gives no variance to select on, so the placebo must yield behaviorally varied but semantically null candidates, and critics will dispute what counts as null.
feedback.addressed: Fix proposed: three nulls (null code edits, shuffled-feedback editor, random ancestor revert). In round 2 only a shuffled-memory/placebo arm survives in #1's appendix, and the placebo evaluator is deferred.

feedback.point: External validity: small open-model archives on one cheap domain will not convince people about SWE-bench-scale DGM/HGM, and the HGM logs may lack per-task data.
feedback.addressed: Not addressed. The fix asks for at least 2 domains and at least 2 improver families.

feedback.point: Held-out split plus shrinkage was already shown at the object level, and only partly works (6–8.5 pt per-setting error). The paper must show what is different at the meta level, e.g. a split by task family.
feedback.addressed: Incorporated into the sharpened claim (meta-held-out split by task family plus two-level shrinkage). Not executed.

feedback.point: To reach accept it needs a closed-form meta-task budget rule, at least one flipped published improver claim (Hyperagents, AIDE², MetaRSI), a properly powered CMP validation with a reliability ceiling, and a reusable MetaAudit artifact. Otherwise it is 'workshop'.
feedback.addressed: Listed as fixes. Round 1 instead folded the idea into #1, and #1's v2 does not include the CMP validation or the ranking-flip audit.

feedback.point: Better used as a section of C1 / the improver-scaling lead paper than as a standalone; park otherwise.
feedback.addressed: Yes. Round-1 verdict: '→ #1 placebo appendix'.

feedback.point: Choosing the 'best' Pk by A-score would build a winner's curse into the Effect gate (HMED: branch credit disagrees in sign with matched Δ in 45–75% of revisions).
feedback.addressed: Yes, in the lead paper v2: Pk is pre-registered as the incumbent improver, not the archive best.

feedback.point: The placebo evaluator (shuffled or always-pass) is a strong control, but it is its own paper, so do not merge it into #1. Shuffled/placebo arms go to the appendix only if money is left.
feedback.addressed: Accepted. v2 lists the placebo evaluator as deferred, a possible follow-up paper. This effectively re-parks the placebo half of this idea.

feedback.point: Add a placebo/shuffled-memory 'vacuous history' arm. The finding that an always-pass verifier still trains skills (2610.11464) hints that shuffled history may work as well as real history.
feedback.addressed: Partly: shuffled/placebo memory survives in #1 as an appendix arm.

feedback.point: Selection regret across generations: replay all candidates on held-out data and split the gen-k gain into generation quality vs oracle-minus-selected regret. Prediction: a winner's curse that grows with archive size. Low–medium scoop risk.
feedback.addressed: Proposed as #1's Effect readout. Its adoption is not confirmed in the effect-cause-decay.v2 text I read.

feedback.point: Winner's Curse 2610.09239 (late commits mostly false positives; lock-in acts as an implicit threshold) is a third rival account of plateaus that must be ruled out.
feedback.addressed: Applies to a different idea (interference-plateau). It shows that the winner's-curse lens is being used as a control elsewhere, not developed here.

feedback.point: 'The gate, not the artifact, is becoming the object of study' (Winner's Curse, Masked Erosion, RSEA, Double Ratchet). Expect gate-design papers for self-improvers in Q1 2027.
feedback.addressed: Not addressed for this idea. It raises scoop pressure on any standalone meta-winners-curse paper.

openRisks: Fast extension by the 2610.09239 authors into agentic/meta-level settings; in R2's view the field is converging on 'gate > artifact' papers by Q1 2027.
2610.14662 and 2611.07624 already cover the DGM-log and parent-selection pieces. What remains open (two-level curse, executed placebo archive, CMP validation) is narrow.
K2: weak open-model improvers may have near-zero true effect, making 'everything is selection noise' trivially true and uninteresting without planted positive controls.
What counts as a valid placebo/null edit is contestable.
External validity from small open-model archives to SWE-bench-scale DGM/HGM; the HGM logs may lack per-task data.
Round 2 never developed it as a standalone: no v2 proposal, red-team or bold-check. Its placebo half was explicitly deferred out of the lead paper, so it currently has no execution path.
Key competitors (2610.14662, 2611.07624) were still only abstract-read in the round-2 lead proposal; they must be read in full before pre-registration.

judges.strongest: Two pieces are still unclaimed by any arXiv or ICLR 2027 paper. The first is validating HGM's CMP and parent-potential proxies against a metaproductivity oracle (K fresh fixed-budget expansions per node) with a split-half reliability ceiling. The second is the claim that an improver x meta-task interaction term sets a floor on meta-level selection error that adding more items per task does not lower. That second claim is the one thing that would make this more than 'the same statistics one level up'. Planted positive-control improvers make the K2 'everything is noise' outcome interpretable, and the work fits the mentor's meta-agent and self-improvement agenda well.
judges.weakest: The winner's-curse and placebo framing is now crowded, at the object level and partly at the search level. 2610.09239 does the object-level winner's curse. ICLR 2027 da1Czy7foS (Mirage Discoveries) measures the winner's curse in LLM evolutionary program search and shows that equal-budget random search transfers as well, which pre-empts the headline of 'placebo archives match much of DGM/HGM gain'. ICLR 2027 yl1XFtnTn4 (Auditing Harness Evolution) finds an evolved lineage has no advantage over one audit-selected edit at matched budget. jd8luqTdQW already gives the winner's curse as a function of N and m with a correction for correlated candidates. TRUST (wV4bK1dHpC) and REUSE/SGM own the gate-fix side. ICLR 2027 9UsBcc69Ua already shows HGM's selection signal scores do-nothing agents the same as invalid children. Add 2610.14662 (zero-mean simulation reproduces DGM maxima) and 2611.07624 (score-based parent selection fails), and what remains is narrow: CMP validation and the interaction term. Both are small-n, open-model, single-domain experiments. External validity to SWE-bench-scale DGM/HGM is unaddressed. The audit target MetaRSI did not turn up as an ICLR 2027 submission. With 30-50 oracle nodes, each needing K expansions, plus 5-seed executed archives, the experiment is underpowered on an undergrad budget.
judges.mustFix:
1. Drop 'placebo archives match DGM/HGM gains' and 'archive gains are selection noise' as headlines. Position against da1Czy7foS, yl1XFtnTn4, 2610.14662, jd8luqTdQW, TRUST/wV4bK1dHpC, VuzgEFCuwx and 9UsBcc69Ua, and use the executed placebo arm only as a control.
2. Make the paper rest on two-sided, pre-registered claims: (a) the improver x meta-task interaction variance does not shrink with items per task, so the meta-task budget rule is closed-form and differs qualitatively from the object-level 1/sqrt(m); (b) CMP vs oracle rank correlation with a reliability ceiling, at n ≥ 40 nodes, in at least 2 domains and with at least 2 improver families.
3. Include planted positive-control improvers so a null is interpretable.
4. Flip at least one existing published improver claim. Use the ICLR 2027 Hyperagents/RSI-Harness/MetaEvoForge transfer claims rather than MetaRSI, which could not be located.
5. Otherwise, keep this as the selection-regret readout and appendix inside the lead paper (Effect, Cause, Decay), not as a standalone paper.
judges.reviewerQuote: The winner's curse in LLM-guided search and self-improvement gates is already well documented (2610.09239, Mirage Discoveries, TRUST, Auditing Harness Evolution), and moving it 'one level up' to improver selection on a small open-model testbed reads as an incremental re-application unless the improver x meta-task interaction floor is shown to be a real, domain-general phenomenon.

judges.strongest: The one piece no 2026 arXiv paper or ICLR 2027 submission has done yet is checking HGM's clade-metaproductivity (CMP) and parent-potential proxies against a ground-truth "metaproductivity oracle": K fresh fixed-budget expansions per node, reported with a split-half reliability ceiling. The claim that an improver x meta-task interaction term does not shrink with more items is the only qualitatively new phenomenon at the meta level. Both pieces are cheap, run on open models, and sit squarely on the mentor's agenda.
judges.weakest:
After the ICLR 2027 sweep, almost every headline arm is already taken.
- Executed placebo archives at equal budget: Mirage Discoveries (OpenReview da1Czy7foS) finds fitness acceptance picks the held-out best in only 5/12 runs and equal-budget random search transfers as well. Auditing Harness Evolution (yl1XFtnTn4) finds no detectable advantage for an evolved lineage over a single audit-selected edit at matched budget.
- Held-out same-start improver swaps: Improvement by Inheritance (ZMmJDeDTXk) already runs nested replay crossing improvers with common start states.
- Winner's-curse statistics: jd8luqTdQW (bias grows with N and shrinks with 1/sqrt(m), with an effective-candidate-count correction), 2610.09239, and TRUST (wV4bK1dHpC).
- Zero-mean archives and parent selection: 2610.14662 and 2611.07624.
What remains (CMP validation plus the interaction term) is a section, not a paper. "Optimizer's curse one level up" is K4: textbook statistics combined with an existing archive method.
judges.mustFix:
Drop the placebo-archive and improver-swap headlines. Cite Mirage Discoveries (da1Czy7foS), Auditing Harness Evolution (yl1XFtnTn4), Improvement by Inheritance (ZMmJDeDTXk), jd8luqTdQW and TRUST (wV4bK1dHpC) as prior work and baselines. Rebuild the contribution around two things:
- A powered CMP / parent-potential oracle validation: 30-50 nodes, split-half reliability ceiling, at least 2 domains, plus HGM-Dual as a comparison.
- A direct test that the improver x meta-task variance component stays flat as items per task grow, with planted positive-control improvers so the null result is not trivial.
Then either fold both into the lead paper (Effect, Cause, Decay) as its Effect-arm readout, or hold them as a short "CMP does not measure metaproductivity" paper. Commit to flipping a named published improving-at-improving claim before writing.
judges.reviewerQuote: Every component here, from equal-budget random/placebo search and matched-budget lineage audits to nested improver replay and winner's-curse corrections for LLM selection, appears in concurrent ICLR 2027 submissions, so the remaining novelty reduces to checking one proxy (CMP) from one prior method.

judges.strongest: The one piece no 2026 paper or ICLR 2027 submission has done is validating HGM's clade-metaproductivity (CMP) and parent-potential proxies against an executed metaproductivity oracle (K fresh fixed-budget expansions per node, with a split-half reliability ceiling). It is cheap, falsifiable either way (CMP works, or it is near chance), and sits squarely in Yin's self-referential/meta-agent agenda.
judges.weakest: The ICLR 2027 sweep (Nov 12) closes most of the remaining space. (1) Mirage Discoveries (openreview da1Czy7foS) measures the winner's curse in LLM-guided evolutionary search and finds that equal-budget random search transfers as well as fitness acceptance, which is effectively the placebo-archive headline. (2) Improvement by Inheritance (ZMmJDeDTXk) already does nested replay that crosses improvers on common start states, on released Hyperagents history, and shows the improver does not improve successors. That is the same-start improver swap plus the "flip a published improving-at-improving claim" audit. (3) Auditing Harness Evolution (yl1XFtnTn4) finds that a lineage has no advantage over one audit-selected edit at matched budget. (4) Gate winner's-curse and fix work is crowded: jd8luqTdQW (curse ∝ N/√m with an effective candidate count), TRUST wV4bK1dHpC, REUSE cnaYLnpsAV, VuzgEFCuwx. (5) 9UsBcc69Ua already reports HGM's selection signal scoring do-nothing agents at 0.0. Add 2610.09239, 2610.14662 and 2611.07624 on arXiv, and what is left reads as "2610.09239 statistics applied to HGM plus a CMP check". That is K4-shaped and K1-partial. The improver × meta-task interaction headline is the only possibly new phenomenon, and it is unpiloted. With weak open-model improvers the true effect may be about zero (K2).
judges.mustFix: Do not pursue this as a standalone NeurIPS paper. Fold the CMP/parent-potential oracle validation (30–50 nodes, K expansions, split-half ceiling, planted positive-control improvers) into the lead Effect-Cause-Decay paper as a readout, alongside verify/leads-b's selection-regret decomposition. The paper must cite and position against these and must not claim any of their findings as new: Mirage Discoveries (da1Czy7foS: equal-budget random search equals fitness search), Improvement by Inheritance (ZMmJDeDTXk: nested improver replay), Auditing Harness Evolution (yl1XFtnTn4: lineage vs single edit at matched budget), jd8luqTdQW, TRUST (wV4bK1dHpC), 9UsBcc69Ua (HGM zero-score failure), 2610.09239, 2610.14662 and 2611.07624. That rules out the placebo archive, the improver swap and the gate winner's curse as contributions. A standalone version would be justified only if a pilot shows an improver × meta-task interaction variance component that stays flat as items per task grow, with planted controls proving the pipeline can detect real improver effects. Otherwise drop the idea.
judges.reviewerQuote: Mirage Discoveries, Improvement by Inheritance and 2610.09239 have already shown the winner's curse, matched-budget random-search parity and same-start improver replay, so beyond a CMP sanity check it is unclear what this submission adds.

dossier.title: More Tasks, No Gain: The Data Multiplier and Saturation Law of Harness Learners (parked in round 1, not carried into round 2)
dossier.claim: Latest version (round-1 critique's sharpened claim, never formally adopted): for frozen-weight harness learners, held-out gain depends on how many distinct latent rules the optimizer sees per update, not on how many tasks exist. The saturation point scales as n* ∝ R/k (latent rules divided by failures shown per step) across evolvers. Past n*, extra tasks only add seen-instance gains. Self-generated tasks are worth real ones exactly to the extent that they expose rules the harness has not yet covered. The original C10 claim was looser: n* is a few dozen tasks, set by evidence bandwidth k; n_eff/m ≥ 1 holds only below n*; curricula help by selecting tasks; and most gains are S_seen.
dossier.design: Original C10 design: build a procedural τ-style world with a known latent rule graph (LatentRule-τ). Vary real tasks n from 5 to 200 against static, adaptive and anchored generated tasks. Use 3 evolvers (GEPA, ACE/DAEDALUS-style memory, Meta-Harness-lite) on 2 open models, vary evidence bandwidth k, and run at least 5 seeds at matched rollouts and tokens. Report S_real, S_gen, n_eff, per-rule coverage, and a seen/held split by re-serving fresh instances (Continual-ARC style). The critique's fixes, which the idea would need, are these. Vary k (1/4/16/64) independently at fixed n and fixed total rollouts. Vary rule-graph size R (8/32/128) and test whether n* moves linearly with R/k. Predict n* out of sample on τ²-retail or AppWorld. Run SSR, GEPA-Curator and ActiveSaddler as arms and test whether coverage per step explains their gains. Compare coverage-aware and coverage-blind generators. Control for repeats per task and context length. Prune to 2 evolvers × 1 model with a fractional factorial design. Cost: $600–1.5k, with a pilot of about $20.
dossier.history: The idea started in round 1 as sweep Idea 1 in round1/sweep/curriculum.md. That sweep recommended merging it with Dan's #3 (self-generated curriculum) and with Goodhart Idea 3, using LatentRule-τ as the instrument. It then became candidate C10 (Dan-modified: #3 data multiplier + #5 anchoring + infra D). The round-1 critique scored it about 61, at the bottom of "viable with fixes". The main reason was that SSR (2610.28815) had already published the "more tasks hurt, selection beats adding" headline. The critique proposed reframing the paper around a causal law, n* ∝ R/k. In the round-1 final ranking it placed #17 of 19, verdict "park; could be a section inside #5" (curriculum-goodhart). No standalone proposal was written. It did not appear in round 2. Its host idea, curriculum-goodhart, became "Blind-Spot Hiding" (v2, 78.3, the round-2 backup), but the v2 does not keep the saturation, n_eff or bandwidth content. Round 2 mentions this idea's key papers only in passing: field_forecast lists SSR as read from the abstract only, and the ICLR'27 check lists 2609.39148 as already known.
dossier.priorScores: R1 critique 60.8 (≈61), N2.0/S3.0/R3.0/C3.5/F4.0/T4.0; R1 final rank #17, park; no R2 score (not carried forward)

closestPapers.title: Forging More Tasks into Better Harnesses: Agentic Harness Evolution via Successive Scale Racing (SSR)
closestPapers.summary: Finds that existing harness-evolution methods get worse as the task pool grows, and traces this to poor evidence selection: different combinations of evidence lead to very different outcomes. Proposes Successive Scale Racing, which builds evidence subsets ranked by task quality and coverage and races the resulting candidate harnesses on a small budget. Reports state-of-the-art results on three benchmarks. The critique's deep read adds that the pool was varied from 40 to 200 tasks, AHE peaked at 80, and a top-40 subset beat all 160 tasks by 3.4 pts.
closestPapers.relation: This is the scoop on the headline. It already shows "more tasks, no gain" and "selection beats adding" on real benchmarks, with a noisy/redundant-evidence explanation. What it leaves open: no generated tasks or n_eff, bandwidth is not varied independently of n, no known latent structure, no seen/held split, and no quantitative law. The idea's only defensible contribution is a causal law n*(k,R) that would explain SSR.

closestPapers.title: Scale and Selection: What Makes Automatic Harness Evolution Work for Visual-Interface Robot Agents
closestPapers.summary: A coding-agent optimizer evolves the harness of a robot agent that acts through a browser-based 3D interface. Holding the number of rounds fixed, held-out success rises as rollouts per round grow from 5 to 100, and small batches overfit the training tasks. It also finds that accepting every revision degrades performance, so a selection gate is needed.
closestPapers.relation: Already shows the positive side of the bandwidth mechanism (more evidence per round leads to better generalization), so the proposal cannot present bandwidth as a surprise. In this paper, batch size B mixes training-set size with per-round bandwidth, it is robotics only, and it runs one campaign per B. The idea would separate k from n.

closestPapers.title: DAEDALUS: Bootstrapping Agent Memory from Self-Generated Tasks
closestPapers.summary: Pairs an explorer, which generates challenging but solvable tasks, with a solver. It derives heuristics from the solver's failures and accepts one only after the solver repeatedly succeeds with it. This builds reusable agent memory without curated tasks or oracle verifiers. The critique's read reports it comes within 0.6/2.5/4.0 of the curated-task variant (AppWorld, τ²-retail, AutomationBench), and performance falls after about 90 sessions.
closestPapers.relation: Already shows that self-generated tasks are close to as good as real ones, and shows saturation over sessions. It provides no n_eff(n) curve, no sweep over real n, no seen/held decomposition, and covers one memory method. This weakens the idea's generated-task arm unless the generator is made coverage-aware.

closestPapers.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
closestPapers.summary: Argues that agent failures caused by harness limits, stochastic execution or noisy judges can be uninformative or even harmful to reflective prompt optimizers such as GEPA. Adds a curation step that chooses which experiences shape the optimization. The critique's read reports up to +20.7% over GEPA on WebArena, ALFWorld, AppWorld and τ-bench.
closestPapers.relation: A second independent result that curation beats volume. There is no sweep over n, no generated tasks and no law. The critique suggests treating it as an arm whose gain the coverage-per-step law should explain.

closestPapers.title: ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization
closestPapers.summary: Points out that harness optimizers fix which training scenarios generate feedback, even though the most useful scenarios change as the harness evolves. It treats curriculum choice as a non-stationary bandit over failure-pattern arms, guided by learning progress. The critique reports +4.4/+7.5 pp over a fixed order at the same rollout budget on GAIA2 and TB2.
closestPapers.relation: Takes the sub-claim that "adaptive curricula help by selecting", which is why Dan's #4 task-selection idea was kept only as a baseline. It does not explain why selection works, and does not study generation or scaling in n. Its failure-pattern clusters could serve as the estimate of R on real benchmarks.

closestPapers.title: Trading Human Curation for Synthetic Augmentation in RLVR
closestPapers.summary: Defines a cost-adjusted trade rate ρ between gate-filtered augmented tasks and human-authored tasks in RLVR for agentic LMs. Measures it through a controlled comparison. The critique's read reports 80 augmented tasks matching about 87 human ones, with diminishing returns (ρ falls from 0.65 to 0.22).
closestPapers.relation: The "data multiplier / n_eff" metric already exists here under another name, for weight training rather than harness learning. Cite it and report ρ for comparison, but do not claim the metric as new.

closestPapers.title: Do Self-Evolving Skills Generalize to Held-Out Tasks?
closestPapers.summary: Tests five self-evolving skill methods plus a one-shot skill on six benchmarks with the same model and splits. Of the 21 skills that improve on training tasks, only 5 keep the full gain on test tasks, 13 keep part of it and 3 keep none. Skills that carry over badly hard-code task-specific details or turn a single fix into a global rule.
closestPapers.relation: Partly makes the "most gains are S_seen" claim already. It has no n sweep or generated tasks. The idea's rule-level seen/held attribution would give that retention gap a mechanism.

closestPapers.title: Harness Evolution as Learning: Approximation, Generalization, and Optimization Limits of Self-Improving Personal Agents
closestPapers.summary: Treats harness evolution for fixed-model personal agents as learning and splits its limits into approximation, generalization and optimization error. It combines a preference-oriented benchmark with theory. The critique's read reports a coverage–estimation U-shape in memory size L, with a bound of L·exp(-2γ²⌊n/L⌋).
closestPapers.relation: Foundation and theory scaffold for an n*(k,R) law. It varies memory size L rather than task count or bandwidth. A reviewer could use it to argue that saturation is already explained.

feedback.point: The headline is not new. SSR 2610.28815 already shows "more tasks degrade evolvers" and "selection beats adding", and fixes it. As written, the paper reads like a toy-world replication of SSR. Novelty is capped at N=2.
feedback.addressed: Not addressed. The idea was parked after round 1 and never revised. The critique's proposed fix (a causal law n* ∝ R/k) exists only as a suggestion.

feedback.point: The mechanism is half-published. Scale and Selection (more rollouts per round leads to better held-out results), SSR (noisy, redundant evidence) and Harness Evolution as Learning (coverage–estimation bound) together already suggest it. It is novel only if k is varied independently of n and of total rollouts, and n* shifts with k in a dose–response pattern.
feedback.addressed: Not addressed (parked).

feedback.point: External validity: the toy world may saturate simply because it has few rules. Needs a sweep over rule-graph size R and at least one real benchmark (τ²-retail or AppWorld) where n* is predicted out of sample.
feedback.addressed: Not addressed (parked).

feedback.point: Confounds under matched rollouts: larger n means fewer repeats per task (denoising confounded with coverage), and larger k means longer reflection contexts (long-context degradation). Needs explicit repeats-per-task and context-length-matched arms.
feedback.addressed: Not addressed (parked).

feedback.point: The self-generated-task arm is an expected null. DAEDALUS nearly matches curated tasks, and 2606.03800 reports many "too easy" rejections. Replace the static/adaptive/anchored sweep with a coverage-aware vs coverage-blind generator, and report the 2606.03800 trade rate ρ. Do not claim n_eff as a new metric.
feedback.addressed: Not addressed (parked). The C10 notes did acknowledge that the "too easy" null is expected.

feedback.point: Overspecified claim: four claims in one sentence. Pick one headline law and make the rest corollaries.
feedback.addressed: Partly. The critique itself drafted a single sharpened headline (the R/k coverage law), but no revised proposal adopted it.

feedback.point: The grid is too large (more than 2,000 runs). Needs a power analysis from the $20 pilot and a fractional design: 2 evolvers × 1 model, with a second model at only 3 n values.
feedback.addressed: Not addressed (parked).

feedback.point: Unify recent methods: run SSR, GEPA-Curator and ActiveSaddler as arms and show their gains are explained by new-rule coverage per step. Add a Gödel-Agent-style meta-agent arm that can edit its own k or curriculum, to raise mentor relevance (R=3).
feedback.addressed: Not addressed (parked).
