feedback.point: K1 not fired but close. K2 partial risk: if n* does not move with k, only an SSR replication remains. K4 partial risk: as written it is SSR's n sweep + DAEDALUS's generated tasks + Continual-ARC's split, merely combined.
feedback.addressed: Not addressed (parked).

feedback.point: Meta FAIR 2610.38882, listed as closest prior in C10, is actually "Aligning Autoresearch: Co-Improvement" and is not a data-scaling paper.
feedback.addressed: Not corrected in candidates.md.

feedback.point: The cause of saturation is unclear: evidence noise, context saturation, rule interference, or noise in acceptance (winner's curse). Evidence bandwidth is only one candidate.
feedback.addressed: Partly. The critique's confound arms (context-length matching) would separate some of these. Rule interference and winner's curse are not separated in any version.

feedback.point: Ranked #17 of 19, score 61, verdict "park; could be a section inside #5 (curriculum-goodhart)".
feedback.addressed: Not folded in. Curriculum-goodhart v2 (Blind-Spot Hiding, 78.3, round-2 backup) became a yoked-control mechanism claim with no saturation or n_eff section.

feedback.point: No round-2 red-team, bold-check or fact-check was run on this idea. Round 2 only notes that SSR's claims rest on its abstract (field_forecast) and that 2609.39148 was already covered in this critique (verify/openreview-iclr27).
feedback.addressed: N/A

openRisks: The headline is scooped by SSR 2610.28815, so the paper only survives if n* actually moves with k and R in a dose–response pattern (K2 risk).
Toy-world artifact: saturation might just reflect a small rule graph. No real-benchmark out-of-sample check has been designed in detail.
Confounds (repeats per task, reflection context length, acceptance noise or winner's curse, rule interference) could explain the plateau instead of bandwidth.
Generated-task results risk an expected null given DAEDALUS and 2606.03800. Even the n_eff metric already has a precedent (trade rate ρ).
The full grid is computationally large (more than 2,000 runs) and needs pruning plus a power analysis.
Low mentor relevance (R=3) unless a self-referential meta-agent arm is added.
Fast-moving area: at least 4 close papers appeared in Jul–Nov 2026, and a quantitative law could appear before NeurIPS 2027.
The idea has no revised proposal and no round-2 vetting, so all the fixes are untested suggestions.

judges.strongest: The sharpened R/k coverage law makes a quantitative, falsifiable prediction: n* should scale linearly with rule-graph size R divided by evidence bandwidth k. Testing it needs a known latent rule graph (LatentRule-tau) and a sweep of k independent of n at fixed rollouts. Neither SSR, Scale and Selection, GEPA-Curator nor ActiveSaddler has that instrument. If the dose-response holds and predicts n* out of sample on tau2-retail or AppWorld, one law would explain why selection-based methods beat adding more tasks.
judges.weakest: The headline is already taken, and so is most of the mechanism. SSR (2610.28815) shows "more tasks hurt, selection beats adding". Scale and Selection (2609.39304) shows that more evidence per round generalizes better. Harness Evolution as Learning (2609.36892) gives a coverage-estimation bound. 2606.03800 already defines n_eff under the name trade rate rho. DAEDALUS gives the generated-task result. The ICLR 2027 sweep piles on further. Opinionated Optimizers (LhhLpXBFgo; 216 meta-optimization runs) already attributes harness overfitting and plateaus to weak, noisy evidence and narrow proposer priors. Two submissions offer competing plateau explanations that a reviewer will raise as confounds: Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling (FPaMYO47j4), where the limit is content failures, and Theory of Reliable Self-Evolution (NxGP6PGiaU), where the ceiling is evaluation cost. ActiveSaddler (xmpyzuagpu) and Do Self-Evolving Skills Generalize (rM2eQio3e3) are now ICLR submissions too. What remains is an untested R/k law in a toy world, and if n* does not move with k it collapses into an SSR replication. The idea has never been revised or vetted since round 1.
judges.mustFix: 1. Adopt the single headline n* proportional to R/k and drop the generated-task, n_eff and curriculum claims; at most keep a coverage-aware vs coverage-blind generator ablation and report rho from 2606.03800. 2. Vary k (1/4/16/64) at fixed n, fixed total rollouts, fixed repeats per task and length-matched reflection context. 3. Sweep R (8/32/128) and pre-register the slope, with the falsification criterion and the null outcome stated up front. 4. Add arms that separate the competing plateau causes: content vs process failures (FPaMYO47j4), evaluation cost and gate noise or winner's curse (NxGP6PGiaU, LhhLpXBFgo), and rule interference. 5. Predict n* out of sample on tau2-retail or AppWorld, estimating R from ActiveSaddler-style failure clusters. 6. Show that the gains of SSR, GEPA-Curator and ActiveSaddler are explained by new-rule coverage per step. 7. Run a power analysis from the $20 pilot and prune to a fractional factorial of 2 evolvers x 1 model. 8. Strongest option: fold this in as one section of Blind-Spot Hiding or the SHARP-1 plateau paper rather than a standalone submission.
judges.reviewerQuote: The qualitative finding that harness learners saturate in task count and benefit from evidence selection is already established by SSR, Scale and Selection and Opinionated Optimizers, and the proposed R/k law is validated mainly in a synthetic world whose rule count the authors chose, so I am not convinced it explains real-benchmark plateaus better than the evaluation-noise and capability-ceiling accounts that already exist.

judges.strongest: The only part that is still defensible is the causal law n* proportional to R/k. It would be tested in a world with known latent rules, with bandwidth k varied independently of task count n and of total rollouts. If the law holds, it would explain at once why SSR, GEPA-Curator and ActiveSaddler work (new-rule coverage per step). No 2026 arXiv paper or ICLR 2027 submission I checked states that law, and either outcome would be clean on a synthetic rule graph.
judges.weakest: The headline and most of the mechanism are already published. SSR (2610.28815) shows "more tasks hurt, selection beats adding". Scale and Selection (2609.39304) shows more evidence per round helps generalization. GEPA-Curator and ActiveSaddler (ActiveSaddler is also ICLR'27 xmpyzuagpu) show curation and curriculum beat volume. DAEDALUS and 2606.03800 pre-empt the generated-task arm and the n_eff/trade-rate metric. 2609.39148 pre-empts "most gains are seen-only". The ICLR 2027 sweep has no direct n* law, but it adds competing plateau explanations a reviewer will cite: "A Theory of Reliable Self-Evolution" (NxGP6PGiaU, ceiling set by evaluation cost), "Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling" (FPaMYO47j4, a capability/content ceiling) and "When Is Enough Enough" (0FaPTsSr9C). My alphaXiv check also found the evidence-per-update axis getting crowded: "What Should the Reflector See?" (2609.32452), "Lineage Is Memory" (2610.41157, a sample of failing cases shown to the proposer), AdaGEPA (2609.39927, feedback allocation) and batched GEPA (2610.36774). Without the R/k dose-response, the paper reduces to SSR's n sweep plus DAEDALUS-style generation plus a seen/held split, which fires K4. The idea was also parked, and no revised proposal or round-2 vetting exists.
judges.mustFix: Drop the four-part claim and pre-register a single law: n* scales with R/k. Vary k (1/4/16/64) at fixed n and fixed rollouts, and vary R (8/32/128). Add arms that match context length and repeats per task, plus an acceptance-noise (winner's curse) control. Explicitly rule out the competing ceiling accounts: evaluation cost (ICLR'27 NxGP6PGiaU), content/capability (FPaMYO47j4) and evidence composition (2609.32452, 2610.41157). Predict n* out of sample on tau2-retail or AppWorld, using ActiveSaddler failure clusters as the estimate of R. Show that coverage per step explains the gains of the SSR, GEPA-Curator and ActiveSaddler arms. Use a fractional design (2 evolvers x 1 open model) powered from the $20 pilot. The realistic path is to fold this in as a section of Blind-Spot Hiding (coverage-aware vs coverage-blind writer) rather than run it as a standalone paper.
judges.reviewerQuote: The phenomenon that more tasks fail to improve harness evolution and that evidence selection matters was already established by SSR, Scale and Selection, GEPA-Curator and ActiveSaddler. The proposed n* proportional to R/k law is shown only in a synthetic rule world built to have exactly that structure, so I am not convinced it says anything about real benchmarks, where the number of latent rules is unknown.

judges.strongest: The only part worth keeping is the causal law n* ∝ R/k. It can be falsified, and it is the one thing that could explain why SSR, GEPA-Curator and ActiveSaddler work. LatentRule-τ gives exact ground truth on rule coverage, so k can be varied independently of n and of total rollouts. No paper on arXiv or in the ICLR'27 sweep has run that dose–response test.
judges.weakest: Novelty is gone from several directions. SSR (2610.28815) already has the headline ("more tasks hurt, selection beats adding"). Scale and Selection (2609.39304) already has the bandwidth mechanism. DAEDALUS and 2606.03800 already cover self-generated tasks and n_eff/ρ. 2609.39148 already covers the seen/held retention gap. The Nov-12 ICLR'27 sweep adds competing explanations of the plateau that a reviewer will raise: NxGP6PGiaU (A Theory of Reliable Self-Evolution, where evaluation cost sets the ceiling), FPaMYO47j4 (Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling, where content failures set it), 0FaPTsSr9C (When Is Enough Enough, saturation as a stopping problem) and PX4Zpvsaca/QDdWiaNkk2 (gains break down into overfitting and compute, and generalize poorly). ecw2VvTeE5 (What Actually Evolves) makes the generated-task arm an expected null. If n* does not shift with k and R, what remains is a toy-world replication of SSR (K2). As written, the design combines SSR's n-sweep, DAEDALUS's generated tasks and a Continual-ARC split (K4). Mentor fit is weak without a meta-agent arm, and there is no revised proposal or round-2 vetting.
judges.mustFix: The paper only survives as one headline law, n*(k,R), tested by dose–response. Vary k over 1/4/16/64 at fixed n and fixed total rollouts. Vary R over 8/32/128. Add arms that match repeats per task and reflection context length. Separate the explanations with explicit arms: coverage, evaluation-cost or acceptance-noise ceiling (NxGP6PGiaU), content/capability ceiling (FPaMYO47j4) and rule interference. Predict n* out of sample on τ²-retail or AppWorld, using ActiveSaddler-style failure clusters to estimate R. Run SSR, GEPA-Curator and ActiveSaddler as arms and show that coverage per step explains their gains. Drop the n_eff novelty claim, cite ρ from 2606.03800, and replace the generated-task sweep with a coverage-aware vs coverage-blind generator. Run a $20 power-analysis pilot, then use a fractional design (2 evolvers × 1 model). Add a meta-agent arm that sets its own k, for mentor fit. Cite SSR, Scale and Selection, NxGP6PGiaU, FPaMYO47j4, 0FaPTsSr9C, PX4Zpvsaca and ecw2VvTeE5. The realistic path is to fold this into Blind-Spot Hiding as a coverage section, not to write a standalone paper.
judges.reviewerQuote: This reads as a toy-world replication of SSR's "more tasks, no gain" finding. The proposed R/k law is never cleanly separated from the evaluation-cost and capability-ceiling explanations already in concurrent ICLR 2027 submissions, so I do not see what we learn that SSR, Scale-and-Selection and DAEDALUS did not already show.

dossier.title: Context Debt: Do Harness-Evolving Meta-Agents Plateau From Anchoring on Their Own History, or From Saturation? (now folded into Meta-Overfitting as the "reset procedure vs forget memory" design-rule contrast)
dossier.claim: Latest standalone version (round-1 critique's sharpened claim): in harness and self-referential evolution, the plateau comes from different state components depending on the metric. Conversation and unverified notes cause search-score stalls (anchoring, false floors). The scored archive and the improver's self-modified code cause held-out stalls (overfitting, code debt). So at matched compute, "flush the conversation, keep the verified archive" recovers most late search gain, and held-out gain comes back only when the archive is re-validated on fresh tasks. In the surviving round-2 form, inside the lead paper, the claim is narrower: on a far domain, resetting the improver's procedure while keeping its memory (P0+Mk) beats the Forgetting-style reset that wipes memory and keeps the procedure (Pk+∅).
dossier.design: Round-1 design: GEPA-style, Meta-Harness-style and Gödel-style evolvers, run 3–4x past their default horizon to establish a late plateau with headroom (pilot gate). Each arm forks from the same plateaued checkpoint, as in SLA's checkpoint-continuation. The arms are a keep/drop factorial over conversation × scored archive × unverified notes × (for Gödel) self-modified improver code, plus fork-and-flush, forget-to-best and a matched-diversity control (higher temperature, "structurally different edit" prompts, random parents). Every arm is scored on both search-split and held-out tasks, with an independent saturation witness: a stronger improver or best-of-many at 4x budget, plus the 2610.24291 headroom∧narrowing∧plateau decision tree. The anytime-valid detector (2610.04756) is reported as a measurement of how often it fires, not as the method. The study uses 2 benchmarks, 2 open models (Qwen3.5 / DeepSeek V4 Flash) and 5–8 seeds per cell. Pilot costs $30–50; the full study $600–1.2k. Round-2 residual: inside Meta-Overfitting v2, one Gödel-lite family with 10 lineages to checkpoint k*, comparing the two transplant cells P0+Mk vs Pk+∅ on a far domain (RQ4) at no extra cost.
dossier.history: Round 1: candidate C5 `context-debt` (T2, meta-agent plasticity). It was independently proposed in 6 of 8 sweeps as "G1 / Idea 1" in frontier-trends. The critique gave it 65/100, "viable with fixes": it is crowded by four Oct–Nov 2026 forgetting/reset papers, all on discovery tasks. The critique offered a sharpened held-out-dissociation claim plus a Gödel "code debt" arm, projected at ~76 if fixed. It never got a full proposal. The REPORT ranked it #13 and folded it into the merged lead paper (#1, Effect/Cause/Decay) as its "reset arms" (meta-plasticity RQ3 had about 6 reset arms, including Forgetting-style Pk+∅ and Fork-and-Flush-style flush). Round 2: the sharpness red team called the reset zoo part of the "three half-papers" bloat and cut it to "6 reset arms → 0 new arms". Only the two transplant cells survive (Pk+∅ = Forgetting reset, P0+Mk = procedure reset), as the secondary "design rule" RQ4 of Meta-Overfitting (v2 score 77.9). The standalone context-debt factorial on improvers survives only as an open angle in verify/factcheck.md ("Forgetting vs archive, factorially ... neither applies it to an improver or meta-agent") and as low-priority "Idea D" in leads-b.
dossier.priorScores: R1 critique 65 (projected ~76 with fixes 1,2,4,5); no standalone proposal or R2 score. It was absorbed into the R1 merged lead (panel 75.8) and then into R2 Meta-Overfitting v2 (77.9), where it is only the secondary design-rule contrast.

closestPapers.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
closestPapers.summary: Scaled autoresearch plateaus in all three forms (one agent running longer, parallel agents, communicating agents) because each agent anchors on its past attempts and makes fewer, smaller edits. Periodically discarding every session and the candidate history, then restarting from the best candidate, pushes the same budget further. Tested on 4 tasks (heuristic programming, kernel optimization, model training) with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and 3 runs.
closestPapers.relation: The direct predecessor and the anchoring hypothesis this idea tests. It drops conversation and archive together, uses a fixed schedule, only discovery tasks (score = objective) and no held-out split, and lists 'when to forget and what to remember' as future work. Context-debt adds a component factorial plus harness/meta-agent evolution with held-out evaluation. Round 2 positions the P0+Mk design rule against this paper's Pk+∅ reset.

closestPapers.title: Scaling Discovery Does Not Require Forgetting: Verified Shared Archives Break the Multi-Agent Plateau on Anthropic's Performance Take-Home
closestPapers.summary: Argues that Forgetting deletes two things it never separates: the scored attempts and each agent's conversation with unchecked conclusions. It proposes a shared verified archive that keeps every scored attempt, with conversations capped at 3 continue prompts. Four Claude Opus 5.5 agents reach a median of 914 cycles, against 948 for a CORAL port and 946 for isolated agents, over 8 matched hours. It names the 'false floor': agents conclude about 951 is near-optimal and stop.
closestPapers.relation: Makes the same qualitative claim as context-debt ('keep scored attempts, drop the conversation and unverified conclusions') but as a comparison of system designs, not a factorial. It covers one task, Claude only, 3 runs, no held-out evaluation and no harness or improver evolution. The critique judged K1 partially at risk but not triggered. It exists only on alphaXiv, with no arXiv ID and no S2 entry.

closestPapers.title: Fork-and-Flush: Escaping Idea Basins in Autoresearch Agents
closestPapers.summary: Independent runs of the same autoresearch agent plateau at different scores and stay in localized 'idea basins'. Fork-and-flush periodically forks K trajectories that inherit the workspace but start with a fresh chat, then continues from the best one. Over 13 multi-day tasks it beats single-run by 66% and best-of-N by 44% (relative).
closestPapers.relation: Ablates flush vs fork (2x2) but never separates workspace from notes from conversation, and uses discovery tasks with no held-out set. Its finding that plateau-detection triggers rarely fired (15/25 runs) is a direct warning for context-debt's anytime-valid trigger arm, which the critique recast as a measurement. A flush arm in the R1 design.

closestPapers.title: Stateless Language Agents: Scaling Long-Horizon Automated Research
closestPapers.summary: Traces long-horizon failures to agents replaying growing histories, duplicating work, or no longer experimenting. In the proposed design no agent carries its conversation: the harness owns the research state and builds a fresh, role-specific context for each invocation, and a stateless Advisor assigns experiments to Workers. Evaluated at long horizons (up to ~1B tokens).
closestPapers.relation: Another design point in the factorial, and the source of the checkpoint-continuation method the critique recommends adopting. The authors say their ablations change what agents see, not whether an agent keeps its conversation, which is exactly context-debt's factor. Discovery and SWE tasks only, mostly single runs.

closestPapers.title: An important Bottleneck in LLM Optimizers: Principle-Level Local Optima
closestPapers.summary: Studies plateaus in feedback-driven LLM optimizers as principle-level search collapse. A decision-tree protocol (principle narrowing + prolonged plateau + gap to reference solutions) finds support for collapse in 78.3% of 161 runs across molecules, sentinel-node selection and GPU kernels. Common diversity injection (higher temperature, multiple LLMs, ...) largely fails to fix it.
closestPapers.relation: Has no reset or history arm, but supplies the headroom-vs-saturation diagnostic that context-debt needs to read 'no recovery' as saturation (critique fix 4). Its diversity-injection failures motivate the matched-diversity control (fix 3).

closestPapers.title: Lineage Is Memory: Parent Inheritance and Feedback Disclosure in Short-Budget LLM-Guided Optimization
closestPapers.summary: Across 1,750 pre-registered runs on nine prompt and program synthesis benchmarks, at matched evaluation budgets, it separates parent inheritance from feedback breadth. Greedy parent inheritance drives most progress and beats seed-reset resampling, even when the reset proposer gets clustered summaries of all failures or a larger model.
closestPapers.relation: Points the opposite way: state carried in the candidate is the main source of progress in GEPA-like loops. It sets the null for the forget-to-best arm. Its short budgets (8–12 evals) also warn that harness evolution may never reach a plateau to explain (critique weakness 2, pilot-gate fix 5).

closestPapers.title: When Is Enough Enough in Self-Evolving LLM Systems?
closestPapers.summary: Frames stopping a self-evolving LLM system as online sequential testing. It builds an anytime-valid restart detector from per-item paired evaluation outcomes, then uses change-point estimation to return an earlier artifact and avoid late overfit updates.
closestPapers.relation: Foundation for the trigger arm: the R1 design compares this detector against a fixed reset schedule. The critique downgraded that to reporting firing rates, given Fork-and-Flush's negative result on triggers. Its saturation/overfit framing overlaps the held-out-stall half of the sharpened claim.

closestPapers.title: HarnessX: A Composable, Adaptive, and Evolvable Agent Harness Foundry
closestPapers.summary: A foundry that builds harnesses from typed primitives and evolves them with AEGIS, a trace-driven multi-agent evolution engine. It also turns trajectories into model training signal. Average gain is +14.5% (up to +44%) across ALFWorld, GAIA, WebShop, tau^3-Bench and SWE-bench Verified.
closestPapers.relation: One of the 'reported harness-evolution ceilings' (post-peak collapse) that context-debt claims partly measure improver anchoring rather than the harness's limit. A target and testbed, not a competitor.

feedback.point: Novelty is thin and shrinking: Forgetting 2610.20563, Fork-and-Flush 2610.07447, SLA 2610.07625 and the verified-archives paper all appeared within 6 weeks. 'Resets help' is known, so the idea reads as a factorial ablation of known components (N=2.0, K4 borderline).
feedback.addressed: Partly. The critique's sharpened claim moves to held-out dissociation plus a Gödel code-debt arm. In round 2 the standalone idea was dropped and only the P0+Mk vs Pk+∅ contrast survives, inside Meta-Overfitting, where the novelty comes from the cross-domain Decay claim.

feedback.point: The verified-archives paper makes the same qualitative claim (keep scored attempts, drop the conversation and unverified notes) on discovery tasks. Re-check scoops in Jan and Mar 2027.
feedback.addressed: Not addressed as a standalone. The R2 factcheck verified the paper's numbers and still lists 'forgetting vs archive, factorially, on an improver' as open.

feedback.point: Harness evolution may have no late plateau to explain, since it typically runs 10–50 iterations and Lineage Is Memory shows short-budget loops gain from carried state. The plateau with headroom must be shown first.
feedback.addressed: Proposed fix 5 (pilot gate: run evolvers 3–4x longer; pivot to 'no anchoring plateau' if none appears). Never executed. Not relevant to the R2 residual, which uses transplant cells rather than plateau recovery.

feedback.point: A reset also raises exploration and acts like a stochastic restart. Without a matched-diversity control, a gain from resetting does not identify anchoring.
feedback.addressed: Proposed fix 3 (matched-diversity control). Not carried into round 2.

feedback.point: The saturation reading is under-specified: 'no recovery' could just mean the reset is weak. An independent headroom witness is needed (stronger improver, human harness, oracle best-of-many). As written, K2 is triggered.
feedback.addressed: Proposed fix 4 (oracle ceiling + 2610.24291 decision tree). Not carried into round 2.

feedback.point: Fork-and-Flush reports that plateau triggers rarely fire, so the anytime-valid trigger arm may give an uninterpretable null.
feedback.addressed: Proposed fix 7 recasts it as a measurement of firing rate. Dropped entirely in round 2.

feedback.point: About 165 runs (5 seeds × 3 evolvers × 11 arms) at $600–1.2k is only feasible with cheap models and short runs, which makes the no-plateau risk worse.
feedback.addressed: Proposed fixes 6 and 9 (checkpoint-continuation from a shared plateau, a scope of 2 benchmarks × 2 models × 3 evolvers). In R2 the cost question goes away because the contrast reuses existing transplant cells.

feedback.point: Make the held-out vs search-split dissociation the headline, and add a fourth state factor (self-modified improver code: code debt vs context debt) for Gödel-style improvers, which no prior paper has.
feedback.addressed: The code-debt idea effectively became the lead paper's 'reset procedure, keep memory' (P0+Mk vs Pk+∅) design rule. The search vs held-out dissociation was not carried forward.

feedback.point: Release a state-ablation harness wrapper (keep/drop conversation, archive, notes, improver code) plus a false-floor detector.
feedback.addressed: Not addressed.

feedback.point: Ranked #13 at 65. Folded into the merged lead paper as its 'reset arms'.
feedback.addressed: Yes, it became meta-plasticity RQ3 (about 6 reset arms) in the merged Effect/Cause/Decay paper.

feedback.point: The reset zoo (6 arms: distill, prune, selectionist, instructionist, ...) is bloat that feeds the 'three half-papers' problem. Cut to 0 new arms; Pk+∅ and P0+Mk are already transplant cells, and the rest belong in a methods paper.
feedback.addressed: Yes. v2 keeps only Pk+∅ vs P0+Mk as secondary RQ4 (design rule).

feedback.point: About a 30% chance that a cross-domain decay arm with a forgetting/reset factorial is also covered, since VERSE G.2 shows the design is cheap and natural. Suggestion: replicate and extend VERSE G.2 with forgetting/reset arms.
feedback.addressed: Partly. v2 keeps the Forgetting-style reset as a cell and cites VERSE.

feedback.point: The Forgetting 2610.20563 numbers are VERIFIED (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, 3 runs, $20–40/run; forget +9.2% vs continue +1.4%). The verified-archives paper EXISTS but only on alphaXiv, with no arXiv ID and no S2 entry; its round-1 numbers are correct. The factcheck still flags 'forgetting vs archive, factorially, on an improver/meta-agent' as an open, feasible angle.
feedback.addressed: Informational. It supports the gap but was not turned into a standalone v2.

feedback.point: Is the mentor comfortable defending the 'reset procedure, keep memory' design rule against the Forgetting 2610.20563 authors?
feedback.addressed: Open, for discussion with Xunjian.

feedback.point: Experience can be net-negative (MetaExp, CL-Bench), so the improver's job may be deciding when to forget. Lower priority, medium scoop risk, because forgetting is a crowded keyword.
feedback.addressed: Suggested only as an edit-type analysis inside #1. Not adopted.

feedback.point: Plasticity/consolidation for agents becomes a named sub-field (70%), with forgetting-vs-archive papers expected from Meta MSL, Mila/GDM and Berkeley. Improver-level plasticity is about 6 months from being reached.
feedback.addressed: Motivates folding into the meta-level Decay claim rather than pursuing an object-level reset paper.

openRisks: Fast follow by the Forgetting (Berkeley), Fork-and-Flush (MSR) or QWNTL groups: 'what to remember' is their stated future work, and the verified-archives paper already argues the conversation/archive split.
Harness-evolution runs may never plateau with headroom (short budgets; Lineage Is Memory), which leaves no effect to explain.
Without a matched-diversity control and an independent saturation witness, a reset gain cannot be attributed to anchoring.
Plateau/anytime-valid triggers may never fire (Fork-and-Flush 15/25 runs).

As a standalone it risks a K4 'factorial of known components' verdict. In its R2 form it is only a secondary contrast inside Meta-Overfitting, whose top risk is that improvers rarely self-edit (SelfImprove-Bench: 0% improver edits unless forced).
The verified-archives paper is alphaXiv-only, so how visible it is to reviewers, and whether it counts as prior art, is uncertain.
OpenReview ICLR 2027 submissions were not checked (host blocked).

judges.strongest: The search-split vs held-out dissociation is a sharp, falsifiable claim, and the component factorial (conversation × verified archive × unverified notes × self-modified improver code) has not been done. Only this design can say which piece of state causes which kind of stall, and the factcheck and the ICLR sweep both still list it as open. "Flush the chat, keep the verified archive, re-validate on fresh tasks" would be a practical design rule if it held.
judges.weakest: Novelty is gone at the mechanism level and is going at the design level. The ICLR 2027 sweep found Branch-reset (8UgphlLDok), which uses exactly this intervention (fresh chat, inherited workspace) and the anchoring explanation. With Forgetting (2610.20563), the verified-archives paper and SLA, that makes four 2026 papers holding "reset helps / keep scored attempts, drop the conversation". For the surviving residual (P0+Mk vs Pk+∅), Learning to Repair the Learner (aEPJT4hW84) already crosses code × history and finds inherited procedure explains 45% of gain. RSI-Harness (EOrtreQLbv) reports that improver procedures transfer to far domains. Opinionated Optimizers (LhhLpXBFgo), the reliable-self-evolution ceiling theory (NxGP6PGiaU) and Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling (FPaMYO47j4) each give a competing plateau explanation. What is left is a factorial of known components (K4) applied to an object where a plateau with headroom was never shown (the pilot gate never ran). The matched-diversity control and the saturation witness were also dropped in round 2. Without them a reset gain cannot be attributed to anchoring, and a null cannot be read as saturation.
judges.mustFix: Do not run this as a standalone paper. Keep only the RQ4 contrast inside Meta-Overfitting, and present it as an extension of Learning to Repair the Learner (aEPJT4hW84, code × history crossing) and Branch-reset (8UgphlLDok) / Forgetting (2610.20563), not as a new design. The contribution has to be the domain-distance axis on LLM improvers. Engage RSI-Harness (EOrtreQLbv) head-on: reproduce its positive near-domain transfer cell, then show that P0+Mk beats Pk+∅ only on far domains. If any standalone piece survives, it is the held-out vs search-split dissociation, and that needs four things: (1) a pilot showing that harness or Gödel-lite evolvers plateau with headroom at 3–4x horizon; (2) a matched-diversity control; (3) an independent saturation witness (best-of-many at 4x budget plus the 2610.24291 decision tree); (4) explicit baselines against Branch-reset-style flush and the plateau ceilings in NxGP6PGiaU and FPaMYO47j4. Use at least 5 seeds per cell and 2 open models.
judges.reviewerQuote: The intervention (fresh conversation, inherited archive) and its anchoring explanation already appear in Branch-reset and Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting, and the code × history crossing in Learning to Repair the Learner, so what is left is an ablation of known state components on a harness-evolution setting where the authors never show a plateau with headroom.

judges.strongest: The only part not yet taken is the search-score vs held-out split, where the conversation plausibly drives search-score stalls and the archive or self-modified code drives held-out stalls. No paper among Forgetting, Fork-and-Flush/Branch-reset, verified archives or SLA tests this on a harness-evolving or self-modifying improver. It also fits the mentor's meta-agent agenda well, because it asks whether the harness-evolution ceilings people report are really the improver anchoring on its own history.
judges.weakest: The mechanism and the intervention are both pre-empted several times over. ICLR 2027 submission Branch-reset (openreview 8UgphlLDok) uses exactly this intervention (fresh chat, inherited workspace) and explains it by anchoring. Forgetting (2610.20563), Fork-and-Flush (2610.07447) and the verified-archives paper already cover conversation-vs-archive. The surviving P0+Mk vs Pk+∅ contrast is close in design to the code x history crossing in ICLR 2027 submission Learning to Repair the Learner (aEPJT4hW84), where inherited procedure explains 45% of gain. Stale-history harm in harnesses is shown by FZd03GwNex, and Contextual Drag (yVo9mX6Bo8) gives the per-step mechanism. So the standalone idea is a component factorial of known parts (K4) on a mechanism that is already claimed (K1 at the mechanism level). The residual is a secondary RQ that depends on improvers actually editing themselves, which ZMmJDeDTXk and SelfImprove-Bench say they rarely do.
judges.mustFix: Do not revive this as a standalone paper. Keep it inside Meta-Overfitting as the P0+Mk vs Pk+∅ cell. In related work, cite Branch-reset (8UgphlLDok) and Learning to Repair the Learner (aEPJT4hW84, code x history crossing) as the precedents for the method and the crossing design, along with 2610.20563, 2610.07447, FZd03GwNex and yVo9mX6Bo8. Put the novelty only on the far-domain axis: procedure reset with memory kept beats Forgetting-style reset with procedure kept, and only at large domain distance. Pre-register this as two-sided. Gate the cell on at least 1 accepted improver self-edit per 4 iterations, or force edits, so that P0 and Pk actually differ. If held-out evaluation is cheap, add a single search-score vs held-out readout for the two cells, since that is the one dissociation nobody has published.
judges.reviewerQuote: The keep-archive, flush-conversation intervention and its anchoring explanation already appear in Branch-reset, Forgetting and the verified-archives work, and the procedure x memory crossing appears in Learning to Repair the Learner, so moving the same factorial onto harness-evolving improvers is an incremental replication unless the far-domain sign flip is shown convincingly.

judges.strongest: The one design no one has run is a held-out-scored state factorial on an improver or meta-agent: conversation × verified archive × unverified notes × self-modified improver code. It would show whether the search-score stall and the held-out stall come from different state components. The improver-code arm is the part that fits the mentor's agenda best, since it is Gödel-style "code debt" versus "context debt". Inside Meta-Overfitting, the P0+Mk vs Pk+∅ contrast adds no cost and gives a concrete design rule to argue against the Forgetting paper (2610.20563).
judges.weakest: The ICLR 2027 sweep makes the scoop worse. Branch-reset (OpenReview 8UgphlLDok, the venue version of Fork-and-Flush) already uses this exact intervention, fresh chat with an inherited workspace, and the same anchoring explanation. Learning to Repair the Learner (aEPJT4hW84) already runs a code × history crossing and finds that inherited procedure explains 45% of gain, which is the procedure-vs-memory decomposition behind P0+Mk vs Pk+∅. Its testbed is neuro-symbolic world models, not LLM agents. FPaMYO47j4 (ceiling = content failures) and NxGP6PGiaU (ceiling = evaluation cost) offer competing explanations of the plateau. Add Forgetting, SLA and the verified-archives paper, and the standalone reads as a factorial of known components with an anchoring story that is already published. Harness evolution may also never reach a plateau with headroom (Lineage Is Memory), and without the matched-diversity control and a saturation witness, a reset gain can't be attributed to anchoring.
judges.mustFix: Do not pursue the standalone; keep it only as RQ4 inside Meta-Overfitting. Cite Branch-reset (8UgphlLDok) and Learning to Repair the Learner (aEPJT4hW84) as design precedent, and do not claim the reset intervention or the procedure × memory crossing as a contribution. The only novel claim to keep is that P0+Mk beats Pk+∅ specifically on a far domain for a self-referential LLM improver, and that the gap grows with domain distance. Report seeds and CIs on 10 lineages. Add a matched-diversity control (resample with a fresh procedure at matched temperature) so that a P0+Mk gain is not just a stochastic restart. Run the held-out evaluation on a split separate from the search tasks. If the R2 reviewers ask for more, add a 2-cell check that the plateau is not FPaMYO47j4's capability ceiling. Re-check arXiv and OpenReview in Jan and Mar 2027 for "what to remember" follow-ups from the Berkeley, MSR or QWNTL groups.
judges.reviewerQuote: Branch-reset already shows that fresh context with an inherited workspace escapes anchoring basins, and prior work already crosses procedure with history. The submission's factorial over which state to keep is therefore a careful ablation of known components, not a new finding about why self-improvers plateau.
